chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体在 20X4年销售电气设备，该公历年度的市场份额为 4%。该主体随后终止经营，因此当其产品的废弃物管理成本分配给在 20X7年拥有市场份额的主体时，该主体已不再处于市场中。由于 20X7年的市场份额为 0%，该主体的义务为零。但是，如果另一主体在 20X7年进入电子产品市场并在该期间取得了 3% 的市场份额，则该主体对前期废弃物管理成本的义务将为分配至 20X7年的废弃物管理总成本的 3%，即使该主体在前期并未参与市场，且未生产分配至 20X7年废弃物管理成本的任何产品。

text: 该税款是否属于 IAS 37 和 IFRIC 21 的范围？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 对雇员福利征收的征费并未被明确排除在该解释公告的范围之外。然而，IAS 37 的范围排除了由其他准则规范的准备。IAS 19 规范了主体为换取员工提供的服务而给予的所有形式的对价。这包括通过直接向员工或向其他方付款来结算的福利。IAS 19 的范围非常广泛，因此，大多数工资税属于 IAS 19 的范围，从而不属于 IAS 37 和 IFRIC 21 的范围。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: FAQ 16.77.3 – 由政府征收但支付给第三方的款项是否属于 IFRIC 21 的范围？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第2、4、5段

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 由政府征收但支付给第三方的款项是否属于 IFRIC 21 的范围？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: IFRIC 21 的范围不仅适用于支付给政府的征费，也适用于“由政府征收”的征费。因此，此类支付给第三方的款项属于该解释公告的范围（例如，家庭向国家广播机构缴纳的电视税）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.78.1 – 国际财务报告准则解释委员会（IFRIC）关于按比例计算且设有年度活动门槛的征费的议程决定

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第9段 正文索引：16.78

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在发布 IFRIC 21 之后，解释委员会被问及在识别征费的导致义务发生的事项时应如何解释 IFRIC 21 第8段。解释委员会讨论了这样一种制度：支付征费的义务因期间内的活动而产生，但直至达到最低活动门槛（由法规确定）时才需支付。该门槛设定为年度门槛，但如果主体在年度中途开始或停止参与相关活动，该门槛将按主体在当年参与相关活动的天数比例相应调减。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 解释委员会指出，根据 IFRIC 21 第12段的指引，该征费的导致义务发生的事项是达到评估期末适用的门槛。解释委员会指出，在满足特定条件时按比例调减年度门槛的征费，与 IFRIC 21 第11段所述的导致义务发生的事项在一段时间内逐步发生的征费之间存在区别；在满足特定条件之前，门槛的按比例调减并不适用。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.78.2 – 导致义务发生的事项：产生收入

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第8段 正文索引：16.78

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体的年度报告日为 12月31日。一旦主体在 20X1年产生收入，即全额触发一项征费。该征费按主体在 20X0年产生收入的一定比例计算。该主体在 20X0年产生了收入，并于 20X1年1月3日开始在 20X1年产生收入。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在此情形下，导致义务发生的事项是什么？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 导致义务发生的事项（即触发支付征费的活动）是在 20X1年首次产生收入。20X0年产生收入并非触发支付征费和确认负债的活动。它是确认的必要条件，但非充分条件。20X0年产生的收入金额仅影响该负债的计量。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.78.3 – 房产税——导致义务发生的事项：某一时点

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第8段

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 法规要求主体如果在 12月31日拥有房产，则需缴纳一项征费。该房产税为最近一次房产估值的 1%，由 12月31日的房产所有者缴纳。最近一次房产估值日为同年 6月30日。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 导致义务发生的事项是在 12月31日拥有房产。房产所有者在年度内不承担支付该征费的现时义务，因为其可能在 12月31日之前出售该房产，或者法规可能发生变化。因此，该负债于 12月31日确认。房产估值日期与此无关，仅用于计量该负债。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.79.1 – 导致义务发生的事项：在特定日期经营

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第9段 正文索引：16.79

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果主体在年度报告期末仍在经营，即触发一项征费。该征费基于年度报告期末主体财务状况表中的总权益计算。该主体的年度报告期末为 20X1年12月31日。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 产生支付该征费负债的导致义务发生的事项是什么？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 导致义务发生的事项是主体在年度报告期末仍在经营。在该时点之前，即使主体在经济上被迫在未来继续经营，也不存在支付该征费的现时义务。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.79.2 – 主体在指定日期作为银行经营时触发的征费（引自 IFRIC 21 的示例）

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第9段 正文索引：16.79

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: C主体的年度报告期于 12月31日结束。仅当C主体在年度报告期末作为银行经营时，才触发一项征费。该征费的金额参照年度报告期末（例如 20X1年12月31日）C主体财务状况表中的金额确定。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该负债于 20X1年12月31日确认，因为法规确定的导致义务发生的事项是在年度报告期末作为银行经营。在年度报告期末之前，即使C主体在经济上被迫在未来继续作为银行经营，也不存在支付征费的现时义务。法规确定的触发支付征费的活动是在年度报告期末作为银行经营，该活动直至 20X1年12月31日才发生。即使负债金额基于报告期的长度确定，该结论也不会改变，因为导致义务发生的事项是在年度报告期末作为银行经营。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在中期财务报告中，该负债在包含 20X1年12月31日的中期期间全额确认，因为该负债于 20X1年12月31日全额确认。年度财务报表和中期财务报告应当适用相同的确认原则。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.81.1 – 随着主体产生收入而逐步触发的征费（引自 IFRIC 21 的示例）

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第9段 正文索引：16.81

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: A主体的年度报告期于 12月31日结束。一项征费随着A主体在 20X1年产生收入而逐步触发。该征费的金额参照A主体在 20X1年产生的收入确定。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在本示例中，该负债在 20X1年期间随着主体产生收入而逐步确认，因为法规确定的导致义务发生的事项是在 20X1年期间产生收入。在 20X1年的任何时点，A主体均承担就截至当日已产生的收入支付征费的现时义务。A主体不承担就未来产生收入而将产生的征费支付款项的现时义务。换言之，导致义务发生的事项在 20X1年期间逐步发生，因为法规确定的触发支付征费的活动在 20X1年期间逐步发生。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在中期财务报告中，A主体承担就自 20X1年1月1日至中期期末产生的收入支付征费的现时义务。因此，该负债在中期期间内逐步确认。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.81.2 – 房产税：随时间推移

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第11段 正文索引：16.81

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 法规要求主体如果拥有房产，则需缴纳一项征费。法规未明确规定导致义务发生的事项。主体可以选择按年或按月缴纳该税款。在年度内出售房产的主体将被要求缴纳截至出售日止期间的税款。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 当法规未明确规定导致义务发生的事项时，主体需要考虑一系列因素，例如付款条款以及出售房产对义务的影响。在本案例中，对这些因素的考虑支持随时间推移予以确认，即使主体拥有按年付款的选择权。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.81.3 – 是否随时间推移确认？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第11段 正文索引：16.81

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果主体在年度报告期末仍在经营，即触发一项征费。该征费基于年度报告期末主体财务状况表中的总权益计算。该主体的年度报告期末为 20X1年12月31日。该法规还包含针对在年度内停止营业的主体的特别条款。对于此类主体，该征费按比例计算（例如，六个月后按总权益的 0.5% 计算，而非年末的 1%）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 这是否会改变所有主体的确认模式，包括那些全年持续经营的主体？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 正如EX 16.78.1所述，解释委员会讨论了类似问题并指出，在满足特定条件之前，门槛的按比例调减并不适用。在我们的示例中，除非主体在年度内停止营业，否则不能早于 12月31日确认该负债。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.82.1 – 当主体产生的收入超过最低金额时触发的征费

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第12段 正文索引：16.82

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: B主体的年度报告期于 12月31日结束。如果主体在 20X1年产生的收入超过 C5,000万，即触发一项征费。该征费的金额参照所产生的全部收入（包括 20X1年产生的前 C5,000万 收入）计算。B主体的收入于 20X1年7月17日达到 C5,000万 的收入门槛。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 与前 C5,000万 收入相关的支付征费负债于 20X1年7月17日达到门槛时确认，因为支付该金额的导致义务发生的事项是达到该门槛。与超过门槛部分收入相关的支付征费负债在 20X1年7月17日至 20X1年12月31日期间随着主体产生超过门槛的收入而确认，因为导致义务发生的事项是达到门槛后开展的活动。负债金额基于截至当日产生的全部收入（包括前 C5,000万 收入）确定。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在B主体 20X1年6月30日的中期财务报告中，不确认 20X1年征费的负债，因为截至该日期尚未达到门槛。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.82.2 – 当主体销售特定产品产生收入时触发、但可通过销售其他产品避免的征费

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第8段 正文索引：16.82

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: X主体的年度报告日为 12月31日。X主体销售两种互为替代品的不同产品（A产品和B产品）。这两种产品在不同的生产工厂制造，且无法改造设施将A产品的生产转为B产品，反之亦然。使用A产品比使用B产品对环境危害更大。为鼓励X主体多销售B产品、少销售A产品，X主体需缴纳一项征费，金额相当于销售A产品产生的收入超过销售B产品产生的收入部分的 10%。每年应付的征费基于截至 12月31日止年度的收入，如果B产品的收入等于或超过A产品的收入，则无需缴纳征费。如果X主体在任何年度的 12月31日之前停止经营，则就年初至今A产品收入高于B产品收入的部分缴纳征费。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: X主体是否应当在中期财务报表中确认该征费的负债？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果在中期报告日，销售B产品产生的收入超过销售A产品产生的收入，则不确认负债，因为X主体可以通过选择不再销售任何A产品而在现实中避免该征费。如果在中期报告日，销售A产品的收入超过销售B产品的收入，X主体需要运用判断，以确定在报告日是否存在无法在现实中避免的义务。该判断应当反映，例如：X主体无法强迫客户购买更多B产品，但可以通过降价来增加需求，以及X主体的设施是否具有生产足够B产品的产能。如果X主体在现实中有可能采取行动以避免未来付款，则在主体的中期财务报表中不确认该征费的负债。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 但是，如果在现实中不可能避免该负债，则主体应当在中期财务报表中对该负债进行会计处理。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.83.1 – 根据 IAS 2 确认资产

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第3段 正文索引：16.83

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某制造主体每年进口一次用于生产的原材料。该进口需缴纳进口关税。该主体应如何对这些关税进行会计处理？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 存货采购成本的定义包括不可退还的进口关税。因此，主体可能需要在导致义务发生的事项发生时（即进口日）确认该征费的负债；但同时应当将该成本确认为所购存货的一部分。随后，该成本构成生产成本的一部分，并在存货出售时结转。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.83.2 – 根据 IAS 16 确认资产

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IFRIC 21 第3段 正文索引：16.79

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某政府对每次购买房产征收一项税费。买方应如何对该征费进行会计处理？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 不动产、厂场和设备购买价款的定义包括不可退还的购买税费。IFRIC 21 要求在导致义务发生的事项发生时（即房产转让日）确认负债。买方应当将该征费确认为房产成本的一部分，从而在房产计提折旧的期间内确认费用。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.1 – 确认标准在诉讼中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 诉讼常被用于说明如何应用 IAS 37 的某些方面。诉讼过程可能很漫长，且结果有时难以预测。与诉讼案件相关的信息可能具有敏感性。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体可能对另一方提起法律诉讼，或针对第三方提起的诉讼进行抗辩。无论主体处于何种立场，都会产生与诉讼过程相关的成本（例如律师费和专家证人费），并最终产生因庭外和解或法院判决而引起的成本（或收益）。此外，对于败诉方，如果该诉讼在保险承保范围内，还可能涉及保险索赔和潜在的保险赔款。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体需要仔细考虑是否存在需要计提准备的现时义务和很可能的流出。清偿的可能性最初可能极小，因此不披露或有负债。一旦诉讼启动，流出可能变为可能（需要披露），进而变为很可能（需要确认准备）。在最终判决作出之前，结果尚不确定。即便如此，针对保险公司的索赔能否成功仍可能存在不确定性。下文示例及各段讨论了其中的若干方面。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体销售一种含铅汽油发动机添加剂，使客户能够满足新的排放要求。十名客户声称产品罐存在缺陷，使用时爆裂，添加剂灼伤了他们的手。该主体已就此责任投保，即使索赔成功，也预期不会蒙受任何经济损失。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体应当首先确定是否存在现时义务。过去事项是向客户销售可能存在缺陷的商品。如果产品罐确实存在缺陷，则存在现时义务。当事实不清楚时，主体将确定存在现时义务是否很可能，这可能需要寻求专家意见。在本示例中，主体可能辩称产品罐没有任何问题，而是客户未遵循主体的使用说明传单（该传单明确说明了如何避免所报告的问题）。如果产品罐很可能存在缺陷，则存在现时义务，主体应当进一步确定是否存在很可能的流出。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 一旦确定存在现时义务，就需要判断经济利益流出是否很可能。该判断基于经济利益流出的可能性是否大于不流出的可能性。作出这些评估可能需要寻求专家意见。在资产负债表日至主体财务报表最终定稿日之间获得的进一步信息，应当纳入考量以确定流出是否很可能。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 当存在现时义务且流出很可能时，下一步是确定主体能否可靠地估计可能的结果。同样，主体可能需要寻求专家意见。IAS 37 提及，仅在极其罕见的情况下无法作出可靠估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 一旦确定应当确认准备，下一个问题是计量。在此考虑简单的“年末”测试会很有帮助。如果主体在年末停止营业，它需要支付多少钱来清偿该义务？主体需要考虑与该案件相关的风险和不确定性。这显然取决于索赔的可能结果。例如，如果主体决定庭外和解，则应按估计的和解成本计提准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 我们认为，在律师提供服务之前，不应确认法律费用的负债。因此，如果未对基础法律索赔确认准备，则不能确认法律费用。但是，当管理层确定应当对基础法律索赔确认准备时，如果第三方在计算接手该义务所收取的金额时会将未来法律费用考虑在内，则在准备中包含对未来直接且增量的法律费用的估计可能是恰当的。如果主体按其预期与索赔人达成和解的金额计量准备，则为未来法律费用计提准备将是不恰当的（例如，预期索赔将在期末后不久达成和解）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 当主体履行该义务时几乎确定能够收到保险赔款时，确认一项保险赔款应收款。如果收到赔款并非几乎确定，则披露一项或有资产。一旦保险公司接受理赔，保险赔款的收取通常即达到几乎确定。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在主体的财务报表中，可能需要披露其针对该诉讼计提的准备以及相关的保险赔款应收款。除该准备的变动情况外，还需要披露其性质、预期清偿时间的简要描述以及不确定性的说明。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 所要求的披露可能会严重损害主体在诉讼中的地位。在那些极其罕见的情况下，主体可以豁免上述披露。但是，主体需要披露争议的一般性质以及未披露相关信息的理由（参见FAQ 16.88.1）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.2 – 确认标准在产品质量保证中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 产品质量保证通常在销售商品或提供服务的同时向客户提供。质量保证的性质可能因不同主体、行业、产品或合同而异。质量保证义务可能通过法律的实施（合同或法规）产生，也可能通过主体明示的政策或习惯做法产生（如第16.11段及以下所述）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果已售物品被证明在销售时存在缺陷（通常基于在标准期限内发现的证据），买方可能有权要求卖方修复缺陷或更换故障物品。此类质量保证被视为“保证类质量保证”，与已售物品在销售日的状况相关。它通常不被视为可与商品销售相区分。如果客户没有单独购买该质量保证的选择权，则此类质量保证按照 IAS 37 进行会计处理。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 服务类质量保证超出了保证类质量保证的范围，除了保证产品按预期运行外，还向客户提供额外服务。服务类质量保证通常单独销售，被视为交易中可区分的组成部分。此类质量保证按照 IFRS 15 进行会计处理，并在第11章第219段及以下中进一步讨论。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 保证类质量保证的准备在销售时按组合基础予以确认。下文解释了 IAS 37 所给示例中包含的原则。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例1 – 产品维修或更换

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体销售园艺商品。其在销售时保证，将通过维修或更换来修复自销售日起一年内显现的制造缺陷。其过往经验表明，该主体确实会收到关于这些产品的质量保证索赔。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 导致义务发生的事项是产品的销售。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 维修成本与主体的未来经营无关。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 过往经验表明，该义务导致经济利益流出的可能性大于不流出的可能性。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 可以根据主体以往的索赔经验对义务作出可靠估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该主体通常会利用其过往索赔经验来估计准备的金额。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例2 – 已投保的产品质量保证义务

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 事实与示例1相同，不同之处在于主体向第三方保险公司支付保费以承保该风险。如果客户提出索赔，主体将向保险公司索赔相应金额。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 基于示例1所述理由，仍应就该产品质量保证计提准备。保险安排的存在并不意味着主体可以忽视该质量保证义务。客户就产品质量保证对主体拥有直接追索权。相应地，主体对保险公司拥有索赔权，但这并未消除主体对其客户的义务。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 因此，主体应当就产品质量保证义务确认准备。主体还将考虑是否可以确认来自保险公司的赔款。除非在质量保证索赔获得清偿时几乎确定能够收回赔款，否则不能就此索赔单独确认应收款。如果并非几乎确定但很可能收回，主体应当披露一项或有资产。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如何计量产品质量保证索赔准备的示例载于FAQ 16.47.1。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.3 – 确认标准在退款中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 许多主体的退款政策超出了消费者保护法赋予客户的权利。例如，许多零售商对退回的产品（无论是否存在缺陷）均给予现金退款，而另一些零售商甚至在客户没有显示购买日期的收据的情况下也给予现金退款。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 这些政策可能已经以某种方式长期实施，以至于客户预期这些政策将继续下去。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: IAS 37 包含一个示例，探讨了应如何处理此类退款政策：

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例1 – 基于过去习惯做法的退款义务

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某零售主体有一项向不满意的客户退款的政策，即使其并无法定义务这样做。该主体已采用该政策多年，且该政策为其客户所熟知。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该主体应当确认准备，因为：

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 其存在现时推定义务。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 导致义务发生的事项是商品销售，这已在客户中形成了主体在现实中无法撤回的合理预期。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 该义务与未来经营成本无关。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 过往经验表明，该义务导致经济利益流出的可能性大于不流出的可能性。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 可以根据过往退款情况对义务作出可靠估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体有时可能需要召回有缺陷的商品。下文示例探讨了期末前销售的商品在期末后被召回的影响。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某零售商必须对其在年末前销售的商品进行产品召回，因为这些商品随后被发现存在缺陷。召回通知是在年末之后发布的。根据该零售商的供应合同，召回成本可向主体的供应商追偿。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该零售商是否需要在年末为召回成本计提准备？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 应当在年末为召回成本计提准备。导致义务发生的事项是销售有缺陷的商品，而非发布召回通知。在资产负债表日，主体承担召回有缺陷商品的义务，存在很可能的流出，且该义务能够可靠计量。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该零售商应如何对向供应商的追偿进行会计处理？ 仅当发生召回支出时几乎确定能够从供应商处收回该成本时，才能确认向供应商的追偿。如果并非几乎确定（例如，对于追偿的法律可执行性或供应商的支付能力存在一定疑问），但很可能收回，则将该成本的追偿披露为或有资产。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.4 – 确认标准在不同情形下大修和维修中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体经常对其自有资产或 IFRS 16 下的租赁资产进行大修和维修。它们是否需要为此类费用确认准备？下文示例对此进行了讨论。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 极不可能为自有资产的大修和维修计提准备，因为这不符合 IAS 37 第14段的确认标准。主体对是否发生该支出拥有自主决定权。例如，主体可以通过出售该资产来避免该支出。但是，当某项不动产、厂场和设备（“PPE”）需要定期更换或大修时，大修组成部分应当在至下一次大修日的剩余期间内计提折旧。[IAS 16 第43段]。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例1 – 不动产、厂场和设备（PPE）的大修

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体拥有一座高炉，其炉衬需要每五年更换一次。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在主体实际发生支出之前，不能为更换炉衬计提准备；在此之前，主体不存在现时义务，因为其并非必须更换炉衬。例如，主体可以通过关闭高炉来避免该义务。在支出发生前不计提准备，但高炉炉衬应当单独识别，并在两次更换之间的期间内计提折旧。当发生更换炉衬的支出时，该支出将作为高炉成本的一部分予以资本化，并在至下一次更换的期间内计提折旧。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 一旦新炉衬的成本予以资本化，原高炉炉衬对应的成本和累计折旧应当予以终止确认。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 自有资产的维修支出不能在实际发生之前预先计提准备，即使外部对该资产的维修提出了要求。以下示例说明了这一点。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例2 – 要求维修的贷款契约

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体全额购买了一些资产，并为此向银行借款。银行贷款契约包含要求主体保持资产处于良好状态的条款。主体是否应当因为该维修契约条款而为自有资产的维修计提准备？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 当自有固定资产用作贷款抵押且契约条款要求对资产进行维修时，未进行维修本身并不会产生违约金。当然，如果以任何方式违反契约条款，银行可以要求提前偿还贷款。此类条款的目的是确保银行在违约情况下拥有充足的抵押品。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 未能维修用于抵押贷款的资产可能会触发提前偿还该贷款（该贷款已确认为一项负债），但并不会触发针对维修工作的赔偿索赔。由于主体可以通过偿还贷款来避免维修，因此主体不存在现时义务。在此情形下不应确认准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 租赁资产也可能存在维修要求，并且可能作为租赁条款的一部分予以规定。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例3 – 租赁资产的大修成本

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体租赁一艘船舶，租期为25年。主体必须取得适航证书，这要求主体每五年在干船坞进行一次重大维修和大修工作。没有该证书，船舶无法运营。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 虽然没有适航证书船舶无法继续运营，但这本身并不使主体承担实施维修的义务。例如，主体可以决定将船舶停航而不再使用。主体应当审阅租赁条款，以确定是否存在任何产生合同义务的约定。如果租赁合同未产生义务，则不存在现时义务。在产生大修义务之前不应计提准备。当大修实际实施时，相关成本将作为使用权资产的一部分予以资本化（根据 IFRS 16），并在至下一次大修的期间内计提折旧。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.5 – 确认标准在租赁损毁修复中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 许多房产租赁合同都包含承租人对损毁进行修复的条款。这些条款通常要求承租人在租期结束时按指定状态将房产归还给出租人。是应当在租赁期内为修复损毁的成本计提准备，还是应当在实施修复工作时将其费用化？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 以下示例说明了相关问题。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例 – 房产租赁条款要求的修复

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体目前是一家租赁房产的承租人，将于五年后腾退该房产。租赁协议中有一项条款规定了在腾退房产之前必须开展的修复工作，还有一项条款允许出租人向承租人追偿与修复建筑物相关的费用。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 应当在租赁期内为估计的修复成本计提准备，因为：

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 承租人因租赁协议而承担现时合同义务。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 导致义务发生的事项是房产的磨损，该磨损在租赁期内发生。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 该义务源自房产的磨损，与未来经营成本无关。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 该义务很可能导致经济利益流出。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 能够对因磨损产生的义务作出可靠估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 从租赁合同中应当可以明确是否存在义务。当识别出任何损毁时，即应当确认准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.6 – 确认标准在租入资产改良支出中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某些租赁允许承租人对房产进行改良（例如加装隔断），但同时规定承租人有义务在租期结束时将房产恢复原状。这可能需要拆除改良设施。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 示例 – 将房产恢复至租赁开始时的状态

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体签订了一项仓库租赁合同，希望将该仓库用作办公场所。租赁合同允许主体耗资 C150万 搭建夹层并加装隔断以改造为办公室。租期为15年，且规定房产必须按原状归还给出租人。主体估计拆除改良设施的成本现值为 C500,000。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该主体应当根据 IAS 16 将 C150万 的租入资产改良支出予以资本化，并在租赁期内摊销。该主体在租赁合同下承担了在租期结束时拆除改良设施的现时义务。该义务在主体完成改良工程时产生，此即过去事项。应当在改良工程完成时确认现值 C500,000 的准备，同时根据 IFRS 16 将相同金额确认为使用权资产的一部分。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.7 – 确认标准在废弃与弃置成本中的应用

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: “废弃”一词用于描述：封井和弃井；拆除井口、生产和运输设施；以及根据许可证要求和相关法规对生产区域进行复原。这些活动通常在设施停止生产、处理、运输或储存可销售数量的石油或天然气之日开始。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体耗资 C1亿 建造了一座核设施，预计该电厂将在未来30年内运行。主体利用现有技术估计，按当前货币计量，电厂停止运行后的弃置成本为 C2亿，50年后的弃置成本为 C1亿。为简化本示例，假设该义务在第1天即已产生，且弃置成本将在第30年末和第50年末发生。同时假设第30年和第50年现金流量的无风险利率均为 4.5%，且多年来保持不变。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 采用 4.5% 的折现率，弃置义务的净现值为 C64,470,000。该设施应按其原始成本 C1亿 加上该义务的初始成本 C64,470,000 入账，总成本为 C164,470,000。该金额随后应当在设施30年的运行寿命内摊销，采用直线法每年计提摊销费用 C5,480,000（其中每年 C2,150,000 与资本化的义务有关）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 多年来该义务的增加完全源自折现的转回。早期年份的影响相对较小（例如，第1年末义务增加 C2,900,000），但折现影响呈后期递增趋势，在第30年，该义务增加 C10,400,000。折现的转回列报为借款费用，而资产带来的收益和折旧则列报于营业利润中。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 设施的使用寿命与弃置发生前的期间之间存在错配。在支付 C2亿 后，第30年末（即设施使用寿命结束时）的义务余额为 C41,460,000。在第31年至第50年，准备的折现按无风险利率转回并确认为借款费用，直至第50年末义务确立。这意味着主体将在第31年至第50年确认 C58,540,000（即 C1亿 减去 C41,460,000）的借款费用。

text: 示例5 – 针对过去污染的已生效法规

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 已出台一项健康与安全法规，要求从所有建筑物中清除石棉。只要已知存在石棉，无论房产是否在使用中或是否已停止运营，均必须清除石棉。该法规自 20X2年12月31日起生效。A主体拥有一座20年历史的工厂，并已确认其中含有石棉。估计清除石棉的成本为 C70,000，此外由于清除石棉期间工厂无法满负荷运转，还将损失 C30,000 的利润。截至 20X2年12月31日，石棉清除工作尚未开始；但已与承包商签订合同，将在 20X3年最初几个月内实施该项工作。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该健康与安全法规已经颁布，因此存在清除石棉的要求。导致义务发生的（过去）事项是石棉的存在所造成的污染。清除石棉的法定要求产生了义务。因此，A主体应当确认 C70,000 的准备，即清除石棉的直接成本。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 不应为清除石棉期间将发生的经营亏损计提准备，因为不存在承担这些亏损的义务。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 已签订合同的存在不影响是否就该成本计提准备的结论。这些合同属于待执行合同，因此在承包商履行合同项下的工作之前，不对承包商产生负债。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 新法律的出台本身并不构成导致义务发生的事项。是过去的污染与新法律的结合产生了清除石棉的义务。这可以与上述示例4中的烟雾过滤器形成对比：在示例4中不存在过去的污染，因此法规生效时产生的义务仅限于处罚和罚款。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: EX 16.85.9 – 确认标准在排放义务中应用的详细讨论

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则索引：IAS 37 正文索引：16.85

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 许多司法管辖区引入了总量控制与交易机制（cap and trade schemes），以鼓励减少温室气体排放。这些机制通常涉及在履约期开始时分配有限数量的排放配额，并要求主体在履约期末拥有足够的配额以覆盖其排放量。部分机制允许主体（在免费配额之外）购买额外配额，或出售因减少排放而产生的盈余配额。 温室气体的排放会产生交付配额的义务。主体应当就截至资产负债表日已产生的排放量，确认与该义务相关的负债（及相关费用）。参与这些机制可采用多种会计模型。负债的计量将取决于所采用的会计模型。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 其中一种模型是 IFRIC 3 模型，该模型规范了“总量控制与交易”排放权机制的会计处理。该模型要求主体将从政府获得的排放配额作为无形资产进行会计处理，并按公允价值初始入账。如果配额以低于公允价值的价格发放，则所付金额与公允价值之间的差额作为政府补助处理，并按照 IAS 20 进行会计处理。该补助在资产负债表中初始确认为递延收益，随后在发放配额所对应的履约期内按系统基础分期计入收益（无论是均匀分摊还是在产生排放时按先进先出法结转），无论该配额是继续持有还是出售。主体应当就交付与已产生排放量相等配额的义务确认一项负债。该负债按照资产负债表日清偿现时义务所需支出的最佳估计数计量（通常为覆盖截至资产负债表日已产生排放量所需配额数量的市场价格）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: IFRIC 3 并未规范自身并非总量控制与交易机制参与者的经纪商——交易商。但是，我们认为，只要排放权是在日常经营过程中持有以备出售的资产，就符合存货的定义，必须按照 IAS 2 以成本与可变现净值孰低进行计量。如果主体适用针对经纪商——交易商的要求，则排放权按公允价值计量（IAS 2 第3段）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果主体按市场价值记录其部分或全部排放义务，通常应当使用其需要购买的相关配额的市场价格来计算准备。但是，如果主体已签订远期合同，在未来某一日期以固定价格购买配额，则允许按远期合同价格（而非市场价格）计提准备，因为这是主体预期为清偿其义务而支付金额的最佳估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 以下示例说明了“完全市场价值”法（即 IFRIC 3 所规定的方法）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某主体参与一项排放权“总量控制与交易”机制；20X6年1月1日，该主体免费获配在 20X6公历年度（亦为其财务会计期间）排放 10,000 吨二氧化碳的配额。20X6年1月1日，每单位配额（相当于一吨二氧化碳）的市场价格为 C10，因此公允价值为 C100,000。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 截至 20X6年6月30日，该主体已排放 6,000 吨二氧化碳，并预计全年排放量为 12,500 吨。配额的市场价格已上涨至每吨 C11。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 年末，该主体实际排放了预期的 12,500 吨，配额的市场价格为每吨 C12。假设主体在初始确认后采用 IAS 38 的重估模式按公允价值计量该无形资产，主体应如何按照 IFRIC 3 规定的方法（“完全市场价值”法）对该机制进行会计处理？

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 该主体将按公允价值 C100,000 记录初始收到的配额，确认同等金额的无形资产，并将政府补助按相同金额记录为递延收益。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 20X6年6月30日，该主体将就截至当日的排放确认 C66,000（6,000 吨 × 每吨 C11）的负债。账面价值为 C100,000 的无形资产重估至 C110,000（10,000 吨 × 每吨 C11）。无形资产产生的 C10,000 重估盈余计入其他综合收益（OCI）。关于主体如何确认与政府补助相关的递延收益，实务中存在不同做法：

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 一种方法是按截至当日的排放量占履约期预计总排放量的比例结转递延收益——即 C100,000 × 6,000 / 12,500 = C48,000。该方法认为 IAS 20 中的配比原则应应用于整个履约期。因此，截至 20X6年6月30日的损益反映结转的递延收益 C48,000 减去计提的排放负债费用 C66,000，当期计入损益的净费用为 C18,000。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: - 另一种方法是随着配额的使用按每单位配额结转递延收益——即 C100,000 × 6,000 / 10,000 = C60,000。该方法反映了截至中期报告期末已使用了 60% 的配额（即 60% 的政府补助）这一事实。因此，截至 20X6年6月30日的损益反映结转的递延收益 C60,000 减去计提的排放负债费用 C66,000，当期计入损益的净费用为 C6,000。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 20X6年12月31日（忽略 20X6年6月30日的分录），该主体确认排放负债 C150,000（12,500 吨 × 每吨 C12）。资产重估至 C120,000（10,000 吨 × 每吨 C12）。全部 C100,000 的递延收益予以结转。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 对全年损益的影响是：就排放义务确认负债 C150,000（基于资产负债表日配额的市场价格），并结转递延收益 C100,000。C20,000 的重估盈余计入其他综合收益（OCI）。计入损益的净费用为 C50,000。将其与计入其他综合收益（OCI）的 C20,000 重估盈余合并考虑，C30,000 的净额代表主体超额排放 2,500 吨（超出免费获授配额的部分）乘以年末市场价格每吨 C12 的成本。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果对该无形资产采用 IAS 38 的成本模式，且在初始确认后按成本（就此目的而言，成本为初始确认日的公允价值）减去摊销和/或减值计量，则年末不会产生 C20,000 的重估盈余，无形资产仍按 C100,000 列报。由于 C150,000 负债中的一部分将通过使用账面价值为 C100,000（但价值 C120,000）的配额来清偿，主体仅需支付 C30,000。负债的剩余余额 C20,000 将在清偿时转回至利润表。因此，计入损益的净费用将为 C30,000。这同样代表超额排放 2,500 吨乘以每吨 C12 的成本。因此，无论采用 IAS 38 的成本模式还是重估模式，对综合收益总额的总体净影响相同（净损失 C30,000）。但会存在时间性差异，因为在成本模式下，清偿负债产生的利得（C20,000）仅在负债清偿时（即年末之后）确认。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 采用“结算成本”法的主体，仅在截至当日已产生的排放量超过所持配额数量时，才按当前（即资产负债表日）配额的市场价格计量义务。如果排放量未超过所持配额，则不存在购买额外配额的义务，从而不存在负债。在上述示例中，配额将按零成本初始确认，负债将按 10,000 × 零（针对主体持有的配额）+ 2,500 × C12（针对需从市场购买的配额）计量，得出年末负债总额为 C30,000（而非“完全市场价值”法下的 C150,000）。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 采用“结算成本”法的主体还需考虑另一项因素，因为对已有配额覆盖部分的义务计量，将取决于配额的账面价值是按先进先出法（FIFO）还是按加权平均法分摊至该义务。当资产负债表日并非履约期末时——例如在中期资产负债表日（财务年度与履约期相同）或在财务年度末（财务年度与履约期不同）——这尤其值得关注。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 采用先进先出法的主体，在截至资产负债表日所持配额数量（如有）范围内，按每单位排放对应的配额账面价值计量义务，对于资产负债表日的配额缺口（如有），则按每单位预期成本（即资产负债表日的市场价格）计量。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 采用加权平均法的主体，按整个履约期预计将发生的每单位排放加权平均成本计量义务。为此，主体需确定履约期的预计总排放量，并将其与政府授予（和/或已购买）且主体仍为该履约期持有的配额单位数量进行比较，以确定履约期内所持配额的预计缺口（如有）。履约期每单位排放的加权平均成本等于所持配额的账面价值（对于无偿获授的配额可能为零）加上弥补预计缺口的成本（使用资产负债表日的市场价格），再除以履约期的预计总排放单位数。换言之：

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 主体可以购买保险以承保潜在的未来损失。该成本根据保费的性质进行会计处理。主体也可以决定实行自保，而非与第三方签订保险合同。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 对部分风险实行自保的主体，应当就资产负债表日之前发生的事项所引起的索赔计提准备，即使这些索赔是在年末之后才报告的。主体应当考虑资产负债表日后出现的任何额外证据，以确定截至资产负债表日已发生哪些导致义务发生的事项。主体还应当就资产负债表日之前已发生但尚未报告的预期索赔（称为“已发生未报告索赔”，即 IBNR 索赔）的估计数计提准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 某经营连锁零售门店的主体决定不向第三方投保客户轻微意外事故的风险，而是实行自保。其过往经验表明，平均每年需就此类事故支付 C200,000。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在事故发生之前，不对另一方产生义务。因此，如果截至年末未发生任何事故，则不存在现时义务，不应计提准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果已经发生事故，零售商可能尚不知晓该事故的发生，但仍应计提准备。零售商应当（可能通过精算方法）估计已发生但尚未报告的事故水平（即客户的 IBNR 索赔），并就其对该义务的估计计提准备。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 在主体年末至财务报表最终定稿日之间，可能会浮现出若干 IBNR 索赔，从而能够对这些索赔作出更准确的估计。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 如果项目的性质足够相似，出于披露目的可以按类别合并准备。不同类别准备的示例包括重组、收购整合、产品质量保证和环境负债。例如，将不同产品的质量保证作为单一类别处理可能是恰当的，但 IAS 37 指出，将与正常产品质量保证相关的金额和涉及法律诉讼的金额作为单一类别处理是不恰当的。此外，还需要考虑各类别的重要性，对于单项不重大的准备可能需要进行一定程度的合并。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 准则并未就 IAS 37 披露目的下“不切实可行”的含义作进一步阐述。可能存在无法确定与某项准备的时间相关的不确定性，或者估计财务影响存在困难的情形。但是，国际会计准则理事会（IASB）的意图是主体应当尽最大努力确定所有要求披露的信息。

chapter: 16 - Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets (IAS 37)
text: 有关准备、或有负债和或有资产的某些信息（例如诉讼和诉讼赔款，特别是通过保险获得的赔款）可能非常敏感，充分披露可能会损害特定案件的结果。国际会计准则理事会（IASB）认可这一点，并允许在极其罕见的情况下，如果披露 IAS 37 要求的部分或全部信息会严重损害主体就准备、或有负债或或有资产所涉事项与其他方发生争议时的立场，则可以接受主体不必提供如此详尽的披露。但是，主体仍需披露争议的一般性质，以及未披露该信息的事实和原因。

17.4 Government grants should not be recognised until there is reasonable assurance that the entity will comply with the conditions attaching to it and that the grant will be received. Reasonable assurance is not defined in IFRS and significant judgment is therefore required when the recognition criteria under IAS 20 is applied in practice.

17.5 The manner in which a grant is received does not affect the accounting method to be adopted in regard to the grant. A grant is accounted for in the same way whether it is received in cash or as a reduction of a liability to the government.

17.6 Government grants are recognised in the income statement on a systematic basis over the periods in which the related costs towards which they are intended to compensate are recognised as expenses.

17.7 Grants for specific expenses are recognised in profit or loss in the same period as the relevant expense. Grants related to depreciable assets are usually recognised in profit or loss over the periods and in the proportions in which depreciation expense on those assets is recognised. The relationship between the grant and the related expenditure is, therefore, of paramount importance in establishing the accounting treatment.

17.8 Government loans that are forgivable, when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will meet the terms for forgiveness of the loan, or where a government loan is below market rate, are grants that should be accounted for in accordance with the standard.

17.9 Grants might be received as part of a package of financial or fiscal aids where a number of conditions are attached. Care is needed in identifying the conditions giving rise to costs and expenses that determine the periods over which the grant will be earned. Measurement (paras 17.11 - 17.12)

17.11 A government grant might take the form of a transfer of a non-monetary asset, such as land or other resources, for the use of the entity. In these circumstances, it is usual to assess the fair value of the non-monetary asset and to account for both grant and asset at that fair value. IAS 20 also allows an alternative course to record both grant and asset at a nominal amount.

17.12 The benefit of a government loan at a below market rate of interest should be accounted for as a government grant under IAS 20 while the relevant standard for measurement of the loan is IFRS 9. The benefit should be measured as the difference between the initial carrying value of the loan determined in accordance with IFRS 9 and the proceeds received.

In order to determine the appropriate accounting treatment, it is important to understand the nature of these reliefs and the conditions attached to them. Broadly, these reliefs and measures are government assistance if they are designed to provide economic benefit specific to an entity or range of entities qualifying under certain criteria. - There must be a transfer of resources to the entity – the government assistance could be in the form of a receipt of an asset or a reduction in a liability. That said, incremental resources provided to the entity, such as cash refunds or the forgiveness of an existing indirect tax obligation, are more likely to be government grants than reductions

- There must be past or future compliance with certain conditions – the government assistance is provided in return for past or future compliance with certain conditions (implicit or explicit). The more substantive the required conditions are, the more likely the relief is a government grant.

- The conditions must relate to the operating activities of the entity – in order to receive or become eligible for the government assistance, there are certain conditions or obligations that are connected with the operating activities of the entity.

However, in certain circumstances, grants might be awarded without regard to further requirements or further actions by specific entities (for instance, in certain regions or industry sectors). [IAS 20 para 3]. FAQ 17.2.2 – How should an entity determine whether it has received a grant within the scope of to which it applies IAS 20?
Reference to standard: IAS 20 para 3
Reference to standing text: 17.2
A government provides a cash rebate to an entity (lessor) in the form of a property tax rebate. The rebate has the following features:

- The rebate does not have an explicit requirement that it is passed on to the lessees. However, due to strong advice and monitoring by the government, it is expected that the lessor will pass on the rebate to lessees in the form of a reduction in rent payments.

- The lessor has discretion over the proportion of the rebate allocated to individual lessees and the manner in which the rebate is passed on. For example, for some leases, the lessor might provide a fixed amount of rebate per month; whereas for other leases, the lessor might provide a percentage rental reduction per month or make a single payment to the lessee. In some cases, the lessor might provide more relief to the lessees than the rebate re
How should the entity determine whether it has received a grant within the scope of IAS 20?

IAS 20 provides no explicit guidance on determining which party receives a government grant. In many cases, it will be clear which party is the recipient of the grant, because there are only two parties. However, many of the government relief programmes are targeted at supporting small or medium-sized businesses or individuals and, as a consequence, the government is using other entities (that is, intermediaries) to facilitate the distribution of

If the intermediary controls the grant before it transfers to the final party, this indicates that the intermediary is the party that obtains the grant from the government, and it should therefore apply IAS 20. If the intermediary does not control the grant before it transfers to the final party, the intermediary would not apply IAS 20 to the transaction. The intermediary might still need to recognise other assets or liabilities related to the ar

Assessing whether control exists helps to identify the economic resource which the entity accounts for. An entity controls an economic resource if it has the present ability to direct the use of the economic resource and to obtain the economic benefits that might flow from it. Factors that might be helpful in determining if the intermediary controls the grant before it transfers to the final party include:

- whether the intermediary has discretion over which end parties receive the relief. For example, if an employer has discretion over which employees receive a relief package, this might indicate that the employer controls the grant before it is transferred to the selected employees;

- whether the intermediary has discretion over how much of the relief it must distribute and the manner in which it makes the distribution. For example, if a lessor can determine how much of a relief package it needs to pass on to lessees, or whether the relief will take the form of a payment holiday, payment deferral or reduced rental, this might indicate that the lessor controls the relief before it transfers to the lessee;

- whether the intermediary has discretion over the timing of when it distributes the relief. For example, if a lessee can demand a lessor to pass over relief that was provided under a relief package, this might indicate that the lessor does not control the grant before it transfers to the lessee; and

- whether the intermediary initiates the application for the relief or whether this is determined by the end party. For example, if a borrower applies through an intermediary bank for a government-subsidised loan, this might indicate that the bank does not control the grant before it transfers to the borrower.
Consequently, in the illustration above, it is likely that the lessor, and not the lessee, would apply IAS 20 to any rebate that it receives.

In this example, the employer is not the recipient of the grant, because it does not control the cash relief and it does not have the present ability to direct the use of the cash to obtain benefits. FAQ 17.14.1 – How should a grant related to an asset be accounted for?
Reference to standard: IAS 20 para 24 Reference to standing text: 17.14

Entity A is awarded a government grant of C100,000 on 1 January 20X6 towards the construction of a manufacturing plant. The plant’s useful life is estimated at 10 years. The entity took two years to construct the plant. At 1 January 20X9 the entity started to use the plant for manufacturing products. The entity has a December year end. How should the entity account for the grant?
The C100,000 grant relates to the construction of an asset and should be initially recognised as deferred income.
The deferred income should be recognised as income on a systematic and rational basis over the asset’s useful life.

The entity should recognise a liability on the balance sheet for the years ending 31 December 20X7 and 31 December 20X8. Once the plant starts being used in the manufacturing process, other operating income of C10,000 should be recognised in each year of the asset’s 10 year useful life to compensate for depreciation costs.
Under the allowed alternative treatment in IAS 20, Entity A would also be permitted to offset the deferred income of C100,000 against the cost of the plant on 1 January 20X9.

17 - 政府补助（IAS 20）
17 - 政府补助（IAS 20）
17.1 本章阐述国际财务报告准则（IFRS）关于政府补助和政府援助的相关要求。
17.2 政府补助是指政府通过向主体转移资源以换取主体在过去或未来满足与主体经营活动相关的特定条件而提供的援助。此类政府补助可能用于帮助主体为特定资产或其他支出提供资金。地方、国家和国际政府（包括政府间机构和类似组织）提供的补助均属于 IAS 20 的范围。
[IAS 20 第3段]。
FAQ 17.2.1 – 主体应如何确定一项政府纾困或措施是否属于 IAS 20 范围内的政府补助？ FAQ 17.2.2 – 主体应如何确定其是否收到了适用 IAS 20 范围的补助？ FAQ 17.2.3 – 主体应如何对支持企业弥补收入损失的纾困计划进行会计处理？
17.3 与所得税、农业相关的补助，以及政府参与主体所有权的情况，不属于 IAS 20 的范围。参见第14章第4段、第33章第27段和第6章第70段。
[IAS 20 第2段]。
17.4 政府补助在合理保证主体能够满足其所附条件且能够收到该项补助之前，不予确认。国际财务报告准则未对“合理保证”作出定义，因此在实务中应用 IAS 20 的确认标准时需要进行重大判断。
[IAS 20 第7段]。
17.5 收到补助的方式不影响针对该补助所采用的会计处理方法。无论补助是以现金形式收到，还是作为对政府负债的减免，均采用相同的会计处理方法。
[IAS 20 第9段]。
17.6 政府补助应在主体将补助拟补偿的相关成本确认为费用的各期间内，按系统的方法计入利润表。
[IAS 20 第12段]。
17.7 针对特定费用的补助在与相关费用相同的期间内计入损益。与可折旧资产相关的补助通常在确认该资产折旧费用的各期间内，按相同的比例计入损益。因此，补助与相关支出之间的关系对于确定会计处理方法至关重要。
[IAS 20 第17段]。
17.8 当有合理保证主体将满足可豁免贷款的豁免条款时，政府提供的可豁免贷款，或者政府提供的低于市场利率的贷款，均属于应按照本准则进行会计处理的补助。
[IAS 20 第10段]。

17.9 补助可能作为附带多项条件的一揽子财务或财政援助计划的一部分而被收到。在识别产生决定补助赚取期间的成本和费用的条件时，需要谨慎判断。将补助的一部分按一种基础（与资产相关的补助）分摊、另一部分按另一种基础（与收益相关的补助）分摊可能是恰当的。随后可以根据补助拟补偿的不同类型的成本和费用，对补助的各部分采用不同的会计处理。如果补助要求履行不同的义务，则应在确认履行这些义务的相关成本和费用的各期间内将其计入利润表。
[IAS 20 第19段]。
FAQ 17.9.1 – 主体应如何识别一项补助拟补偿的相关费用？ FAQ 17.9.2 – 补助应如何分摊至已识别的支出？ FAQ 17.9.3 – 达成非财务目标后应支付的补助应如何进行会计处理？
17.10 在某些情况下，政府补助可能是无条件授予的，不考虑主体的未来行动，也不要求发生进一步成本。此类补助可能是为向主体提供即时财务支持或援助而给予，也可能是为补偿先前已发生的成本而给予。它们还可能用于在特定期间内为主体的一般经营活动提供资金，或用于补偿收入损失。在此基础上授予的补助，应在其成为应收款项的期间内计入利润表。
[IAS 20 第20段]。
FAQ 17.10.1 – 主体应如何对无条件补助进行会计处理？
17.11 政府补助可能采取向主体转移非货币性资产（如土地或其他资源）供其使用的形式。在此类情况下，通常的做法是评估该非货币性资产的公允价值，并按该公允价值对补助和资产进行会计处理。IAS 20 也允许采用另一种替代方法，即按名义金额记录补助和资产。
[IAS 20 第23段]。
17.12 低于市场利率的政府贷款所带来的利益应按照 IAS 20 作为政府补助进行会计处理，而计量该贷款的相关准则为 IFRS 9。该利益应按照依据 IFRS 9 确定的贷款初始账面价值与收到的款项之间的差额进行计量。
[IAS 20 第10A段]。
与收益相关的补助的列报（第17.13段）
17.13 IAS 20 对于补助收益在利润表中的列报位置提供了一定的灵活性。与收益相关的补助（补助收益）有时在利润表中作为贷项列报，既可以单独列报，也可以归入“其他收益”等一般项目下列报。或者，也可以在报告相关费用时予以冲减。所采用的列报方法应对所有类似补助一致应用。
[IAS 20 第29段]。
17.13.1 关于与收益相关的补助在现金流量表中的列报，正如第7章第13段所述，现金流量分类应以最适合主体业务的方式进行列报。FAQ 7.13.2对此进行了更详细的说明，并提供了在补助收益背景下的示例。
[IAS 7 第11段]。
与资产相关的补助的列报（第17.14段）
17.14 与资产相关的政府补助（包括按公允价值计量的非货币性补助），在资产负债表中应当通过将补助确认为递延收益，或者通过将补助冲减资产账面价值的方式予以列报。无论采用哪种方式，都会使补助收益在资产计提折旧的同一期间内得到确认。通过这种方式，补助收益在与该资产相关支出相同的期间内计入损益。
[IAS 20 第24段]。
FAQ 17.14.1 – 与资产相关的补助应如何进行会计处理？ FAQ 17.14.2 – 当相关资产因减值而被减记时，与资产相关的补助应如何进行会计处理？
17.14.1 关于与资产相关的补助在现金流量表中的列报（正如第7章第13段所述），现金流量分类应以最适合主体业务的方式进行列报。FAQ 7.13.2对此进行了更详细的说明，并提供了在与资产相关的补助背景下的示例。
[IAS 7 第11段]。
17.15 已确认政府补助收益的主体应当作出以下披露：
- 确认补助所采用的会计政策。
- 在财务报表中所采用的列报方法。
- 已确认政府补助的性质和金额。
- 主体从中直接受益的其他形式政府援助的说明。
- 与已确认政府援助相关的未满足条件及其他或有事项。
[IAS 20 第39段]。
FAQ 17.2.1 – 主体应如何确定一项政府纾困或措施是否属于 IAS 20 范围内的政府补助？
准则索引：IAS 20 第3段
在许多司法管辖区，当政府试图应对本辖区的经济下行时，可能会提供多项纾困措施或政策以帮助受影响的企业。这些纾困措施可能以多种组合方式提供，包括退还先前已缴纳的征费和间接税、可用于抵减未来间接税的抵免额、通过贷款或担保提供的财务支持、临时减免税费或营业税率、豁免义务或延期付款安排。
主体应如何确定一项政府纾困或措施是否属于 IAS 20 范围内的政府补助？

为了确定恰当的会计处理方法，了解这些纾困措施的性质及其所附条件非常重要。广义而言，如果这些纾困措施旨在向符合特定条件的某一主体或某类主体提供特定的经济利益，则它们属于政府援助。[IAS 20 第3段]。然而，并非所有政府援助均按照 IAS 20 作为政府补助进行会计处理；只有符合政府补助定义的纾困措施才应按照 IAS 20 进行会计处理。判断一项政府援助是否符合政府补助的定义需要进行判断。根据政府补助的定义，必须具备以下三个关键特征：
- 必须存在向主体的资源转移——政府援助的形式可以是收到一项资产或减少一项负债。收到纾困或激励措施的方式不影响会计处理。尽管如此，向主体提供的增量资源（如现金退还或豁免现有的间接税义务）比未来应付间接税或征费的减免更有可能构成政府补助。
- 必须存在过去或未来对特定条件的遵守——政府援助是以过去或未来遵守特定条件（隐含或明示）作为回报而提供的。所要求的条件越具实质性，该纾困措施就越有可能构成政府补助。
- 相关条件必须与主体的经营活动相关——为了获得政府援助或取得享受政府援助的资格，存在与主体经营活动相关的特定条件或义务。
然而，在某些情况下，补助的授予可能不考虑特定主体的进一步要求或进一步行动（例如，针对特定地区或特定行业部门）。为取得政府援助资格而在特定地区或行业部门开展经营的一般性要求，满足政府补助定义所要求的条件[SIC-10 第4段]。纾困措施越具体或越有针对性，就越有可能构成政府补助。

无法合理确定价值的政府援助，以及与政府之间无法与主体正常贸易交易相区分的交易，不属于政府补助。[IAS 20 第3段]。以在确定应纳税所得额时可享受的利益形式提供的纾困和措施不属于 IAS 20 的范围，而应按照 IAS 12 进行会计处理。[IAS 20 第2段]。适用于所有主体的其他间接税优惠或税率下调，实质上是对实际征费率或税率的减免或折扣，通常按照 IAS 37 和 IFRIC 21 进行会计处理。
关于金融机构实施的财务支持安排所涉及会计影响的进一步讨论，参见FAQ 42.97.4。
FAQ 17.2.2 – 主体应如何确定其是否收到了适用 IAS 20 范围的补助？
准则索引：IAS 20 第3段
政府以房产税退税的形式向某主体（出租人）提供现金退还。该退税具有以下特征：
- 该退税并未明确要求将其转交给承租人。然而，由于政府的强烈建议和监督，预计出租人将以减免租金付款的形式将该退税转交给承租人。
- 出租人有权自主决定分配给各个承租人的退税比例以及转交该退税的方式。例如，对于部分租赁，出租人可能每月提供固定金额的租金减免；而对于其他租赁，出租人可能每月提供一定比例的租金减免，或向承租人一次性支付款项。在某些情况下，出租人向承租人提供的减免金额可能高于其从政府收到的退税金额。
该主体应如何确定其是否收到了属于 IAS 20 范围内的补助？
IAS 20 并未就确定哪一方收到政府补助提供明确指引。在许多情况下，由于仅涉及两方，哪一方是补助的接收方是很明确的。然而，许多政府纾困计划旨在支持中小企业或个人，因此政府会利用其他主体（即中介机构）来协助发放纾困款项。在某些情况下，需要进行判断以确定中介机构是否收到了政府纾困并因此应当适用 IAS 20。
如果中介机构在将补助转交给最终接收方之前控制该补助，则表明该中介机构是从政府取得补助的一方，因此应当适用 IAS 20。如果中介机构在将补助转交给最终接收方之前并不控制该补助，则中介机构不对该交易适用 IAS 20。但中介机构可能仍需确认与该安排相关的其他资产或负债，以符合其他国际财务报告准则的要求。
评估是否存在控制有助于识别主体应当进行会计处理的经济资源。如果主体具有主导该经济资源的使用并从中获取可能产生的经济利益的现时能力，则主体控制该经济资源。有助于判断中介机构在将补助转交给最终接收方之前是否控制该补助的因素包括：
- 中介机构是否对哪些最终接收方获得纾困拥有自主决定权。例如，如果雇主有权自主决定哪些雇员获得纾困方案，这可能表明雇主在将补助转交给选定雇员之前控制该补助；
- 中介机构是否对必须分配多少纾困金额以及分配方式拥有自主决定权。例如，如果出租人能够决定需要将纾困方案中的多少金额转交给承租人，或者决定该纾困将采取免租期、延期付款还是减免租金的形式，这可能表明出租人在将纾困转交给承租人之前控制该纾困；
- 中介机构是否对发放纾困的时间拥有自主决定权。例如，如果承租人可以要求出租人转交根据纾困方案提供的纾困，这可能表明出租人在将补助转交给承租人之前并不控制该补助；以及
- 纾困申请是由中介机构发起，还是由最终接收方决定。例如，如果借款人通过中介银行申请政府贴息贷款，这可能表明银行在将补助转交给借款人之前并不控制该补助。
因此，在上述示例中，很可能由出租人而非承租人对其收到的任何退税适用 IAS 20。
以下是一个中介机构可能并非政府补助接收方的示例。
政府推出一项计划，允许符合特定条件的选定雇员在线申请政府纾困。随后，政府通过其雇主向雇员支付该纾困款项。雇主对于哪些雇员获得补助或补助金额没有任何自主决定权。雇主在法律上有义务在收到相关纾困款项后的七日内将现金转交给雇员。
在此示例中，雇主并非补助的接收方，因为其不控制该现金纾困，也不具有主导该现金使用以获取利益的现时能力。雇主对向雇员分配补助的时间、金额或方式均无自主决定权。为符合其他国际财务报告准则的要求，雇主可能仍需确认与该安排相关的其他资产或负债——即在报告期末已收到但尚未发放现金的情况下，确认现金资产及对雇员的相关负债。
关于金融机构实施的财务支持安排所涉及会计影响的进一步讨论，参见FAQ 42.97.4。
FAQ 17.2.3 – 主体应如何对支持企业弥补收入损失的纾困计划进行会计处理？
准则索引：IAS 20 第3段
政府提供一项纾困计划，以支持企业弥补收入损失。
主体应如何对该纾困计划进行会计处理？
主体应首先评估政府提供的纾困是否符合政府补助的定义[IAS 20 第3段]。政府补助应在主体将补助拟补偿的相关成本确认为费用的各期间内，按系统的方法计入利润表。与收益相关的补助有时在损益表中作为贷项列报，既可以单独列报，也可以归入“其他收益”等一般项目下列报；或者，也可以在报告相关费用时予以冲减。[IAS 20 第29段]
政府补助不符合客户合同收入的定义。[IFRS 15 第6段] 它们也不符合租赁收入的定义。[IFRS 16 第81段]。IAS 20 中的冲减选项是在将补助收益从相关费用中扣除、从而列示主体承担的净费用的背景下制定的。将这种方法类推适用于旨在弥补收入损失的补助是不可接受的，因为这会导致补助收益被不当分类（例如，分类为客户合同收入或租赁收入）。
然而，主体将用于弥补收入损失的补助列报在“其他收益”、“其他收入”或“补助收入”中是可以接受的。以下列报替代方案可能是恰当的：
- 主体可以将这些补助在营业利润内的收入项目之外列报为“其他收益”，即在采用总额法时列报其他政府补助收益的位置。

- 主体也可以认为该补助符合更广义的收入定义，因此将其列报在更广义的收入类别中。这是因为 IFRS 15 将收入定义为主体在日常活动中产生的收益。因此，如果主体因在日常经营活动中提供商品/服务而遭受收入损失并因此有权获得该补助，将该补助列报在总收入中可能是可接受的。如果该补助在利润表中作为总收入的一部分列报，则应将其与 IFRS 15 范围内的客户合同收入以及 IFRS 16 范围内的租赁收入分开列报。[IAS 20 第29段]。这种单独列报可通过对总收入的不同组成部分进行分解来实现。
无论采用哪种方式，主体都应就所遵循的列报方法制定明确的会计政策。
FAQ 17.9.1 – 主体应如何识别一项补助拟补偿的相关费用？
准则索引：IAS 20 第17段 正文索引：17.9
当补助条款未指明其拟资助的具体支出时，识别补助拟补偿的相关费用可能会面临困难。在实务中，补助可能被授予用于支付同时包含收益性支出和资本性支出的项目成本。例如，项目补助可能既与项目的资本性支出成本相关，又与创造或保留的就业岗位数量相关。在此类情况下，符合补助资助条件的支出可能是该项目直接归属的所有已发生成本。通常需要仔细审视补助条款本身，以判断其意图是支付成本，还是对补助的全部金额设定一项条件。
示例 − 与资产相关的补助还是与收益相关的补助？
某主体就一项投资项目从工业发展机构获得一项补助。该项目是建造一座用于容纳制造工厂的建筑物。主要条款为：补助付款与资本性支出水平挂钩，补助的目的是帮助确保进口产品可由本国生产的产品替代，并保留500个就业岗位。如果资本性支出不足，或者在最后一次购置固定资产之日起18个月内未能保留这些就业岗位，则必须退还该补助。这是与资产相关的补助还是与收益相关的补助？
该补助与资本性支出相关。因此，根据 IAS 20，它属于与资产相关的补助。就业条件应被视为防止以资本替代劳动力的附加条件，而非授予该补助的原因。如果该补助属于与收益相关的补助，则其应与收益性支出挂钩，例如工资成本的一定比例或每个保留就业岗位的固定金额。
FAQ 17.9.2 – 补助应如何分摊至已识别的支出？
准则索引：IAS 20 第17段 正文索引：17.9
有时，补助拟补偿的实际支出可能与构成其付款基础的支出不同。例如，补助可能与项目总支出相关，除资本性支出外，项目总支出还可能包括营运资金成本、培训成本和搬迁成本。然而，随着项目推进，该补助可能在发生特定金额的资本性支出时分期成为应收款项。主体应如何对此类差异进行会计处理？
将全部补助仅分摊至资本性支出是不恰当的。因此，最恰当的处理方法是将收到的补助按比例分摊至补助拟补偿的各项支出。这样，补助就会按比例分摊至项目支出的各个组成部分。这恰当地将补助的一部分按一种基础分摊，而将另一部分按另一种基础分摊。因此，当存在充分且具说服力的证据表明补助附带一组条件时，将收到的补助分摊至补助拟补偿的已识别支出是恰当的。
FAQ 17.9.3 – 达成非财务目标后应支付的补助应如何进行会计处理？
准则索引：IAS 20 第17段 正文索引：17.9
补助可能基于不同的基础成为应收款项——例如，在达成某项非财务目标时。该补助应当旨在补偿达成该目标的可识别成本。此类成本必须以合理的基础进行识别或估计。例如，如果支持新产品制造的补助以创造并维持就业岗位达到最短期限为条件，则该补助应在将提供这些就业岗位的成本确认为费用的期间内予以确认。由于补助拟补偿的早期非生产性成本和筹建成本较高，较大比例的补助可能需要在项目早期阶段予以确认。
主体A获得一项金额为 C60,000 的政府补助，分三年收取（第1年 C40,000，第2年和第3年各 C10,000），条件是创造10个新就业岗位并维持三年。招聘员工的总成本为 C30,000，第一年的工资总额为 C100,000，此后每年增加 C10,000。该政府补助应如何进行会计处理？
C60,000 的收益应在三年期间内确认，以补偿相关成本。在第1年，从政府收到的 C40,000 中有 C21,667 用于补偿当年发生的 C130,000 相关成本，因此应确认为收益。尚未计入收益的补助金额（即 C18,333，为收到的现金 C40,000 减去计入收益的 C21,667）在资产负债表中列示。
FAQ 17.10.1 – 主体应如何对无条件补助进行会计处理？
准则索引：IAS 20 第10段 正文索引：17.10
主体A在20X1年5月至20X1年9月期间发生了与员工培训相关的费用 C5,000。该员工培训为政府要求。主体A于20X1年12月与政府就已发生的培训费用补偿事宜展开谈判。20X2年2月，政府同意就主体截至20X1年12月31日止年度发生的该项费用予以补偿。该无条件补助应如何进行会计处理？
尽管主体A是在截至20X1年12月31日止年度发生该费用，但其应在截至20X2年12月31日止年度确认从政府收到的收益。该项 C5,000 的补助仅在20X2年2月政府同意就培训费用向主体A提供补偿时才成为应收款项。
FAQ 17.14.1 – 与资产相关的补助应如何进行会计处理？
准则索引：IAS 20 第24段 正文索引：17.14
主体A于20X6年1月1日获得一项金额为 C100,000 的政府补助，用于建造一座制造工厂。该工厂的预计使用寿命为10年。主体耗时两年建成该工厂。20X9年1月1日，主体开始使用该工厂生产产品。该主体的会计年度截止日为12月31日。主体应如何对该补助进行会计处理？
该项 C100,000 的补助与资产的建造相关，初始应确认为递延收益。
递延收益应在该资产的使用寿命内按系统、合理的基础确认为收益。
主体应在截至20X7年12月31日和20X8年12月31日止年度的资产负债表中确认一项负债。一旦该工厂开始用于生产过程，应在资产10年使用寿命内的每一年确认其他营业收益 C10,000，以补偿折旧成本。
根据 IAS 20 允许的替代处理方法，主体A也可以在20X9年1月1日将 C100,000 的递延收益冲减工厂成本。
FAQ 17.14.2 – 当相关资产因减值而被减记时，与资产相关的补助应如何进行会计处理？
准则索引：IAS 20 第24段 正文索引：17.13
某主体多年前在政府补助的资助下建造了一座工厂。该补助无需偿还，且在工厂建成后政府不得追回。该补助未附带主体需要满足的进一步条件。收到的补助已作为递延收益处理，并在工厂计提折旧的同一期间内计入利润表。由于该工厂所服务的业务线发生不利变化，董事们认为该工厂的账面价值已无法全额收回，需要进行减值减记。该减记金额完全被与该补助相关的未摊销递延收益余额所覆盖。主体应如何对该补助进行会计处理？
与资产相关的政府补助（包括按公允价值计量的非货币性补助），在资产负债表中应当通过将补助确认为递延收益，或者通过将补助冲减资产账面价值的方式予以列报。[IAS 20 第12段]。政府补助应在主体将补助拟补偿的相关成本确认为费用的各期间内，按系统的方法确认为收益。无论补助采用净额法还是递延收益法，在利润表中的结果应当相同。
如果该补助在初始时已冲减工厂的购置成本，且冲减后的净账面价值低于可收回金额，则无需进行减值减记。利润表将按净购置成本计提年度折旧。
如果该补助一直作为递延收益列示，且资产初始按总成本入账，则通过将一定金额的递延收益转入利润表以补偿减值减记，从而实现相同的结果是合理的。如果该补助除建造工厂之外还附带进一步条件，则将一定金额的递延收益转入利润表以补偿减值减记可能并不恰当。主体需要评估这些进一步条件，以确定应当转入利润表的递延收益金额（如有）。
在主体选择类推适用 IAS 20 指引的投资税收抵免情形下，上述会计处理也会有所不同。（参见第14章第7段。）

Introduction and scope (paras 21.1 - 21.8)
21.1 This chapter addresses the IFRS requirements for intangible assets as follows:
- Initial recognition of intangible assets.
- Initial measurement of intangible assets.
- Measurement subsequent to initial recognition, including the cost and revaluation models.
Impairment of intangible assets is addressed by IAS 36 (see chapter 24 para 3). Fair value is addressed in IFRS 13 (see chapter 5 para 8).
21.2 Initial recognition and measurement, subsequent measurement (including revaluation, depreciation and impairment), derecognition and disclosure requirements are addressed in IAS 38.

21.3 Borrowing costs directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of a qualifying asset form part of the cost of this asset. [IAS 23 para 1]. Intangible assets could be qualifying assets in some circumstances (see chapter 22 para 45).
21.4 An intangible asset is defined as “an identifiable non-monetary asset without physical substance”.
21.5 The standard does not apply to:

- Intangible assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business, such as inventories under IAS 2 (see chapter 25 para 2) and assets from contracts with customers that are recognised in accordance with IFRS 15 (see chapter 11).
- Deferred tax assets under IAS 12 (see chapter 14 para 4).
- Assets arising from leases within the scope of IFRS 16 (see chapter 15 para 3 or for IAS 17 see chapter 15A para 2).
- Assets arising from employee benefits under IAS 19 (see chapter 12 para 3).
- Goodwill arising from a business combination under IFRS 3 (see chapter 29 para 26).

- Deferred acquisition costs and intangible assets arising from an insurer‘s contractual rights under insurance contracts that are within the scope of IFRS 4 (see chapter 50 para 3). Deferred acquisition costs that are not within the scope of IFRS 4 are in the scope of IAS 38. The IAS 38 disclosure requirements apply to all such intangible assets.
- Intangible assets classified as held-for-sale in accordance with IFRS 5 (see chapter 30 para 9).
- Financial assets as defined in IAS 32 (see chapter 40 para 8).

- Exploration and evaluation assets under IFRS 6 and expenditure on the development and extraction of minerals, oil, natural gas and similar non-regenerative resources. The recognition criteria in IAS 38 for internally generated costs will need to be applied once the technical feasibility and commercial viability of extracting the non-regenerative resource has been determined (the development phase). [IFRS 6 para 10].
[IAS 38 para 2]. [IAS 38 para 3].

21.6 Expenditure on advertising, training, start-up and research and development (R&D) are within the scope of IAS 38. R&D activities are directed to the development of knowledge. These activities might result in a physical asset, but the physical element of the asset is secondary to its intangible element. Development expenditure might result, in some circumstances, in the creation of an intangible asset (see para 21.30).

21.7 The underlying asset in a lease might be intangible in nature. An intangible asset in a lease transaction might be accounted for under IFRS 16, depending on the type of intangible asset and whether the entity is the lessee or the lessor. For more details see chapter 15 para 3.

21.8 Rights held by a lessee under licensing agreements for items such as films, videos, plays, manuscripts, patents and copyrights are within the scope of IAS 38 and are excluded from the scope of IAS 17/IFRS 16.

Recognition (paras 21.9 - 21.40)

21.9 An item should be recognised in the financial statements as an intangible asset if it meets the definition of an intangible asset (see para 21.4) and it meets the recognition criteria (see para 21.16).
21.10 The key characteristics of an intangible asset are that it:
- is a resource controlled by the entity from which the entity expects to derive future economic benefits;
- lacks physical substance; and
- is identifiable to be distinguished from goodwill.

21.11 An entity controls an asset if it has the power to obtain the future economic benefits from an underlying resource and to restrict the access of others to those benefits. Control is usually evidenced by legally enforceable contractual or other rights, such as legal title or a licence. It is more challenging to demonstrate control in the absence of legal rights. 21.12 An entity usually has insufficient control over the expected future economic benefits derived from its workforce for the workforce to be recognised as an intangible asset.
EX 21.12.1 – Sign-up bonuses paid to new employees
21.13 Future economic benefits might include revenue from the sale of goods or the provision of services, cost savings, or other benefits derived by the entity from the use of the asset.

21.14 Some intangible assets might be contained in or on a physical substance, such as on a compact disc (computer software) or in legal documentation (licence or patent). The physical and non-physical elements might be incapable of separation in these instances, and judgement is required to determine which element is the more significant. The asset should be treated as an intangible asset if the intangible element is the more significant.
EX 21.14.1 – Categorising an asset as tangible or intangible
21.15 An intangible asset is identifiable when it:

- is separable (that is, it is capable of being separated or divided from the entity and sold, transferred, licensed, rented or exchanged, either individually or together with a related contract, asset or liability); or
- arises from contractual or other legal rights, regardless of whether the rights are transferable or separable from the entity or from other rights and obligations.

21.16 The recognition criteria for an intangible asset are:
- it is probable that the expected future economic benefits that are attributable to the asset will flow to the entity; and
- the cost of the asset can be measured reliably.

21.17 An entity should assess the probability of expected future economic benefits using reasonable and supportable assumptions. These assumptions should represent management’s best estimate of the set of economic conditions that will exist over the asset’s useful life. [IAS 38 para 22]. In assessing future economic benefits the entity could use cash flow models. See chapter 5.

21.18 Judgement is required in assessing the degree of certainty to attach to the flow of economic benefits expected from the asset’s use based on evidence available at the date of initial recognition. Management should place greater reliance on external evidence.
EX 21.18.1 – External evidence
21.19 If the asset will generate economic benefits only when combined with other assets, the IAS 36 concept of cash generating units should be applied.
21.20 An entity might obtain an intangible asset in a number of ways:
- by separate acquisition for monetary or other consideration;
- as part of a business combination;
- by exchange for other non-monetary assets;
- by way of government grant; or
- by developing or generating the asset internally.

The criteria for recognition are applied differently in each of these situations. The extent and reliability of the evidence available to the entity, in determining whether the criteria are met, vary depending on which situation is involved. For example, in each of the first three situations listed above, there is an exchange transaction, which gives evidence that economic benefits are likely to flow to the entity.
Applying recognition criteria to externally acquired assets

21.21 The probability recognition criterion is always assumed to be met for separately acquired intangible assets. The price paid reflects expectations about the probability that the future economic benefits of the asset will flow to the entity. The greater the price paid, the higher the expectations of future economic benefits to be derived from the asset. [IAS 38 para 25]. A business combination is an exchange transaction. Internally generated intangible assets
21.22 It might be challenging to determine whether an internally generated intangible asset qualifies for recognition because:
- there is uncertainty that the intangible asset will generate expected future economic benefits; and

- it might not be possible to determine the asset’s cost reliably or distinguish the costs attributable to such an asset from costs of maintaining or increasing the entity’s internally generated goodwill or the costs of carrying out the entity’s day-to-day operations.

EX 21.22.1 – Research and development costs that cannot be attributed to a specific product EX 21.22.2 – Reliable measurement criterion for customer lists developed internally and customer lists acquired as part of a business combination
21.23 The process of generating an intangible asset is divided into a research phase and a development phase.
21.24 If the two phases are indistinguishable, all the expenditure on the asset should be attributed to the research phase.

21.25 ‘Research’ is defined as “… original and planned investigation undertaken with the prospect of gaining new scientific or technical knowledge and understanding”. ‘Development’ is defined as “… the application of research findings or other knowledge to a plan or design for the production of new or substantially improved materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services before the start of commercial production or use”.
21.26 Examples of research activities include:
- Activities aimed at obtaining new knowledge.
- Searching for suitable applications of research findings or other knowledge, evaluating the applications and making a final selection of suitable applications.
- Searching for alternatives for materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services.
EX 21.26.1 – Research activities

21.27 Expenditure on the research phase of an internal project should be expensed as incurred. No intangible asset arising from research, or from the research phase of an internal project, can be recognised.

21.28 An entity is unable to demonstrate that there will be future economic benefits during the research phase. The absence of probability of future economic benefits means that the expenditure does not meet the definition of an intangible asset, nor does it meet the criteria for recognition.
EX 21.28.1 – Intangible assets used in a research and development project
21.29 Research projects that are acquired as part of a business combination are treated differently. [IAS 38 para 34]. In such cases, an asset will usually be recognised. See paragraph 21.40.
EX 21.29.1 – Research project acquired in a business combination
21.30 Examples of development activities include:
- Designing, constructing and testing pre-production or pre-use prototypes and models.
- Designing tools, jigs, moulds and dies involving new technology.
- Designing, constructing and operating a pilot plant that is not of a scale that is economically capable of commercial production.
- Designing, constructing and testing a selected alternative for new or improved materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services.

21.31 The future economic benefits might become more apparent as a project progresses into the development stage. The development phase of a project is more advanced than the research phase. An entity can, in some instances, identify an intangible asset in the development phase.
EX 21.31.1 – Unit of account for capitalisation of research and development expenses
21.32 An intangible asset arising from development, or from the development phase of an internal project, should be recognised if an entity can demonstrate all of the following:
- The technical feasibility of completing the intangible asset so that it will be available for use or sale.
- Its intention to complete the intangible asset and use or sell it.
- Its ability to use the intangible asset or to sell it.

- The way in which the intangible asset will generate probable future economic benefits. Among other factors, the entity must be able to demonstrate the existence of a market for the intangible asset’s output or for the intangible asset itself; or, if the asset is to be used internally, it must be able to demonstrate the usefulness of the intangible asset.
- The availability of adequate technical, financial and other resources to complete the development and to use or sell the intangible asset.
- Its ability to measure reliably the expenditure attributable to the intangible asset during its development.

Expenditure which cannot be capitalised as internally generated intangible assets

21.34 The criteria for recognising internally generated intangible assets cannot be satisfied for some types of intangible asset. These include internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists and items that are similar in substance. It is extremely difficult to distinguish the costs of such items from the costs of developing the business as a whole. The standard prohibits recognition of those items as intangible assets.

- Start-up costs, unless such costs are included in the cost of a tangible fixed asset under IAS 16. - Advertising and promotion costs, including mail order catalogues.

Assets acquired in a business combination
21.37 An acquirer recognises an intangible asset of the aquiree, irrespective of whether the asset had been recognised by the acquiree before the business combination.

21.38 It is always assumed that the probability recognition criterion is met for intangible assets acquired in a business combination. The fair value of an intangible asset reflects market participants’ expectations at the acquisition date about the probability that the expected future economic benefits embodied in the asset will flow to the entity.

21.39 The reliable measurement criterion will always be met for intangible assets acquired in a business combination (see para 21.39). If an asset acquired is separable or arises from contractual rights, sufficient information exists to reliably measure the fair value of the asset.
21.40 An in-process research and development project of the acquiree should be recognised if the project:
- meets the definition of an asset; and
- is identifiable (that is, it is separable or arises from contractual or other legal rights).

What are CC costs in a cloud computing arrangement?

21.40.2 Many entities will pay a fee for the SaaS arrangement and an additional amount to configure and/or customise those services to their own specific requirements in advance of receiving the services. For example, an entity might have a SaaS arrangement for a human resources system but want to customise it to create additional reporting functionalities. As part of the discussion papers which led to the agenda decision, the IASB staff defined

(i) Configuration: Typical configuration relates to the setting of various ‘flags’ or ‘switches’ within the software, or defining certain values or parameters, to implement a particular set-up for the software’s existing functionality. Configuration does not involve the modification or writing of additional software code, but rather involves setting up the software’s existing code to function in a particular way for the entity’s benefit.

(ii) Customisation: Typical customisation involves modifying existing software code in the application or writing additional code. The effect of significantly altering or adding software code is generally to change, or create additional, functionalities within the software so that it can provide the intended benefits.
The CC might be performed by the customer themselves, the SaaS provider, or a third party and is often a substantial cost in relation to the total cost of the SaaS arrangement.

According to IFRS 15, a good or service that is promised to a customer is distinct if:

- the customer can benefit from the good or service, either on its own or together with other resources that are readily available to the customer (that is, the good or service is capable of being distinct); and

- the entity’s promise to transfer the good or service to the customer is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract (that is, the promise to transfer the good or service is distinct within the context of the contract).
Therefore, the assessment of whether a good or service is distinct has two elements; the good or service must be both: (a) capable of being distinct; and (b) separately identifiable.

Initial measurement (21.41 - 21.71)
21.41 Intangible assets should be measured on initial recognition at cost.

21.42 Cost is defined as the amount of cash or cash equivalents paid, or the fair value of other consideration given, to acquire an asset at the time of its acquisition or construction. Alternatively, where applicable, cost is the amount attributed to that asset when initially recognised in accordance with the specific requirements of other IFRSs, such as IFRS 2.
Measurement of separately acquired intangible assets

21.43 The cost of a separately acquired intangible asset (including in-process research and development projects) can usually be reliably measured. This is particularly so for assets acquired for cash.
21.44 The cost of a separately acquired intangible asset comprises:
- the purchase price, including import duties and non-refundable purchase taxes, after deducting trade discounts and rebates; and
- any directly attributable cost of preparing the asset for its intended use.
21.45 Directly attributable costs include, but are not limited to:
- The cost of employee benefits, as defined in IAS 19, that arise directly from bringing the asset into its working condition (see para 21.63).
- Costs of testing whether the asset is working properly.
FAQ 21.45.1 – Is the guidance on directly attributable costs applicable to separately acquired assets?
21.46 Expenditures that are not part of the cost of an intangible asset include:
- The cost of introducing a new product or service, including advertising costs and promotional activities.
- Costs of conducting business in a new location or with a new class of customer, including training costs.
- Administration and other general overheads.

21.47 Capitalisation of eligible costs should cease when the asset is capable of operating in the manner intended by management. Costs of using the asset or for redeploying it to other uses or another location are not capitalised. Such costs include any that are incurred while an asset is capable of operating in the manner intended by management and any initial operating losses, such as those that might be incurred while demand builds up for the

Assets acquired in exchange for non-monetary assets
21.54 An intangible asset acquired in exchange for a non-monetary asset, or for a combination of non-monetary and monetary assets, should be recognised initially at its fair value, unless:
- the exchange transaction has no commercial substance; or
- the fair value of neither the asset received nor the asset given up can be reliably measured.

21.55 The decision as to whether a transaction has commercial substance depends on the extent to which the entity’s future cash flows are expected to change as a result of the transaction. ‘Configuration of the cash flows’ means the risk, timing and amount of the cash flows. An exchange transaction has commercial substance if:
- the configuration of the cash flows of the asset received differs from the configuration of the cash flows of the asset given up; or
- the entity-specific value of the part of the entity’s operations affected by the transaction changes as a result of the exchange,
and the difference in either case is significant relative to the fair value of the assets exchanged.

21.58 The absence of market transactions does not mean fair value cannot be established. The fair value of either the asset given up or the asset received can still be reliably measured if:
- the range of reasonable estimates of fair value does not vary significantly (that is, the range is reasonably narrow); or
- the range of reasonable estimates is not narrow, but the probabilities of the various estimates within the range can be reasonably assessed and used in estimating fair values.

Where both the fair value of the asset given up and the fair value of the asset received can be estimated with equal reliability, the fair value of the asset given up is used to measure the cost of the asset received.

Measurement of internally generated intangible assets

21.61 The cost of an internally generated intangible asset that meets the recognition criteria is the sum of directly attributable expenditure incurred to create, produce and prepare the asset so that it is capable of operating in the manner intended by management.
21.62 Examples of directly attributable costs are:
- Costs of materials and services used or consumed in generating the intangible asset.
- Cost of employee benefits (as defined in IAS 19) that arise directly from the generation of the asset.
- Fees paid to register a legal right, such as patent registration fees.
- Amortisation of patents and licences that are used in generating the asset.
- Borrowing costs, to the extent that they are eligible for capitalisation as part of the cost. Borrowing costs are dealt with by IAS 23 (see chapter 22 para 42).

Introduction to the cost model and the revaluation model

21.74 An entity can adopt either the cost model or the revaluation model as its accounting policy after initial recognition. The revaluation model can only be adopted if the intangible assets are traded in an active market, so it is not frequently used. The policy should be applied to the whole of a class of intangible assets and not merely to individual assets within a class, unless there is no active market for an individual asset.
21.75 The cost model requires that, after initial recognition, intangible assets should be carried at cost less accumulated amortisation and impairment losses.

21.76 The revaluation model requires that, after initial recognition, intangible assets should be carried at fair value, determined by reference to an active market. Revaluations should be carried out with sufficient regularity that the carrying amount of the asset does not differ materially from that which would be determined using fair value at the balance sheet date.
Classes of intangible assets
21.77 An entity can adopt classes of assets that meet the following definition: “A grouping of assets of a similar nature and use in an entity’s operations”.

21.78 Other than ruling out classes of assets determined on a geographical basis, this definition is reasonably flexible. An entity can adopt meaningful classes that are appropriate to its business. Most companies have a few broadly drawn classes of intangible assets. Examples of classes of intangible assets are:
- Mastheads and publishing titles.
- Licences and franchises.
- Copyrights, patents and other industrial property rights, service and operating rights.
- Recipes, formulae, models, designs and prototypes.
- Intangible assets under development.

21.87 Valuations should remain up to date to be meaningful. Revaluations should be made with sufficient regularity that the carrying amount does not differ materially from fair value at the balance sheet date.

Treatment of accumulated amortisation under revaluation model
21.89 The carrying amount of an asset is adjusted to the revalued amount when this intangible asset is revalued. The asset is treated in one of the following ways at the date of the revaluation:

- The gross carrying amount is adjusted in a manner that is consistent with the revaluation of the carrying amount of the asset (for example, the gross carrying amount might be restated by reference to observable market data, or it might be restated proportionately to the change in the carrying amount). The accumulated amortisation at the date of the revaluation is adjusted to equal the difference between the gross carrying amount and the carryin
- The accumulated amortisation is eliminated against the gross carrying amount of the asset.
21.90 The amount of the adjustment of accumulated amortisation forms part of the increase or decrease in the carrying amount that is accounted for as part of the gain or loss on revaluation.

21.91 A revaluation increase should be recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity under the heading of revaluation surplus, unless it reverses a revaluation decrease on the same asset previously recognised as an expense. Reversals of previous revaluation decreases are credited to profit or loss to the extent that the decrease was recognised as an expense.
21.92 The revaluation surplus included in equity can be transferred directly to retained earnings when the surplus is realised (where the asset is retired or disposed of).

21.93 Some of the surplus can also be transferred directly to retained earnings as the asset is used by the entity (that is, as the surplus is realised). The amount transferred is the difference between amortisation based on the revalued carrying amount of the asset and amortisation based on the asset’s original cost. This amount can be transferred directly from revaluation surplus to retained earnings (reserves transfer).

21.94 A revaluation decrease should be recognised in profit or loss. If there is a credit balance in the revaluation surplus on the same asset, the decrease should be recognised in other comprehensive income. The decrease in other comprehensive income also decreases the amount accumulated in equity under the heading of revaluation reserve.

21.95 Amortisation is defined as “the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an intangible asset over its useful life”. The depreciable amount is defined as the asset’s “cost, or other amount substituted for cost, less its residual value”.
21.96 Amortisation applies to all intangible assets, whether held at cost or fair value, except intangible assets with indefinite useful lives.

21.97 Amortisation should begin as soon as an asset is available for use – that is, when it is in the location and condition necessary for it to be capable of operating in the manner intended by management.

Derecognition of intangible assets is discussed at paragraph 21.134 onwards. An intangible asset is classified as held for sale in accordance with IFRS 5 when it meets the conditions in that standard for such classification (see chapter 30 para 10).
21.99 Amortisation does not stop when an asset is retained but no longer used, unless it has been fully amortised or classified as held for sale under IFRS 5.
21.100 An intangible asset with an indefinite useful life should not be amortised.
Useful lives – finite and indefinite
21.101 Useful life is defined as:
- the period over which an asset is expected to be available for use by an entity; or
- the number of production or similar units expected to be obtained from the asset by an entity.
FAQ 21.101.1 – What periods are covered by useful life?

21.102 Management should assess whether an intangible asset’s useful life is finite or indefinite. An intangible asset should be regarded as having an indefinite useful life if, based on all the relevant factors, there is no foreseeable limit to the period over which the asset is expected to generate net cash inflows for the entity.
21.103 IAS 38 contains guidance on factors to be taken into account when estimating useful lives, which includes:
- Expected usage by the entity of the asset and whether it could be managed efficiently by another management team.
- The typical product life cycle for the asset and published information about useful lives of similar assets that are used in a similar way.
- Technical, technological, commercial or other types of obsolescence.
- The stability of the industry in which the asset operates, and changes in market demand for the products or services from or related to the asset.
- Expected actions by actual or potential competitors.
- The level of maintenance required to maintain the asset’s operating capability, and whether management intends to perform that level of maintenance.
- The period for which the entity has control of the asset and any legal or similar limits on the asset’s use.
- Whether the asset’s useful life is dependent on the useful life of other assets of the entity.

- Investigate competitors’ use of other technologies.

- Send the shortlist to line managers for input and list three alternatives based on feedback.
- Present the final three to the board for final selection.
- Finalise a development plan for the final selection.
- Develop new technology.
- Train staff on new technology.
- Roll out new technology to the production line.
