text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第15、22段，IAS 37 第14段 参考正文：30.29

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 就处置组确认的减值损失应冲减处置组内属于其计量要求范围的非流动资产的账面金额。当公允价值减去出售费用后的净额为负数时，适用 IFRS 5 不会导致确认一项负债，因为处置组内资产的账面金额不能减记至低于零。是否确认预计负债应由 IAS 37 的指引决定。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.31.1 – 资产负债表日后出售谈判破裂

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第26段 参考正文：30.31

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某会计年度止于12月的主体于10月决定出售其一家子公司。董事会开始积极推销该子公司并与潜在买方谈判。截至12月31日，管理层认为该出售极有可能在12个月内完成。然而，到了2月，谈判破裂，该主体决定对该子公司进行清算而非出售。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 该子公司在年末符合划分为持有待售的条件。年末后决定清算该公司的事项并不影响年末时业已存在的状况，管理层在划分资产和负债时不应使用后见之明。然而，2月之后持有待售分类将不再适用，在后续期间，该子公司应重分类为持有并使用。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: FAQ 30.31.2 – 后续应如何评估一年期限条件？

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第26、27段 参考正文：30.31

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在每个评估日重新评估资产或处置组是否满足“持有待售”条件，并非将其视为在该评估日新近符合条件（即评估该资产是否将在该日起一年内售出），而是指重新评估初始划分为持有待售之日所适用的期限。准则提供了一定的灵活性以适应情况变化。在特定情形下，准则允许延长“预期自划分为持有待售之日起一年内完成出售”的条件，并允许该资产保留其持有待售分类。详见第30.15段。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.36.1 – IASB 与 IFRS IC 关于子公司、联营企业和合营企业追溯重述的讨论

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第28段 参考正文：30.36

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 国际财务报告准则解释委员会（IFRS IC）收到一项请求，要求澄清如何应用 IFRS 5 第28段的列报要求。第28段要求，非流动资产（在终止划分为持有待售时）重新计量的影响应在当期损益中确认。第28段还要求，如果终止划分为持有待售或持有待向所有者分配的处置组或非流动资产是子公司、共同经营、合营企业、联营企业，或在合营企业或联营企业中的部分权益，则应“相应修订”自划分为持有待售或持有待向所有者分配以来的各期财务报表。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 第一个问题涉及：就涉及子公司、共同经营、合营企业、联营企业或在合营企业或联营企业中部分权益的出售计划变更而言，追溯修订（如 IFRS 5 第28段所要求）是仅适用于计量，还是同时适用于列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 解释委员会注意到，当出售计划发生变更时，IFRS 5 的要求并未明确第28段中的“相应修订”一词是仅指计量，还是同时指列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 第二个问题涉及这样一种情形：同时包含子公司和其他非流动资产的处置组终止划分为持有待售。在此情形下，主体是否应在不同的会计期间确认与子公司和其他非流动资产相关的重新计量调整，以及任何修订是否应同时适用于列报和计量？

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 解释委员会指出，第28段的要求存在不一致之处；原因在于，当出售计划发生变更时，IFRS 5 第28段要求对属于子公司、共同经营、合营企业、联营企业或在合营企业或联营企业中部分权益的处置组的重新计量影响进行追溯确认，而对非流动资产的重新计量影响则要求在当期确认。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 鉴于存在大量且多样的未决问题，解释委员会得出结论认为，可能有必要就 IFRS 5 开展一项广泛范围的项目。因此，解释委员会决定不将该问题纳入其议程。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 5 的列报与披露

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.1 – 关闭单家零售门店

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体 B 是一家外卖食品零售商。其决定出售位于法国的一家名为“C”的门店。主体 B 将继续在法国经营其他 500 家门店。IFRS 5 关于划分为持有待售的所有条件于 20X7年5月23日首次得到满足。C 门店将于 20X7年9月售出。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 管理层认为 C 门店属于一项终止经营，并希望将 C 门店的经营成果列报为“终止经营”。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 尽管 C 门店是一个处置组，但它不属于终止经营，因为它仅是一家门店，既不代表一项独立的主要业务或一个主要经营地区，也不是专为转售而取得的子公司。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.2 – 终止经营的时点

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 为了满足“终止”的定义，某项经营活动必须（截至特定报告日）已经被处置，或者在该时点被划分为持有待售。这意味着必须满足 IFRS 5 第6至第9段规定的划分为持有待售的条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 根据 IFRS 5，拟终止或关闭而非出售的经营活动，在主体作出关闭决定时并不符合终止经营条件。由于该经营活动不会主要通过出售收回，因此不满足“持有待售”条件。然而，许多经营活动一旦实际关闭，即符合列报为终止经营的条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 5 第13段规定，如果某处置组符合终止经营条件，则应在该处置组停止使用之日将其现金流量和经营成果列报为终止经营。在许多情形下，确定某项经营活动何时“停止使用”非常明确，因为所有收入来源和成本均已终止，且所有资产均已处置；但是，根据具体事实和情况，这也可能是一个需要判断的领域。例如，尽管所有创收活动可能均已停止，但可能仍有收尾成本尚待发生，且仍有资产尚待出售或报废。在这些情形下，有必要考虑尚待发生的成本（以及在适用情况下尚待收取的款项）的性质，并判断其是否构成一项经营活动。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.3 – 关闭药品批发业务

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某公司开展药品批发业务，在全国各地通过若干租赁物业运营。该业务已经关闭，所有存货均已处置，员工也在下一财务年度开始后三个月届满前被裁减。截至该时点，仍有一些应收账款尚待收回，且在租约处置前，就腾空的物业仍将继续发生成本。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在本例中，原先的药品批发活动已经停止。尚未结清的未来交易不构成该活动的延续，因此，该经营活动已终止。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.4 – 关闭工程承包分部

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某集团宣布正在关闭一个工程承包分部。尽管不再承接新合同，但所有现有合同都将履行完毕，业务亦将随之逐步缩减。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在此情形下，当承包活动完成之时（即最后一份合同结束之时），该经营活动才停止使用。在完成现有合同期间，尽管该活动正在逐步缩减，但集团仍在继续开展创收活动，因此该分部不符合终止经营条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.5 – 关闭贷款业务

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某集团正在关闭其贷款业务。该业务不再发放新贷款，但将继续收回未偿还贷款的本金和利息，直至原定期限届满。该业务何时应划分为终止经营？

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在收回最后一笔利息款项之前，该业务不能划分为终止经营，因为这才是创收活动停止的时点。这与 EX 30.93.3 形成对比，在那一示例中，尽管尚有未收回应收账款，该业务仍可划分为终止经营。两者的区别在于，在 EX 30.93.3 中，剩余活动仅是单纯的现金催收工作，并未产生重大利息收入。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.6 – 主要业务或主要经营地区

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 终止经营的“规模”定义与 IFRS 5 的前身准则 IAS 35 中的定义一致。IFRS 5 未纳入 IAS 35 中关于终止经营定义的详细阐述，但这些阐述仍然是有用的指引。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IAS 35 指出，IAS 14 所定义的独立业务分部或主要地区分部通常满足“终止经营应代表一项主要业务或一个主要经营地区”的条件。（IAS 35 使用了“正在终止（discontinuing）”一词，但时态的变化仅涉及分类的时点，因此在考量经营规模时该指引仍具有参考价值。）然而，IAS 35 进一步指出，IAS 14 所定义的业务分部或地区分部的一部分，也可能满足构成主要业务或主要经营地区的条件。若主体仅在单一业务分部或单一主要地区分部经营，因而不报告分部信息，则主要产品线或服务线也可能满足该条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IAS 14 允许将实质上相似的业务分部或地区分部合并为单一的报告业务分部或地区分部。根据 IFRS 8，报告分部可能包含多个经营分部。因此，在 IAS 14 下报告的单一业务分部或地区分部，或在 IFRS 8 下的单一报告分部，实际上可能由若干实质上相似的分部组成。终止其中一个相似分部似乎符合终止经营的定义。请注意，IFRS 5 中的条件是该组成部分代表一项“独立的（separate）”而非“不同的（different）”主要业务或主要经营地区。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IAS 35 指出，IAS 14 允许但不要求将纵向一体化经营的不同阶段识别为独立的业务分部。IAS 14 给出的示例是，许多国际石油公司将其上游活动（勘探与生产）和下游活动（炼油与销售）作为独立的业务分部进行报告。IFRS 8 同样允许将纵向一体化经营识别为独立的经营分部。IAS 35 指出，此类纵向一体化经营（即示例中的上游或下游活动）可能满足构成一项独立的主要业务或主要经营地区的条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.7 – 正在出售的美国业务

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某主体拥有一个业务分部，并在英国、美国和澳大利亚开展经营。这些经营活动各自代表主体的一个组成部分以及一个主要经营地区。管理层决定出售美国业务，该业务在年内满足了划分为持有待售的条件。尽管业务分部的数量没有发生变化，美国业务仍应在主体财务报表中作为终止经营予以披露。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.8 – 休闲事业部的分项处置

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在分项处置的情形下，需要对处置计划进行分析，以确定分项处置是否应视为单一处置计划。整体经营的不同部分可能在不同时间符合终止经营条件。IFRS 5 要求，如果该组成部分本身并非一项独立的主要业务或主要经营地区，则它必须是“拟处置该项主要业务或主要经营地区的单一协调计划的一部分”。因此，定义中的关键点在于应当存在一项单一计划。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 某集团决定出售其休闲事业部，该事业部由一家酒店集团和一家连锁健身中心组成。销售代理建议分别为酒店和健身中心业务寻找不同的买方，以实现处置收益最大化。尽管预期有两位买方，但酒店和健身中心的处置是相互协调的：若另一项不出售，其中任何一项（酒店或健身中心）的出售都不会推进。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 存在处置该事业部的单一协调计划。因此，交易可能包含多个组成部分的事实并不妨碍将该处置组划分为终止经营。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.9 – 分项处置与终止经营

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在依据单一计划进行分项处置的情形下，不存在一个使整体经营同时符合终止经营条件的单一日期。“终止”定义的第一部分要求该组成部分满足划分为持有待售的条件。在作为更大单一计划一部分的分项处置中，在任何报告日，仅拟出售的整体经营中已满足划分为持有待售条件的部分才属于终止经营。尽管某项主要业务或主要经营地区正在出售中，但在某一资产负债表日，并非其全部内容都会按终止经营进行列报和计量。构成该单一计划组成部分的其他经营活动，可能在未来满足条件时被划分为终止经营。一项单一计划可能持续数年，随着计划推进，不同组成部分陆续满足终止经营条件。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.39.10 – 不符合终止经营定义的其他项目

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 第32段 参考正文：30.39

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 所有终止经营都必须满足相关定义方可作此分类。还有多种其他项目也不符合该定义，此处予以探讨。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体经常出售或关闭工厂、放弃产品或产品线以及裁减员工。通常，此类重组不符合 IFRS 5 中终止经营的定义，尽管它们可能伴随某项终止经营而发生。例如，主体可能宣布一项详细正式计划，出售一项符合准则下终止经营条件的业务。与此同时，管理层可能决定因未来总部职能缩减而裁减总部员工，或者将总部搬迁至更靠近剩余业务的位置。总部裁员或总部搬迁虽然与终止经营相关，但其本身并非终止经营。因此，应将其作为持续经营处理，而不应纳入终止经营。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 仅当该经营活动被处置后，主体将不再有权取得相关收入或不再发生相关费用时，才应将收入和费用分摊至终止经营。相同原则亦适用于资产和负债，但 IFRS 5 对此表述得更为明确：划分为终止经营的金额为拟出售的资产以及拟转移的相关负债。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 费用分摊常见于总部管理费用。例如，集团母公司可能按比例将其总部管理费用分摊至所有子公司。如果某项经营活动被处置，相关的总部管理费用可能不会减少（至少在短期内如此）。所有总部管理费用必须在集团利润表中分摊至持续经营，因为无论是否发生该项处置，集团均会发生这些成本。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体 A 出售一条主要业务线。由于该项出售，主体 A 发生了若干导致费用的成本，若未发生该项处置本可避免这些成本，具体如下：

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 主体 A 与某供应商签有协议，约定在三年内采购最低订购量的个人电脑。由于拟议的处置，主体将不再需要该最低订购量，且必须支付可计量的违约金。买方将使用其他个人电脑供应商，不会承接该合同。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 主体 A 为现拟出售的业务聘请了一名高级管理人员。该候选人放弃了原本稳定的工作，且不愿面临被潜在收购方接管的前景。为解决此顾虑，主体 A 在合同中加入条款，约定若发生控制权变更，将向该管理人员支付补偿金。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 主体 A 与某供应商签有一份包含控制权变更条款的合同。如果涉及该处置组发生控制权变更，主体 A 须向该供应商支付补偿金。该项义务由主体 A 清偿，买方从未成为该安排的一方。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在所有上述情形中，相关成本均由主体 A 承担，且负债不转移给买方。然而，由于这些成本与终止经营相关，因此应在终止经营中列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 尽管这些成本需要在终止经营中列报，但它们并非直接归属于处置本身。因此，它们不被视为“出售费用”，不应计入“公允价值减去出售费用后的净额”的计量中。这些成本应在满足 IAS 37 条件时计提预计负债，而非在满足 IFRS 5 划分为持有待售条件时计提。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体应当披露与终止经营损益相关的所得税费用。然而，持续经营的税务状况可能影响终止经营的税务状况，反之亦然。例如，同一法律主体内持续经营的利润可能被终止经营的亏损所抵销，从而使该主体的纳税义务降低。准则未强制规定应如何分摊此类影响。主体可以选择是否将所得税费用分摊至持续经营，并将所得税收益分摊至终止经营。主体应当选定一项会计政策并一贯应用。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 还可能需要就划分为终止经营的子公司净资产账面金额与该项投资计税基础之间的差额（即外部基础差异——参见第14.124段）确认递延所得税。这是因为由于决定处置该项投资，IAS 12 中关于子公司投资递延所得税的豁免规定不再适用。相关的递延所得税费用或收益通常在利润表中分摊至终止经营，因为该递延所得税与终止经营净资产的变动（例如以前期间的利润）有关。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

text: 在现金流量表中列报相关信息有多种符合 IFRS 5 要求的方式。基本原则是：现金流量表必须列示主体整体的现金流量（包括持续经营和终止经营），并在现金流量表正面或附注中提供与终止经营相关的补充信息。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 若采用此列报方式，现金流量表中的每一项目均应包含持续经营和终止经营两者的现金流量（例如，收到的利息金额将为持续经营与终止经营之和）。将利润调节至经营活动产生的现金时，应同时包含持续经营利润和终止经营利润，以便与利润表中列示的金额核对一致。应当在现金流量表正面或附注中，分别披露归属于终止经营的经营活动、投资活动和筹资活动的现金流量。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 若采用此列报方式，在现金流量表正面上仅应列示持续经营的现金流量（例如，收到的利息金额仅与持续经营活动有关）。来自终止经营的经营活动现金流量应作为单独一行计入经营活动现金流量总额中。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 专为转售而取得的联营企业或合营企业将根据 IFRS 5 构成一个处置组，并适用与其他持有待售的联营企业和合营企业相同的规则。然而，专为转售而取得的联营企业或合营企业可能不属于终止经营。IFRS 5 的定义仅允许专为转售而持有的子公司直接构成终止经营。但是，如果一家重要的联营企业被划分为持有待售，它可能符合一项主要业务或主要经营地区的定义，因此可能符合终止经营条件。

text: 当采用权益法核算的联营企业或合营企业自身拥有一项划分为持有待售的非流动资产或处置组时，我们的观点是，该非流动资产或处置组应保留在该联营企业或合营企业的整体账面金额之内。换言之，不应将该资产从联营企业投资重分类至投资主体的“持有待售资产”行项目中。一旦该等资产或处置组符合划分为持有待售的条件，即在计入投资方或合营方财务报表的金额中按照 IFRS 5 进行计量。

text: 划分为持有待售的联营企业或合营企业权益的列报方式与其他非流动资产或处置组相同。由于该投资的性质，采用权益法核算的投资所列示的单一金额应作为单项净资产列报，而非按资产和负债总额分别列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 就利润表列报而言，我们的观点是：由于联营企业或合营企业权益在划分为持有待售后不再按照 IAS 28 和 IFRS 11 进行会计处理，因此 IFRS 5 下的所有计量和重新计量均应在持续经营中报告，而不作为享有联营企业或合营企业利润份额的一部分。这仅适用于按 IFRS 5 核算之后；在此之前，应按照 IAS 28 和 IFRS 11 进行常规会计处理。在实务中，唯一相关的变动很可能涉及该资产的减值，因此应在利润表的适当行项目中列示，并在具有重要性时按照 IAS 1 单独披露。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 12 要求披露联营企业的汇总财务信息，包括流动资产、长期资产、流动负债、长期负债、收入和费用。如果持有待售的非流动资产或处置组的资产和负债金额相对于主体对联营企业的账面价值而言具有重要性，我们建议将该金额与其他资产和其他负债分开列示。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 12 还要求披露主体在合营安排中所占权益对应的流动资产、长期资产、流动负债、长期负债、收入和费用各自的合计金额。与联营企业类似，我们认为，如果合营安排中非流动资产或处置组的金额具有足够重要性，则应将其与其他流动资产和流动负债分开披露。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 12 第B12段和第B13段要求的披露同时适用于共同经营和合营企业。如果共同经营者拥有持有待售的资产或处置组，由于共同经营财务报表中的分类会穿透反映至共同经营者，因此这些资产或处置组将在共同经营者的财务报表中按照 IFRS 5 进行分类。不过，仍需进行单独披露。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 第一种可行方法遵循 IFRS 5 第23段的指引。该段规定，处置组的减值损失分摊至属于 IFRS 5 适用范围的非流动资产，且以这些资产的账面价值为限。其他资产和负债在处置组的初始计量和后续计量中均按照适用的国际财务报告准则计量。因此，超过非流动资产账面金额的任何减值损失将在处置时确认。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 第二种方法是将减值损失分摊至处置组内的全部资产，而不仅限于非流动资产。这一观点得到了 IFRS 5 第15段的支持，该段规定主体应当将划分为持有待售的非流动资产（或处置组）按账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低计量。此外，准则还规定，如果属于 IFRS 5 计量要求范围内的非流动资产构成处置组的一部分，则这些计量要求适用于整个处置组，从而使处置组整体按账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低计量。在此观点下，由于未满足 IAS 37 中负债的定义，超过可分摊至处置组全部资产金额的减值损失不会单独确认为负债。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 国际会计准则理事会（IASB）承认 IFRS 5 内部存在冲突，即准则既要求将处置组按公允价值减去出售费用后的净额确认，又要求损失仅分摊至非流动资产。迄今为止尚未作出相应修订。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 根据第一种观点，处置组的减值损失仅分摊至属于 IFRS 5 适用范围的非流动资产。因此，在本例中，减值损失将以不动产、厂场和设备的账面金额（即 C60）为限。除非满足 IAS 37 的条件，否则剩余的 C20 不能确认为负债。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 根据另一种观点，减值损失并不仅限于非流动资产。因此，将确认 C80 的减值损失。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.78.1 – 减值转回：两种方法

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 国际财务报告准则解释委员会（IFRS IC）于 2010年5月注意到的一项冲突与减值损失转回有关。IFRS 5 第23段援引 IAS 36 的指引以确定此类转回的分摊顺序。具体而言，IAS 36 第124段禁止恢复已减值的商誉。然而，IFRS 5 第22段似乎并未禁止此类转回，只要转回金额不超过先前根据 IFRS 5 或在划分为持有待售前根据 IAS 36 确认的累计减值损失即可。我们的观点是，与 IAS 36 的指引一致，IFRS 5 的指引禁止转回商誉减值损失。但是，IFRS IC 认为这是一个潜在的实务分歧领域，并建议 IASB 在 IFRS 5 实施后审议中予以考虑。因此，在进一步指引发布之前，对该指引的两种解释目前均可能是可接受的。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 实施指南第13段（IG 13） 参考正文：30.88

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 当主体专为转售而取得一家子公司时，在购买日及后续资产负债表日存在会计处理选择。主体可以选择对单项资产和负债采用完全合并法，或者采用 IFRS 5 实施指南中规定的简便方法（快捷法）。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 选择采用完全合并法的主体必须对所取得的业务进行完整的公允价值评估，随后应用 IFRS 5 的一般计量原则。特定非流动资产以及全部流动资产、流动负债和非流动负债均按照适用的会计准则进行估值（参见第30.19段）。完成此步骤后，该处置组（即该子公司）应作为一个整体按账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低计量。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在每个后续报告日，对于不属于 IFRS 5 适用范围的非流动资产以及全部流动资产、流动负债和非流动负债，应按照适用的会计准则重新计量其账面价值。重新计量产生的任何损失均计入利润表。对不属于 IFRS 5 适用范围的资产和负债进行重新计量时，也可以确认利得。对于属于 IFRS 5 适用范围的非流动资产，其账面价值将等于购买时分配的初始账面价值。因此，仅在转回先前报告期已确认减值的限度内方可确认利得。每个报告期还需按照 IFRS 5 的计量原则重新评估该处置组的公允价值（参见第30.19段）。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 当处置组继续运营且其流动净资产增加时，购买后产生的任何利润均予以确认。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 作为替代方案，IFRS 5 的实施指南针对专为转售而持有的子公司提供了一种合并的简便方法（快捷法）。允许采用简便方法（快捷法）的原因在于，它避免了按照企业合并指引进行完整公允价值评估的负担，从而使该子公司在实质上能够作为单项投资资产进行处理。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 简便方法（快捷法）要求在每个报告日按公允价值减去出售费用后的净额对拟处置主体进行估值。采用简便方法（快捷法）的结果是，无需对专为转售而取得的主体的全部单项资产和负债进行公允价值计量。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 出于资产负债表列报目的，该主体的可辨认负债按公允价值计量，并将该金额加至公允价值减去出售费用后的净额，以确定拟披露的资产价值。

text: 示例——简便方法（快捷法）的应用

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体 A 收购了控股公司主体 H，后者拥有两家子公司 A 和 B。子公司 B 系专为出售而取得，且满足划分为持有待售的条件。根据 IFRS 5 第32(c)段，子公司 B 同时属于一项终止经营。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 子公司 B 的估计公允价值减去出售费用后的净额为 C135。主体 A 对子公司 B 的会计处理如下：

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 初始计量时，主体 A 按公允价值计量子公司 B 的可辨认负债，假设为 C40。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 初始计量时，主体 A 将所取得的资产计量为 C175，即子公司 B 的公允价值减去出售费用后的净额（C135）加上可辨认负债的公允价值（C40）。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 于资产负债表日，主体 A 按成本与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低重新计量该处置组，假设为 C130。这意味着需要记录 C5 的减值损失。负债按照适用的国际财务报告准则重新计量，假设为 C35。此时资产总额为 C165（C130 + C35）。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 于资产负债表日，主体 A 在其合并财务报表中将上述资产（C165）和负债（C35）与其他资产和负债分开列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: - 在利润表中，主体 A 将子公司 B 的税后损益与子公司 B 后续重新计量确认的税后利得或损失合计列报为 (C5)，等于该处置组从 C135 重新计量至 C130 的变动额。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 若采用简便方法（快捷法），则无需对资产和负债或处置组的价值变动进行进一步分析。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在财务报表附注中，通常需要披露处置组和终止经营的主要资产和负债类别。对于专为转售而持有的子公司，无需对资产和负债进行（除资产负债表列报要求之外的）进一步分析。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 本例说明了若干要点。首先，按照 IFRS 5 中的简便方法（快捷法）对专为转售而持有的子公司进行合并，并非传统的逐行合并。初始时，该子公司按公允价值减去出售费用后的净额计量；在每个后续报告日，按初始账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低重新计量（遵循处置组的一般要求）。该子公司账面价值的净变动额即为按照 IFRS 5 第33段在终止经营中报告的单行结果。然而应当注意，在后续期间通常无需进行此类重新计量，因为持有待售的主体一般会在该期间内售出。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 准则中的简便方法（快捷法）示例还表明，尽管要求主体合并专为转售而持有的子公司，但无需单独辨认被收购主体的可辨认资产（包括无形资产）、负债和商誉。简便方法（快捷法）允许主体先计量该子公司整体的公允价值减去出售费用后的净额，然后计量其负债的公允价值，而其资产（包括商誉）的公允价值减去出售费用后的净额则作为倒轧差额得出。这比执行完整的 IFRS 3 公允价值评估工作量小得多。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 上述示例显示，该子公司整体被重新计量至较低的公允价值减去出售费用后的净额 C130（原账面金额为 C135）。账面价值的减少额 C5 代表了子公司 B 后续重新计量所确认的税后损失。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 准则并未专门涉及价值增加的情形；但是，由于专为转售而持有的子公司属于一个处置组，其必须始终按账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额两者孰低计量。因此，公允价值减去出售费用后的净额的增加（超过该子公司初始列报金额的部分）不得确认，除非属于转回先前已确认的减值。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.88.2 – 应用简便方法（快捷法）的实务问题：集团内部交易

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 参考准则：IFRS 5 实施指南第13段（IG 13） 参考正文：30.88

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: IFRS 5 未就采用简便方法（快捷法）时集团内部交易的处理提供任何指引。当处置组是专为转售而持有的子公司且采用简便方法（快捷法）时，很难应用常规合并程序抵销集团内部余额。合并的一般原则是集团资产负债表上的内部往来余额应当予以抵销。若采用完全合并法，则适用第30.86段的指引。当采用简便方法（快捷法）时，并不单独辨认各项资产和负债余额（包括内部往来余额）。由此产生的问题是，如何处理采用简便方法（快捷法）计量的处置组与持续经营集团其余部分之间的集团内部余额。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 我们认为，即使内部往来余额未被单独辨认，直接针对处置组的账面金额记录抵销分录也是恰当的。尽管这会导致处置组账面金额发生变动（可能增加或减少），但该变动是由记录集团内部抵销分录引起的，而非计量变动所致。IFRS 5 的计量规则仍然得到了正确应用。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 利润表中集团内部交易的处理则不那么直接。采用完全合并法时，适用第30.86段给出的指引。采用简便方法（快捷法）时，重新计量采用的是资产负债表法，因此利润表中与处置组相关的金额代表了公允价值减去出售费用后的净额与账面金额之间的净变动。因此，利润表中不会辨认出单项经营收入或费用项目。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 由于采用简便方法（快捷法），专为转售而持有的子公司不会列示任何单项利润表项目。当持有待售子公司支付或收取集团内部股利和利息时，这可能会引发问题。持续经营集团已在其利润表中记录了集团内部收入或费用；但在处置组中，该收入或费用项目并未单独记录，因此利润表中不存在可予抵销的集团内部项目。在这些情形下，我们认为应适用的一般原则是：在利息或股利以现金结算且不太可能退还现金（即并非循环交易）的限度内，在合并利润表中记录持续经营集团的应收或应付利息是恰当的。如果利息或股利支付是通过集团内部往来交易结算的，我们认为在合并利润表中记录该收入/费用是不恰当的。持续经营集团利润表中记录的金额应予冲回并暂挂于资产负债表上。资产负债表上的该余额将在处置组后续出售时释放，并作为处置损益的一部分予以确认。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: EX 30.88.3 – 抵销应收专为转售而持有子公司的利息

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 处置组以现金支付其向主体 P 借款所产生的到期利息。在处置组的个别账簿中，其会记录利息费用并按支付金额减少现金。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 主体 P 会在其个别账簿中记录利息收入，并按收到金额增加现金。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 在合并财务报表中，增加的现金需要在持续经营集团中予以反映。由于已经收到现金，该利息收入将保留在利润表中。出于合并目的，处置组不会就该交易记录任何分录。然而，应将处置组的账面金额与公允价值减去出售费用后的净额进行比较，以核查从处置组转出现金后是否存在减值。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 2)
text: 如果由于利息系通过集团内部往来账户支付而未收到现金，则在合并利润表中记录该利息收入是不恰当的。在此情形下，我们认为最恰当的做法是将该利息记录为递延收益，并在处置组出售时将该余额释放，作为处置损益的一部分。

text: The contract to receive contingent consideration meets the definition of a financial asset, because it gives the seller a contractual right to receive cash when the contingency is resolved [IAS 32 para 11]. It should be included as part of the consideration received in determining any gain/loss on disposal, and it should be classified and measured under IFRS 9.

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)

This is because the asset’s return does not represent only compensation for time value of money, credit and other basic lending risks, costs, plus a profit margin; rather, it also includes an exposure to the revenue of subsidiary B that is inconsistent with a basic lending arrangement. chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: Inter-company balances will need to be eliminated on consolidation where cash has been passed between the disposal group and other businesses in the group through inter-company accounts. These transfers of cash to and from the disposal group through the inter-company account will have an impact on the carrying amount shown in the consolidated financial statements. However, this does not mean that the fair value of the disposal group has changed.

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: Inter-company income and expenses (for example, interest or dividends) also need to be eliminated. This is straightforward where an entity is classified as held for sale after it has formed part of the consolidated trading group. Where an entity is acquired exclusively with a view to resale, and so it has only ever been held in the consolidated financial statements under IFRS 5, the situation is more complicated (see para 30.82).

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: IFRS 10 第25(b)段要求“在原剩余子公司中保留的投资”按其公允价值计量。该投资包括在不再纳入合并范围时保留的任何权益性利益。但是，主体也可能保留其他权益，例如优先股、债务或其他合同安排。当公司因丧失控制权而不再合并某子公司时，应评估所有保留权益和关系，以识别在不再合并时是否应确认其他保留要素，从而影响处置损益。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 主体 A 拥有子公司 B 100% 的股权。子公司 B 以名义成本向主体 A 租赁一栋办公楼。主体 A 将子公司 B 60% 的股份出售给无关联第三方，并在丧失控制权时不再合并子公司 B。该租赁合同将由买方承继。作为谈判的一部分，双方同意租赁协议中的定价将延续五年，之后恢复至市场费率。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 在不再合并子公司 B 时，主体 A 将保留 40% 的股权权益，以及与子公司 B 之间的一项偏离市场条件的租赁关系。在确定不再合并子公司 B 时应确认的损益金额时，主体 A 应确定从买方收到的对价中哪一部分属于对该租赁合同的补偿，哪一部分与所出售的 60% 股权相关。该偏离市场条件的租赁合同及其相关对价的影响，应在 IFRS 16 的规定框架下予以考虑，详见第 15 章。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 收取或有对价的合同符合金融资产的定义，因为该合同赋予卖方在或有事项解决时收取现金的合同权利（[IAS 32 第11段]）。在确定处置损益时，应将其作为所收取对价的一部分予以计入，并按照 IFRS 9 进行分类和计量。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 在本例中，该或有对价资产未能通过 IFRS 9 中的“仅为对本金和以未偿付本金金额为基础的利息的支付”（SPPI）标准，因此主体 A 应将其以公允价值计量且其变动计入当期损益（FVTPL）。这是因为该资产的回报并非仅代表对货币时间价值、信用风险以及其他基本借贷风险、成本加利润率的对价；相反，它还包含与基本借贷安排不一致的对子公司 B 营业收入的敞口（[IFRS 9 附录 B 第B4.1.7–B4.1.9段]）。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: IFRS 9 并未要求对以公允价值计量且其变动计入当期损益的资产的公允价值变动进行拆分。但是，主体可以选择将公允价值变动拆分为类似于利息收入的金额（可采用实际利率法计算）以及其他公允价值变动。如果主体选择如此处理，则应遵循 FAQ 4.102.5 中的指引。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 如果应收出售对价仅仅是递延支付，而不取决于未来业绩（即金额在出售日已固定，并在固定日期或若干固定日期支付），则该资产将符合 IFRS 9 中的 SPPI 标准。如果主体 A 的业务模式为“以收取合同现金流量为目标”，则该应收款项按摊余成本计量。利息收入采用实际利率法计算并确认，且该应收款项适用 IFRS 9 的预期信用损失减值规定。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 如果或有对价的解决与终止经营相关，则应在利润表的“终止经营”项目下列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 当处置组与集团内其他业务之间通过集团内部往来账户划转现金时，合并时需要对集团内部余额进行抵销。这些通过集团内部往来账户在处置组与其他业务之间进行的现金划转，将影响合并财务报表中列示的账面价值。但是，这并不意味着处置组的公允价值发生了变化。上述变动系抵销集团内部余额所致。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 当处置组向持续经营业务出售商品（或反之）时，也可能产生集团内部交易。在此类情况下，应适用相同的原则：集团内部余额和交易应当全额抵销。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 集团内部收益和费用（例如利息或股利）同样需要抵销。若某主体在成为合并经营集团的一部分后被划分为持有待售，这一处理较为直接。若某主体是专为转售而取得的，因此在合并财务报表中始终仅依据 IFRS 5 持有，则情况较为复杂（参见第30.82段）。

text: 主体 A 编制合并财务报表，纳入其所有子公司，包括主体 C。主体 C 符合 IFRS 5 下处置组的定义。在初始划分为持有待售之日至资产负债表日期间，主体 C 向主体 A 出售了一批商品。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)

text: FAQ 30.97.4 – 集团内部交易应在何处抵销？

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 国际财务报告解释委员会（IFRIC）指出，不对集团内部交易进行抵销将与 IFRS 10 的抵销要求不一致。在缺乏明确指引的情况下，主体应当选择一项会计政策并一贯采用。尽管 IFRS 5 对此事项未作规定，但部分国家的监管机构可能对持续经营与终止经营之间集团内部交易的会计处理和列报持有特定观点。在考虑下述指引时，如适用，应当考虑相关监管机构的此类要求。我们认为，主体可以选择：

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: - 不作任何调整地抵销集团内部交易（即在持续经营和终止经营内部各自抵销）；

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: - 针对终止经营抵销集团内部交易；或者

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: - 考察处置后的情况，确定针对终止经营抵销还是针对持续经营业务抵销更为恰当。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: IFRIC 指出，视具体事实和情况而定，主体可能需要提供额外披露，以便财务报表使用者能够评估终止经营的财务影响。在此情况下，可在附注中对终止经营的集团内部交易作出补充列报。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 如果主体选择考察处置后的情况，则应确定持续经营与终止经营之间的安排在处置后是否会继续。如果预计该安排将继续，则在持续经营中记录销售额和成本，从而在终止经营中记录抵销分录将是恰当的。这将反映持续经营业务在持续基础上的经营成果。终止经营的经营成果将仅包括在处置时将从集团中消除的成本和收入。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 如果该安排不太可能继续，则抵销分录应针对持续经营记录。终止经营的经营成果将包括在处置后不再归属于集团的销售额和成本。下图流程对此进行了说明：

text: 某集团正在处置业务 A，该业务符合 IFRS 5 划分为终止经营的条件。该集团还拥有业务 B 和业务 C，二者按市场价格向业务 A 出售原材料。本年度业务 B 和业务 C 向业务 A 出售商品的价值为 C100 万（生产成本：C70 万）。业务 A 在其制造过程中使用这些商品，并通过向外部销售产成品实现外部营业额 C150 万。集团预计未来将继续向业务 A 进行销售。业务 B 和业务 C 向业务 A 的销售应如何进行会计处理？

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 如果集团选择了评估安排未来是否继续的会计政策，则集团应针对终止经营记录抵销分录。由于该安排未来将继续，业务 B 和业务 C 的经营成果应包含在后续期间将成为外部收入的金额。应列报为终止经营的收入为剩余的 C50 万，因为这是处置后不再归属于集团的收入。

text: IFRS 10 与 IAS 28 之间的相互作用目前尚不明确。IAS 28 指出，当向联营企业或合营企业进行非货币性投入时，仅就不再拥有的部分确认利得或损失。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: IFRS 10 包含关于子公司所有者权益变动的会计处理指引，包括与非控制性权益的交易以及取得或丧失控制权的交易。IFRS 10 明确规定，当丧失对子公司的控制权时，任何保留权益应按其公允价值重新计量，由此产生的任何利得或损失计入损益。因此，除不再拥有部分的利得或损失外，保留部分也会确认利得或损失。IFRS 10 规定，与非控制性权益的任何交易（维持控制权）应作为权益性交易进行会计处理。因此，当部分处置后子公司仍为子公司时，任何利得或损失直接计入权益。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: IAS 28 适用于联营企业和合营企业。当向某主体投入子公司或业务以换取股份并保留控制权或金融资产时，不应类推适用 IAS 28 中的指引。然而，如果向联营企业或合营企业投入子公司或业务以换取重大影响或共同控制权益，则 IAS 28 与 IFRS 10 之间存在冲突。主体在处理向联营企业或共同控制主体投入子公司或业务时，应选定一项会计政策，并一贯适用 IAS 28 或 IFRS 10。

chapter: 30 - Disposal of subsidiaries, businesses and non-current assets (IFRS 5) (Part 3)
text: 2014 年 9 月，国际会计准则理事会（IASB）发布了对 IFRS 10 和 IAS 28 的修订，以解决两项准则之间的不一致。该修订澄清，当出售或投入的非货币性资产构成一项业务时，投资方应全额确认利得或损失；但当资产不符合业务定义时，投资方仅以其他投资方所占权益为限确认利得或损失。该修订原定于 2016 年 1 月 1 日或之后开始的期间生效，并要求采用未来适用法。然而，其生效日期已被无限期推迟，以作为更广泛的权益法会计项目的一部分予以解决。在确定新的生效日期之前，投资方拥有会计政策选择权，并应一贯应用。

Introduction and scope (paras 31.1 - 31.8)

31.1 Investments in associates and joint ventures are accounted for under the equity method set out in IAS 28, subject to certain exceptions. Associates are those investments where the investor has significant influence. A joint venture is a joint arrangement where the investor has joint control but does not have direct rights to assets or obligation for liabilities (see chapter 32 para 25). The related disclosure requirements are set out in IFRS
31.2 An investor uses the equity method to account for its interests in joint ventures and associates.
Exceptions from using the equity method
31.3 An investment in an associate or a joint venture must be accounted for using the equity method under IAS 28, unless one of the following applies:
- The investment is classified as held for sale in accordance with IFRS 5. [IAS 28 para 20].
- The reporting entity is a parent exempt from preparing consolidated or economic interest financial statements. [IAS 28 para 17].
- The investment in associate or joint venture is held by (or is held indirectly through):
- venture capital organisations; or
- mutual funds, unit trusts and similar entities including investment-linked insurance funds.

The exemption from using the equity method in the third bullet is available if the investments are measured at fair value through profit or loss in accordance with IFRS 9 (IAS 39). See chapter 42 para 7. An entity can make this election separately for each associate or joint venture at initial recognition.
[IAS 28 para 18]. [IAS 28 para 19].

FAQ 31.3.2 – Practical issues relating to ‘venture capital’ organisations FAQ 31.3.3 – Venture capital organisations that undertake both venture capital and other business activities FAQ 31.3.4 – What are the characteristics of mutual funds, unit trusts and similar entities including investment-linked insurance funds? FAQ 31.3.5 – How to account for a change in intention

31.4 An investor measures an associate or a joint venture that is classified as held for sale at the lower of its carrying amount at the date of classification as held for sale and fair value less costs to sell. Equity accounting ceases once an associate or a joint venture is classified as held for sale. See further chapter 30 para 68 on disposals.
Exemption from preparing consolidated or economic interest financial statements

31.5 Some parent companies and investors with investments in subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures are exempt from the requirement to prepare consolidated financial statements or economic interest financial statements. Those parent companies and investors, therefore, do not consolidate and equity account for their interests. See chapter 26 para 11.

31.6 An entity that is not a parent but that has an investment in an associate or a joint venture must prepare financial statements that include the associate or the joint venture on an equity accounting basis. These financial statements are referred to in this chapter as ‘economic interest’ financial statements.

31.7 Entities that only have investments in associates or joint ventures are exempt from the requirement to prepare ‘economic interest’ financial statements if certain conditions are met. These conditions, all of which must be met, are:

- The entity is a wholly owned subsidiary, or is a partially owned subsidiary of another entity and its other owners have been informed about, and do not object to, the entity not applying the equity method.
- The entity’s debt or equity instruments are not traded in a public market and the entity did not file, and is not in the process of issuing, any class of instruments in a public market.
- The ultimate or any intermediate parent of the entity produces consolidated financial statements available for public use that comply with IFRS.

FAQ 31.7.1 – Availability of the exemption from preparing consolidated or economic interest financial statements FAQ 31.7.2 – Is the exemption available in relation to economic interest financial statements?

31.8 Entities that are exempt from preparing economic interest financial statements prepare ‘separate’ financial statements as their only financial statements. Separate financial statements include subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures, either at cost, in accordance with IFRS 9 (IAS 39), or using the equity method as described in this chapter. See further chapter 28 para 3 on separate financial statements.

Classification and measurement as an associate or joint venture (paras 31.9-31.39)
Significant influence and joint control

31.9 An associate is an investment over which the investor has significant influence. Significant influence is the power to participate in decision making but not control or joint control. A joint venture is a joint arrangement where the parties have joint control and rights to the net assets of the joint arrangement. An investor uses the equity method to account for its interests in associates and joint ventures. See chapter 32 para 29 for discu

31.10 An investor that holds 20% or more of the voting power of another entity, either directly or indirectly, is presumed to have significant influence over that entity. The presumption of significant influence from a 20% or more investment can be rebutted where an entity can demonstrate that it has or does not have significant influence. Likewise, significant influence could be demonstrated for an investment of less than 20%. The existence of a
FAQ 31.10.1 – What is the concept of voting power?
31.11 An entity could demonstrate that it has significant influence over an investment in the following ways:
- Representation on the board of directors or equivalent governing body of the investee.
- Participation in policy-making processes, including participation in decisions about dividends or other distributions.
- Material transactions between the entity and the investee.
- Interchange of managerial personnel.
- Provision of essential technical information.

Potential voting rights exist where an entity owns share warrants, share call options, debt or equity instruments that are convertible into ordinary shares, or other similar instruments that have
Measurement under the equity method
Overview of the equity method

31.13 The equity method presents the investment in the associate or joint venture in a single line in the balance sheet. The investment is initially recognised at cost and adjusted thereafter for the post-acquisition change in the investor’s share of the investee’s net assets (‘share of results’) of the associate or joint venture.
31.14 An overview of the equity method is as follows:
- The investment is stated as one line item, initially recognised at cost (see para 31.22).
- A notional ‘purchase price allocation’ is carried out to recognise any necessary fair value adjustments, similar to business combination accounting (see para 31.37).
- The investor recognises its share of the profit or loss of the associate or joint venture for the period in the income statement, with an adjustment to the carrying amount of the investment.

- The investor’s share of profit or loss is adjusted for the effect of any fair value adjustments that arose in the notional purchase price allocation at initial recognition and any adjustments to conform to accounting policies.
- Appropriate adjustments are made for any unrealised profits or losses arising from upstream and downstream transactions.
- Any distributions received from the associate or the joint venture reduce the investment’s carrying amount.

- The investor recognises directly in other comprehensive income its share of other comprehensive income of the associate or joint venture. Amounts might be reported in other comprehensive income, for example, from the revaluation of property, plant and equipment, remeasurements of net defined benefit obligations or from foreign exchange translation differences.

- Investments in associates and joint ventures are tested for impairment using the measurement guidance in IAS 36, where indicators of impairment under paragraphs 41A to 41C of IAS 28 (previously IAS 39) are present.
- Equity accounting ceases when significant influence or joint control is no longer present.

IAS 28 is silent on these transactions. In 2012, the IASB added this issue to its agenda as a separate amendment rather than an annual improvement. Split measurement accounting

31.15 An investor might hold its interest (or a portion of its interest) in an associate indirectly through venture capital organisations, or mutual funds, unit trusts and similar entities. The investor might elect to measure that portion at fair value through profit or loss under IFRS 9 (IAS 39) (see para 31.3). This treatment is available even if the investor has significant influence over the investment. The remaining investment is accounted f
FAQ 31.15.1 – Accounting in the consolidated financial statements of the parent
Initial recognition and application of the equity method

31.16 Equity accounting begins on the date when an investment becomes an associate or a joint venture. The equity method applies many of the same procedures as purchase accounting under IFRS 3 and consolidation under IFRS 10.

31.17 An investment in an associate or a joint venture is initially recognised at cost. An investor might acquire its interest in an associate or a joint venture in a number of ways, and each has an impact on the determination of cost at initial recognition. An interest in an associate or joint venture might be acquired:
- for cash or another financial asset;
- through an exchange of non-monetary assets, including through contribution of an asset to an associate or joint venture on formation;
- through losing control of a business and retaining an interest that gives the investor significant influence or joint control; or
- through an increase in an existing stake, accompanied by the investor obtaining significant influence or joint control (step acquisition).
FAQ 31.17.1 – Methods of obtaining an equity stake
31.18 Any difference between the cost of the investment and the investor’s share of the fair values of the investee’s identifiable assets and liabilities acquired is accounted for as follows:
- Notional goodwill relating to an associate or a joint venture is included in the carrying amount of the investment.

- Bargain purchase gain or negative goodwill (in other words, ‘excess of the entity’s share of the net fair value of the associate’s identifiable assets and liabilities over the cost of the investment’) is included as part of the investor’s share of the associate or joint venture profit or loss in the period in which the investment is acquired.

31.19 The carrying amount of an investment in an associate or a joint venture will be stated at an amount greater than its cost after the recognition of a bargain purchase gain at initial recognition. A carrying value in excess of market price is an indicator of impairment under IAS 28. Therefore, after recognising a bargain purchase gain, an investment in an associate or joint venture should be tested for impairment.
Long-term loans to associates or joint ventures

31.20 An investor might have other financial interests in an associate or a joint venture that, in substance, form part of the net investment in the associate or the joint venture. That interest might take different legal forms, such as preference shares, long-term receivables and loans for which settlement is neither planned nor likely to occur in the foreseeable future. The long-term interest is part of the net investment in the associate or th

31.21 A long-term interest is initially recognised as a financial asset by the investor at fair value in accordance with IFRS 9 (IAS 39), and it is subsequently measured in accordance with that standard.
[IAS 28 para 14]. [IAS 28 para 14A].

Cost at initial recognition

31.22 Cost is not defined in the standard, but it is usually understood to be the fair value of cash or other consideration paid by the purchaser. Cost, in most asset standards under IFRS, includes transaction costs. It is reasonable for those costs to form part of the investment in the associate or joint venture at initial recognition.
Acquisition of an associate or joint venture for cash or other financial assets

31.23 The cost of an investment in an associate or a joint venture at initial recognition usually includes an estimate of any contingent consideration at fair value. Contingent consideration is further consideration due to the seller where the amount is uncertain or payment depends on the outcome of future events. The most common form of contingent consideration arises where the acquirer agrees to pay additional consideration, in cash or in share

31.24 An investor has an accounting policy choice on how to account for subsequent changes in the value of the contingent consideration until settled. The investor can follow a cost accumulation approach, adjusting all changes in contingent consideration to the investment in the associate or joint venture, by analogy to variable consideration for the acquisition of an asset (see chapter 22 para 32). Alternatively, the investor can apply IFRS 3, b
FAQ 31.24.1 – Determination of cost of an investment in an associate and treatment of contingent consideration
Contributions of an asset or a business

31.25 An investor might contribute assets or a business to its associate or joint venture on formation. The investor might lose control of a business and retain an interest in an associate or a joint venture. These are economically similar transactions. The investor might also receive additional consideration (in the form of cash or other assets) from other investors, as well as an equity interest in the associate or the joint venture in exchange

31.26 An entity that contributes a non-monetary asset, not a business, in exchange for an equity interest in the associate or joint venture recognises any gain or loss from the transaction to the extent of the unrelated party’s interest. Exchanges with third parties are presumed to have commercial substance. If commercial substance is lacking, any gain or loss is unrealised (see chapter 22 para 38 for a description of commercial substance). The c

31.27 An entity might contribute a controlled business to a joint venture or associate, or it might decrease its stake in a controlled business to that of an investment in an associate or joint venture. There is a conflict between the requirements of IFRS 10 and IAS 28 on accounting for such a transaction. This acknowledged conflict gives rise to an accounting policy choice.

31.28 IFRS 10 requires the retained interest in an associate or joint venture to be remeasured at fair value, with both the disposal gain and the holding gain recognised in the income statement. IAS 28 requires the elimination of gains that arise between an investor and its associate or joint venture to the extent of the investor’s interest. Therefore, the investor can choose to recognise a partial gain under the IAS 28 approach or a full gain un

The amendments are available to be adopted, but the IASB has deferred the mandatory effective date of the amendment indefinitely, pending finalisation of its rese

Step acquisition of an associate or a joint venture from an investment

31.30 There is an accounting policy choice available for acquisition of an associate or joint venture in stages (that is, a step acquisition). See further discussion in paragraph 31.31. The investor can follow a cost approach, and accumulate the cost of all purchases (including transaction costs), to determine the amount of the investment. Accounting for ownership changes in an investment from financial asset to subsidiary

31.31 The following chart summarises the accounting for changes in an investor’s interest: from a financial asset (equity instrument) to an associate and then to a subsidiary; from a subsidiary to an associate; to a financial asset; and, finally, disposal.
Increasing a stake in an existing associate and continuing to have significant influence

31.32 An increase in the investor’s interest in an existing associate or joint venture, where the investor continues to have significant influence, is accounted for using a cost accumulation approach. The cost of acquiring the additional stake, including any directly attributable costs, is added to the carrying value of the associate. An entity applies the requirements of IFRS 3 when it acquires a business. See chapter 29 para 166. There is no specific guidance relating to the scenario where control is obtained over an existing associate or joint venture that does not meet the definition of a business in accordance with IFRS 3. Decreasing a stake in an existing associate and retaining significant influence

31.34 An investor might reduce its ownership interest in an associate or joint venture but retain significant influence or joint control. The investor de-recognises the relevant proportion of the carrying amount, and reclassifies to profit or loss or transfers within equity, based on how the reserve should be reclassified on the disposal of related assets or liabilities, a proportionate amount of any gain or loss previously recognised in other co
FAQ 31.34.1 – Partial disposal of an associate retaining significant influence
Increase in share without acquisition

31.35 A reduction of the shares on issue (through a share buyback or other means) might result in an increase in the investor’s interest. The investment might remain an associate following this transaction, or the investor might gain control and the investment would become a subsidiary.

Associates or joint ventures and common control transactions

31.36 An investor might acquire an associate or a joint venture from another entity, and both entities are ultimately controlled by the same party or parties, both before and after the acquisition. There is no scope exemption in IAS 28 for such transactions; therefore, the normal measurement rules (described at para 31.16 onwards) are applicable.

Notional purchase price allocation

These fair value adjustments are not recorded separately, because the investment itself is a single line item. However, the fair values identified form the basis for additional depreciation, amortisation and similar adjustments that are reflected in the investor’s

31.38 The notional goodwill that arises in the notional purchase price allocation is not amortised, and separate disclosure of it is not required. It is not required to be separately tested for impairment, nor does it trigger an annual impairment test, because it is included in the carrying amount of the associate or the joint venture and not shown as a separate asset.

Share of the associate or joint venture (paras 31.40 - 31.75)

31.40 An investor records its share of the results of each associate or joint venture. The ‘share’ to be accounted for might be straightforward, where an investor has a single investment of a specified number of common shares in an associate or joint venture, with no other types of shares or potential voting rights in issue. However, determining the investor’s ‘share’ in results might be complicated by holdings by other members of the group, pote
FAQ 31.40.1 – Determination of the group’s share or holding FAQ 31.40.2 – Subsidiary has an investment in an associate FAQ 31.40.3 – Indirect holding in an associate
Impact of preference shares on share of results

31.41 An associate or a joint venture might issue preference shares. Preference shares need to be classified as a financial liability, an equity instrument, or a compound instrument with both liability and equity components. Classification is based on the substance of the contractual arrangements. Classification as an equity instrument will have implications for the investor’s equity accounting.

31.42 Dividends on preference shares classified as equity that are held by parties other than the investor are deducted from profit or loss of the associate or joint venture by the investor when measuring its share of profit or loss of the associate or joint venture, regardless of whether the dividends are declared. The investor, to the extent that it does not hold the preference share, is not entitled to a share of the after-tax result that is n

31.43 Dividends on preference shares classified as a liability are shown as interest. The investor’s share of the associate’s share of results is determined after deduction of the preference dividend, and it is based solely on the investor’s equity interest.
Impact of options, warrants and convertible debt on share of results

31.44 Potential voting rights (such as share warrants, options and convertibles) held by an entity in an associate or joint venture should be considered when determining whether an entity has significant influence. However, those potential voting rights are not included when determining the investor’s proportion of the net assets and profit or loss of the associate or joint venture, unless they constitute a present ownership interest.

31.45 An investor might have, in substance, an interest in an associate or joint venture that gives it access to the returns associated with an ownership interest. The share of results allocated to the entity is determined after considering the eventual exercise of the potential voting rights and other derivative instruments that currently give the entity access to the returns.

31.46 If the investor includes returns from potential voting rights in its share of results, the instruments that give rise to those rights are not subject to the requirements of IFRS 9 (IAS 39). The investor has included a greater share of the results of its associate or joint venture under the equity method than that which would arise on the basis of the entity’s existing equity holding. The investor does not simultaneously fair value the instr
FAQ 31.46.1 – Determination of present ownership interest FAQ 31.46.2 – Accounting for symmetrical put and call options over associates and joint ventures
Impact of compound instruments issued to the investor on share of results

31.47 The investor ignores potential ownership interests, and considers its present ownership interest, when determining the share to be equity accounted for. This includes a share in the equity element of any convertible loan recorded by the associate or the joint venture. The investor could eliminate the share of the equity element of the convertible loan against the value of the financial asset recorded by the investor.
FAQ 31.47.1 – Accounting for compound instruments issued by the associate or the joint venture to the entity
Impact of cross-holdings on share of results

31.48 Cross-holdings (where the investor and its associate or joint venture own shares in each other) complicate the application of the equity method. No specific guidance is provided in the standard in respect of cross-holdings. The investor needs to develop an approach that follows the principles of IAS 28.
FAQ 31.48.1 – Accounting for cross-holdings of shares
Adjusting the reported ‘results’ of the associate or joint venture
Consistent accounting policies

31.49 The investor should adjust the results of its associate or joint venture, as applicable, to align the investee’s accounting policies with its own policies. An entity that is not an investment entity, but has an interest in an investment entity associate or joint venture, could elect to retain the fair value measurement applied by that associate or joint venture to its interests in subsidiaries. This election is made separately for each inve
[IAS 28 para 35]. [IAS 28 para 36A].
FAQ 31.49.1 – Practical situation requiring adjustment for different accounting policies
Financial statements of associates and joint ventures

31.50 The financial statements of associates and joint ventures should be co-terminous with those of the investor; where this is impracticable, the financial statements should be prepared to a date not more than three months before or after the investor’s reporting date.
FAQ 31.50.1 – Listed associate’s period end more than three months before or after the entity’s period end

31.51 There might be significant transactions or events that occur between the date of the associate’s or joint venture’s year end and that of the investor, where the dates are different. The results of the associate or joint venture should be adjusted for such events, where the effect is material.

FAQ 31.51.1 – Abnormal transaction between associate’s period end and that of the entity FAQ 31.51.2 - Should an investor make adjustments to its equity-accounted earnings for changes to its investee’s earnings during the lag period?

1. What are the characteristics of ‘venture capital’ organisations?

Where an entity is a member of a recognised venture capital organisation, or it meets the conditions for membership of a recognised venture capital organisation, this would be evidence that it met the conditions for exemption in IAS 28.
In less obvious situations, the following characteristics indicate that an entity is a venture capital organisation:

- It has, as its principal business, the provision of equity finance to unquoted companies and makes its returns mainly through medium- to long-term capital gain. These activities might include start-up and other early-stage expansion, management buy-out or management buy-in investment which includes an ‘equity-type’ return.
- It takes an active role in helping to build and develop the companies in which it invests.
- It is a member of a recognised regulatory authority, where appropriate.
2. Is the exemption available if the entity undertakes both venture capital and other business activities?

In this case, the distinction might be more difficult to make. The exemption applies to venture capital ‘organisations’. The ‘organisation’ does not have to be a separate legal entity, but it does have to be a division or a branch that is clearly separated and managed independently from the entity’s other business activities (for example, the division or branch might have its own management team). See FAQ 31.3.3 for an example of such a situation.

IFRS 9 – No. To take advantage of the scope exemption in IAS 28 for a venture capital organisation’s economic interest or consolidated financial statements, a venture capital organisation cannot make the irrevocable election, on initial recognition, to present changes in fair value in other comprehensive income as allowed under IFRS 9, because the scope exemption in IAS 28 requires fair value changes to be recognised in profit or loss.

IAS 39 – A venture capital organisation holds investments for periods up to three to five years and classifies such investments under IAS 39 as available-for-sale. To take advantage of the scope exemption in IAS 28, these investments need to be designated as at fair value through profit or loss on initial recognition and not classified as available-for-sale under IAS 39. The classification as available-for-sale would not result in fair value chan
4. Does the exemption apply where the ‘venture capital’ organisation is a subsidiary?

The exemption in IAS 28 applies if the venture capital organisation is a subsidiary included in the parent’s consolidated financial statements, even if the parent itself is not a venture capital organisation.
However, the scope exemption is not applied to investments in the same investee that are held by the parent’s other subsidiaries or divisions that are not venture capital organisations.

It would also be necessary to consider whether the investment made by the subsidiary venture capital organisation in a related group entity is a venture capital investment, and whether the parent (in its consolidated financial statements) and subsidiary (in its own financial statements) should equity account the investment instead.

Reference to standard: IAS 28 paras 18, 19 Reference to standing text: 31.3
The exemption from equity accounting in IAS 28 also applies to mutual funds, unit trusts and similar entities including investment-linked insurance funds.
Investment-linked insurance funds are insurance structures in which policy holders participate directly in the risks and returns from those investments.

Unit trusts, mutual funds and similar funds typically pay a return on their liabilities that is contractually linked to changes in the fair value of an asset or a pool of assets. The application of the exemption avoids a mismatch between the measurement of the assets and liabilities.

FAQ 31.11.3 – Practical considerations regarding participation in the policy-making process
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 6 Reference to standing text: 31.11

An associate relationship will exist if it can be demonstrated that the entity has the power to participate in the direction of its investee through representation in the policy decisions covering aspects of policy relevant to the entity, including decisions on strategic issues, dividends and other distributions.
Participation in the policy-making process means being involved in strategic decisions, such as:
- expansion or contraction of the business;
- participation in other entities;
- changes in products, markets and activities; and
- determining the balance between dividend and reinvestment.

Such participation will be with a view to gaining economic benefits from the entity’s activities, although the entity will also be exposed to the risk that those activities might be loss-making. For example, this would be accomplished by representation on the board of directors, because a director has power to participate in decision-making, where voting is often carried out by a show of hands.

A single shareholder with less than 20% of the voting rights has significant influence and the power to participate in policy-making decisions if, for example, it has board representation. A shareholder with the same percentage shareholding and no board representation would not have the equivalent influence or power to participate.
A fund manager might have significant influence, regardless of the percentage shareholding, and needs to make an assessment of whether or not it does, based on the specific facts and circumstances.

FAQ 31.51.2 – Should an investor make adjustments to its equity-accounted earnings for changes to its investee’s earnings during the lag period?
Reference to standard: IAS 28 paras 33, 34 Reference to standing text: 31.51

Due to a local or global event that is ongoing, many entities are experiencing adverse trading conditions, and financial results are being impacted. For entities that have equity-accounted investments, this could have accounting implications – these could include a decline in operational results, impairment and other related impacts for their associates.

Where an investor has an equity-accounted investment in an investee which has a different reporting period from the investor, IAS 28 requires the investor to adjust the earnings of the investee for significant transactions or events that occur between the date of the associate’s or joint venture’s year end and that of the investor. [IAS 28 para 33]. [IAS 28 para 34].

The difference in reporting periods between the investor and the associate or joint venture is often referred to as the ‘lag period’. As a result of ongoing events, an investee’s results during the lag period might have been affected.
Question Should an investor make adjustments to its equity-accounted earnings for changes to its investee’s earnings during the lag period?

Answer It depends. If the transactions or events in the lag period are significant, the investor should make adjustments during the lag period. Judgement will be required to determine whether the transactions or events in the lag period are significant.

This does not necessarily mean that distinct accounting entries must be recorded in the investee's accounts, in terms of IFRS, for the transaction or event to be deemed significant for adjustment in the investor's accounts. However, there does need to be a significant event in order for paragraph 34 of IAS 28 to apply. Determining whether there has been a significant event is a matter of judgement. It is not sufficient to consider only relatively
The illustration below sets out examples of how the event might impact reporting for entities that have associates with non-coterminous year ends.
Entity A prepares annual financial statements at 31 March 2020 each year. One of entity A’s associates, entity Y, prepares annual financial statements at 31 December 2019.
Due to the ongoing event, entity Y saw a decline in operational results during the period from 31 December 2019 to 31 March 2020.
Example 1 – The investee recognised a significant impairment during the lag period

There has been a significant event – namely, a material impairment in one of the investee’s cash-generating units during the lag period. The investor should make an adjustment to the lag period accounting if this is material to the investor.
Example 2 – The investee has seen a decline in results as a consequence of the general economic decline.

There has not been a significant event during the lag period. Relatively poor trading results in the lag period would not, on their own, indicate the existence of a significant event that requires adjustment during the lag period.

Example 3 – The investee was forced by government decree to shut down its stores due to the events, but no impairment or provision has been recognised by the investee, and the entity can reliably measure the impact of the shutdown on its results

There has been a significant event. The requirement for the investee to shut down its stores as a result of the events is a specific and significant event. Therefore, the investor should make an adjustment to the lag period accounting if the amount is material to the investor’s accounts.
The above guidance would apply equally to an improvement in operational results.

If the assessment of whether the ongoing events were considered a significant event required significant judgement and was material, the disclosure as required by paragraph 122 of IAS 1 should be provided.

If subsequently entity B earns profits, entity A will first eliminate the remaining unrealised gain, up to the amount of entity B’s profits otherwise available. Therefore, a further C12 (20% of C60) of unrealised gain is eliminated in 20X6. This means that no share of entity B’s profits is recognised as equity earnings in the consolidated profit or loss in 20X6.
At the end of 20X6 the journals look as follows in the consolidated financial statements of entity A:
DR CR Investment in associate C12 Share of equity-accounted profit C12
To record 20% share of current year profits.
DR CR Share of equity-accounted profit C12 Investment in associate C12
The net impact of the current year journals is C0, as unrealised gains are being eliminated against current year profits. The remaining unrealised gain is now C3.

When the asset is sold to a third party in 20X7, the unrealised gain of C20 has been realised by entity A. Entity A will therefore recognise a gain of C17 (the amount that it previously eliminated in 20X5 and 20X6). C3 of the C20 gain was not previously eliminated. Entity A’s carrying amount of the investment in entity B will therefore be C17 (C5 + C12) at the end of 20X7, representing the pre-transaction carrying amount of C5 plus its share of s
At the end of 20X7 the journals look as follows in the consolidated financial statements of entity A:
DR CR Investment in associate C17 Gain on sale of asset C5 Share of equity-accounted profit C12
Treatment 2 – Deferred gain (applying paragraph 31.56.2 of MoA)
In 20X5, the unrealised gain of C20 is eliminated against the investment in associate, up to the point at which the carrying amount of the associate is reduced to zero (that is, C5).
The remaining unrealised gain is eliminated by recognising a deferred gain of C15 in the consolidated financial statements.
On the sale of the asset, the journals look as follows in the consolidated financial statements of entity A:
DR CR Cash C400 Asset C300 Gain on sale of asset C80 Investment in associate C5 Deferred gain (B/S) C15

In 20X6, entity A will recognise C12 in the consolidated profit and loss as earnings from an associate representing its share of entity B’s profit. The deferred gain will be eliminated against the investment by the same amount, resulting in a remaining deferred gain amount of C3. The carrying amount of the associate will continue to be recorded at zero in the consolidated accounts.
At the end of 20X6 the journals look as follows in the consolidated financial statements of entity A:
DR CR Investment in associate C12 Share of equity-accounted profit C12 Deferred gain (B/S) C12 Investment in associate C12

In 20X7, when the asset is sold to a third party, the full amount of the original unrealised gain of C20 is recognised in the consolidated profit and loss, including the C17 eliminated against the investment in associate and the C3 deferred gain remaining at the end of 20X6.
At the end of 20X7 the journals look as follows in the consolidated financial statements of entity A:
DR CR Investment in associate C17 Deferred gain C3 Gain on disposal of asset C20
FAQ 31.58.1 – Accounting for inter-company trading transactions
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 26 Reference to standing text: 31.58

An entity has a 25% interest in an associate. The entity charges interest of C10,000 on a loan that it has made to the associate. Therefore, the entity has interest income in its profit and loss account of C10,000, and the associate has an interest expense of C10,000.

On equity accounting for the associate, the entity would show, for these items, interest income of C10,000 and a share of the associate’s expense payable of C2,500 (as part of the overall share of the associate’s after-tax result). The entity has only recognised net income of C7,500, which represents the net interest charged by the entity to the associate.
FAQ 31.60.1 – Distributions from associate in excess of carrying amount of investment
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 39 Reference to standing text: 31.60

Entity A has an associate, entity B. The carrying amount of entity A’s investment in entity B is C2,000. Entity B has distributed a dividend to entity A of C2,400. The dividend has no restrictions, and entity A cannot be required to refund the dividend.
Entity A should reduce the carrying value of entity B to nil and recognise the excess of C400 as a gain in its consolidated or economic interest financial statements.
Entity A has no obligation to repay the dividend, and there are no restrictions to recognise the benefit for the excess.

In subsequent years, where entity B makes profits, entity A has to consider how to account for its share of entity B’s profits. Entity A could increase the carrying value of its investment in entity B by its share of subsequent profits and then assess whether the investment is impaired. On the other hand, entity A might consider it appropriate not to recognise its share of entity B’s subsequent profits until the gain previously recognised in prof
FAQ 31.66.1 – Practical considerations in calculating recoverable amount
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 43 Reference to standing text: 31.66

The carrying amount of an investment in an associate or joint venture is not automatically written down to the current share price. The price decline is an indicator and also establishes the ‘fair value less costs of disposal’ of the associate or the joint venture. IAS 36 requires that the recoverable amount using the ‘value in use’ method should also be calculated before recording an impairment loss. If the value in use is higher than the carryi

Calculating the value in use of an associate or a joint venture might entail obtaining cash flow forecasts from the associate’s or the joint venture’s management. The future expected dividend streams from the investment in the associate or the joint venture could also be used in measuring the associate’s or the joint venture’s value in use. [IAS 28 para 42].
FAQ 31.71.1 – Practical considerations regarding loss of significant influence
Reference to standard:IAS 28 para 9 Reference to standing text: 31.71
1. Can an investor continue to have significant influence over an associate operating under restrictions?
An associate might operate under the following restrictions:
- Insolvency or administration procedures in progress
- Government restrictions on the transfer of currency out of the country.
- Significant international sanctions against the country that have a direct impact on the entity’s ability to trade and/or remit profits out of the country.
- Significant government regulation.
In these circumstances, the entity might or might not continue to have significant influence.

An investor entity might still have significant influence over an associate, despite restrictions on the associate’s ability to transfer funds to the investor entity. Such restrictions on the transfer of funds should be considered when assessing an investor entity’s ability to exercise significant influence over an entity. Such restrictions, independently, do not preclude the existence of significant influence.
2. Can a contractual arrangement not to interfere in the associate’s ongoing business result in loss of significant influence?

An entity that has significant influence over an associate might enter into a contractual agreement not to interfere with the associate’s ongoing business. It would be necessary to consider carefully the facts and circumstances to determine whether the contractual arrangement means that the entity has lost its significant influence over the associate. This would depend on, for example, the contract’s legal enforceability and how severe the penalt
FAQ 31.73.1 – Reduction of associate interest to an investment
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 22(b) Reference to standing text: 31.73

Entity A has a 40% stake in entity B. It sells 75% of its stake (reducing its investment to 10%) for a consideration of C7.5 million. The carrying value of entity B (including goodwill) at the date of partial disposal is C9 million and it has a foreign currency translation reserve of C0.5 million. Hence, entity A retains a 10% stake of entity B at a fair value of C2.5 million.

On disposal, entity A will recognise its remaining 10% stake in entity B as a financial asset at its fair value of C2.5 million, record the consideration received of C7.5 million, de-recognise the associate at C9 million, and recycle entity B’s foreign currency translation reserve of 0.5 million to the profit and loss as part of the gain or loss made on disposal.
The resulting difference gives a gain on disposal of C1.5 million ((7.5m + 2.5m – 9m) + 0.5m).
FAQ 31.74.1 – Entity’s stake in associate is diluted
Reference to standard: IAS 28 para 22(b), (c) Reference to standing text: 31.74

Entity A has an associate, entity B, that has 100 shares in issue, of which entity A owns 30. At the time when the investment was made, the fair value of entity B’s net assets was C233 and the initial carrying value of the investment was C100, including C30 of goodwill.
Since the investment was made, entity B has generated profits and the carrying value of the investment is now C127. Entity B now has a fair value of C600.
Entity B issues 50 shares at C300 (fair value) to investors other than entity A. Entity A’s holding is now diluted to 20% (30/150 shares).

The dilution means that entity A has ‘disposed’ of one-third of its interest in entity B, because the interest is diluted from a 30% to a 20% shareholding. The dilution gain or loss is calculated by comparing the carrying value of the disposed interest (C127 × 1/3 = C42) to entity A’s share of the proceeds received for the new shares issued (C300 × 20% = C60), represented by an increase in the associate’s net assets. The gain on dilution is, ther

A portion (C42) of the carrying value of the associate is de-recognised, including de-recognition of C10 of goodwill, being one-third of the original goodwill of C30. The share of proceeds (C60) is added to the carrying value of the investment in the associate. The gain (C18) increases the carrying value of the associate and is recorded in profit or loss.
FAQ 31.79.1 – Common presentation issues in the statement of comprehensive income or income statement
Reference to standard: IAS 1 para 82 Reference to standing text: 31.79
1. Can the entity’s share of the associate’s or the joint venture’s results be included before or adjacent to operating profit?

Yes. This might apply where the associate or the joint venture is an integral vehicle through which the group conducts its operations and its strategy. Using this presentation, the associate’s results are still shown post-tax.
2. How should impairment charges relating to the investment in the associate or joint venture be disclosed?

The presentation of impairment charges should follow the presentation of the entity’s share of the associate’s or the joint venture’s results. The impairment charge should be presented as a separate line item adjacent to the share of the associate’s or the joint venture’s results, and not included as part of the share of the associate’s or the joint venture’s results.
3. How should gains and losses on disposals of associates and joint ventures be presented?
Presentation is dependent of the facts and circumstances. These will normally be presented as part of the entity’s operating activities.

In certain circumstances, it might be appropriate to recognise gains and losses from disposals of associates and joint ventures outside the entity’s operating profit, if it is clear that the disposal is a one-off transaction (that is, it is not expected that the entity will have similar transactions in the future and there is no history of having similar transactions in the past).
The entity’s consolidated or economic interest financial statements should also include sufficient disclosures to aid the users of the financial statements.
4. Should the associate’s or joint venture’s discontinued operations be included within the IFRS 5 discontinued operations line?
No, there is no requirement to ‘strip out’ the entity’s share of its associate’s or its joint venture’s discontinued operations and include it within the IFRS 5 discontinued operations line.
FAQ 31.80.1 – Common presentation issues in the balance sheet
Reference to standard: IFRS 12 para 21 Reference to standing text: 31.80
1. Can the investment in the associate or joint venture be revalued?

It is not permitted, once the balance sheet interest has been ascertained using the equity method of accounting, to then revalue the investment in the associate or the joint venture to its market value, even where the entity is listed. However, the fair value of investments in associates and joint ventures for which there are quoted market prices is required to be disclosed.
2. Should other interests, such as loans to associates and joint ventures, be included within this line item?
This issue is dealt with in FAQ 31.21.1 – Long-term loans to associates.
