text: 准则索引：IAS 32 第50段 正文索引：47.28

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 集团X包含多家子公司，每家子公司在银行B均开立了单独的银行账户。在任何时点，部分账户有正现金余额，另一些账户有负（透支）余额。集团X出于现金管理目的运作以下安排：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 零余额管理（有时称为“现金归集”），即定期（包括在资产负债表日）将多个指定账户的余额划转至单一轧差账户。在某些情况下，划转的金额会在不久之后归还给相关子公司。这可能通过合同约定或由集团管理层选择决定。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 名义现金池，即银行B计算多个指定账户的净余额，并按净额收取或支付利息。余额可能会划转至轧差账户，但并非总是在资产负债表日进行。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 集团X能否将现金余额和透支余额抵销，从而在其合并资产负债表中按净额列报？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 如果要按净额列报余额，必须同时满足IAS 32第42段规定的两项标准。集团X必须拥有当前具有法定可执行性的抵销权，这意味着该权利在任何时候均具有可执行性，而不仅仅在约定情形下（例如违约或破产事项）才具有可执行性。此外，正如国际财务报告准则解释委员会（IFRS IC）2016年3月议程决定所澄清的，集团X必须证明其具有与同一交易对手净额结算期末余额的明确意图。仅用于计算利息而不涉及相关余额结算的名义现金池，不满足第47.23段所述的要求。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 假设与银行B的协议赋予集团X必要的法定可执行抵销权，其会计处理情形如下：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 如果在资产负债表日实行零余额管理，且在次日或其后任何日期均未发生资金归还（现金流量转回），则集团X在资产负债表日仅拥有单一的现金余额或透支余额，并据此列报。在此情况下，IAS 32的抵销要求不相关。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 如果在资产负债表日实行零余额管理，但划转的金额作为集团X的惯例在不久之后归还给相关子公司，则资产负债表日通常仍为单一的现金余额或透支余额，并据此列报。在此情况下，IAS 32的抵销要求同样不相关。然而，在某些情形下，集团X可能拥有单独的现金余额和透支余额（例如，集团X负有在次日将余额归还给各子公司的合同义务）。在此类情形下，现金余额和透支余额在IFRS下通常被视为单独的资产和负债，从而适用IAS 32的抵销要求。此时，集团X无法证明“以净额结算的意图”，因此不能在其合并资产负债表中按净额列报余额。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 如果实行名义现金池，但未将余额实际划转至一个账户，则集团X无法证明“以净额结算的意图”，因为该安排并未实际涉及净额现金结算。因此，余额应按总额列报。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 如果实行伴随定期净额结算的名义现金池，主体仅在拥有法定权利且有意图对期末实际存在的余额进行净额结算时，才能按净额列报名义现金池余额。如果余额在期末日与结算日之间发生变动，主体便无法证明其有意图对先前余额进行净额结算。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 需要注意的是，上述安排可能较为复杂；每项安排均应结合其具体事实和情况予以审视。如果资产负债表日的金额不能反映全年的正常现金余额，则可能需要对总额余额作出进一步披露。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.28.2 – 为衍生工具提交的现金担保物（抵押品）是否应抵销？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IAS 32 第50段 正文索引：47.28

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 提交的现金担保物（抵押品）（例如为衍生工具提交的现金担保物）是否应与资产负债表头寸相抵销？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体可能与银行或清算所签订了衍生工具合同。为降低信用风险，双方可能同意定期向对方提交金额等于该衍生工具公允价值的现金担保物（抵押品）。提交担保物并不导致未结清余额的法定结算。然而，担保协议的条款规定，当付款到期时（以及在任何一方违约、破产或无力偿债时），该担保物将用于结算该衍生工具，且双方均有意以此方式结算。如果是这种情况，主体将拥有抵销该衍生工具和该担保物的法定可执行权利，并计划以净额结算。如果市场价格不变，将不会产生进一步的现金流量。资产负债表日之后担保物余额的任何变动均源于未来事项，与资产负债表日的评估无关。因此，IAS 32的抵销要求得到满足，该担保物应当予以抵销。反之，如果现金担保物不用于结算该衍生工具，则不满足IAS 32的抵销要求。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.30.1 – IFRS 7是否适用于非金融服务行业的主体？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第3段 正文索引：47.30

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 与IAS 32和IFRS 9一致，IFRS 7适用于所有主体，而不仅仅是金融服务行业的主体。这意味着它既适用于金融工具可能仅限于现金、银行贷款和透支、应收账款和应付账款的制造企业，也适用于拥有众多复杂金融工具的银行。它也适用于合并集团中子公司的财务报表，尽管在大多数大型集团中，风险是在合并层面进行管理的。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.30.2 – IFRS 7是否适用于子公司？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第3段 正文索引：47.30

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: IFRS 7对子公司的财务报表没有范围豁免。对子公司适用IFRS 7可能带来挑战，因为金融风险通常在合并或集团层面进行管理。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.30.3 – IFRS 7是否适用于商品合同？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第3段 正文索引：47.30

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于签订商品购买、出售或使用合同的主体而言，适用IFRS 7可能具有挑战性。以现金净额结算且不符合“自用”豁免的商品合同，或通过其他金融工具结算的商品合同，属于IFRS 7的范围；符合“自用”豁免的合同不属于IFRS 7的范围，因为它们不是金融工具。[IFRS 9 第2.4段]。这些条款在第40章第81段中有详细讨论。出于内部报告目的，管理层在评估主体的金融风险敞口（如流动性风险、信用风险和市场风险）时，可能会剔除“自用”合同，也可能对所有商品合同采用相同处理方式。因此，管理层有责任确定如何提供披露，以完整反映报告主体与其商品合同相关的风险敞口。IFRS 7并不禁止管理层提供额外说明或细节，以协助财务报表使用者解读披露内容或提供完整图景。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.30.5 – IFRS 7是否适用于预计负债、应计项目和预付款项？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第3段 正文索引：47.30

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 预计负债（按IAS 37的定义）不属于IFRS 7的范围，因为它们不是金融工具。代表收取现金权利或交付现金义务的应计项目属于IFRS 7的范围。例如，已收货但尚未开票的应计项目属于IFRS 7的范围。另一方面，通过未来交付商品或提供服务结算的预付费用不是金融工具，不属于IFRS 7的范围。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.30.6 – IFRS 7是否适用于已签发的财务担保合同？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第4段，IFRS 7 第3(d)段，IFRS 4 第4(d)段，IFRS 17 第7(e)段 正文索引：47.30

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于已签发的财务担保合同，如果损失准备金额高于未摊销保费金额，则按照IFRS 9的减值原则计量，但它们属于IFRS 9范围内的金融工具，因此也属于IFRS 7的范围。被视为保险合同并按照IFRS 4 / IFRS 17计量的财务担保合同不属于IFRS 7的范围。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.31.1 – 属于IFRS 7范围内的未确认金融工具有哪些示例？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第4段 正文索引：47.31

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 某些贷款承诺在计量方面不属于IFRS 9的范围，但在终止确认和减值方面属于IFRS 9的范围。[IFRS 9 第2.1(g)段]。贷款承诺属于IFRS 7的范围，因为它们使主体面临金融风险，例如信用风险和流动性风险。然而，对于在公允价值套期中被指定为被套期项目的确定承诺而言，情况未必如此。根据IFRS 9的套期会计规则，归因于被套期风险的确定承诺公允价值的后续累计变动确认为一项资产或负债。[IFRS 9 第6.5.9段]。然而，在成为金融资产或金融负债之前，该“确定承诺”资产或负债并不会使主体面临信用风险或流动性风险。适用套期会计这一事实并不意味着该“确定承诺”资产或负债是金融工具，也不意味着IFRS 7的披露要求适用。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.37.1 – 银行如何将以摊余成本计量的金融资产划分为不同类别？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第B2段 正文索引：47.37

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于银行而言，“以摊余成本计量的金融资产”这一分类通常包含多个类别，可能包括贷款和某些投资。除非贷款具有相似特征，否则可进一步细分。在此情况下，将贷款划分为以下类别可能是恰当的：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 客户类型（例如商业贷款和个人贷款）；或

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 贷款类型（例如抵押贷款、信用卡、无担保贷款和透支）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 然而，在某些情况下，如果所有贷款都具有相似特征（例如仅向个人提供单一类型贷款的储蓄银行），“发放客户贷款”可以作为一个类别。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.44.1 – 主体如何估计归因于负债信用风险变动的公允价值变动？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第10段 正文索引：47.44

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体需要计算负债公允价值变动中归因于该负债信用风险变动的金额。在实务中量化此类变动可能较为困难。IFRS 9第B5.7.18段提供了一种相对简便的方法来计算应在其他综合收益中列报的金额，如下例所示。当对该负债而言市场条件的唯一相关变动是可观察基准利率的变动时，可适用该方法。假定由该工具信用风险变动或利率变动以外的因素引起的公允价值变动并不重大。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 20X1年1月1日，主体发行了一项10年期债券，面值为C150,000，年固定票面利率为8%，与具有类似特征债券的市场利率一致。主体使用伦敦银行间同业拆借利率（LIBOR）作为其可观察（基准）利率。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体假定收益率曲线平坦，所有利率变动均源于收益率曲线的平行移动，且LIBOR的变动是市场条件的唯一相关变动。同时假定由该债券信用风险变动或利率变动以外的因素引起的公允价值变动并不重大。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 在债券发行日，10年期LIBOR互换利率为5%。第一年末，LIBOR下降至4.75%。该债券的公允价值为C153,811，与该债券7.6%的市场利率一致。该市场利率反映了第一年末该债券的信用评级（见下文）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体应如何估计归因于该负债信用风险变动的公允价值变动？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体按如下方式估计该债券公允价值变动中不归因于导致市场风险的市场条件变动的金额：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 计算该债券内含报酬率中工具特定组成部分： 在发行日，该10年期债券的内含报酬率为8%。由于发行日LIBOR为5%，内含报酬率的工具特定组成部分为3%（8% − 5%）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 使用该债券的合同现金流量，确定第一年末计算债券现值所用的折现率：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 由于市场条件的唯一相关变动是年末LIBOR下降至4.75%，因此现值计算所用的折现率为7.75%（4.75% + 3%）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: - 使用上述折现率和该债券的合同现金流量，计算第一年末的现值如下：

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: C 9年期（第2至第10年）应付利息C12,000的现值 = 12,000 × [1 – (1 + 0.0775) -9 ] 75,748 0.0775 第10年应付C150,000的现值 = 150,000 × (1 + 0.0775) -9 76,619 现值合计 152,367 使用市场利率和该债券的合同现金流量，计算第一年末的现值如下： （注意：此第二次计算使用与第一次计算相同的现金流量和相同的基准利率——主要差异在于信用利差已调整以反映当前市场价格。） C 9年期（第2至第10年）应付利息C12,000的现值 = 12,000 × [1 – (1 + 0.076) -9 ] 76,226 0.076 第10年应付C150,000的现值 = 150,000 × (1 + 0.076) -9 77,585 观察到的负债市场价值 153,811 计算不归因于基准利率变动的公允价值变动 C 观察到的债券市场价值 153,811 上述计算的债券现值 152,367 不归因于可观察基准利率

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 不归因于可观察基准利率变动的公允价值变动是归因于该负债信用风险变动的公允价值变动的合理替代值，因为按7.75%和7.6%计算的现值之间的差额假定反映了该工具信用风险的变动。因此，应在其他综合收益中列报的金额为C1,444。[IFRS 9 第B5.7.18段]。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.51.1 – IFRS 7中的“已转移资产”是否与满足IFRS 9过手测试的资产相同？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第42A段 正文索引：47.51

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: IFRS 7第42A段将“已转移资产”定义为：（a）主体转移了收取现金流量的合同权利，或（b）主体保留了收取现金流量的合同权利并承担了将该现金流量支付给另一方的合同义务的资产。然而，与IFRS 9的要求不同，在（b）情形下并不要求满足IFRS 9第3.2.5段的过手测试。因此，IFRS 7第42D段的披露（包括现行IFRS要求）延伸至因未通过IFRS 9第3.2.5段过手测试而未终止确认的已转移资产。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.51.2 – 披露要求如何适用于相似金融资产组合及金融资产的一部分？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第42A段 正文索引：47.51

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: IFRS 9的终止确认要求适用于一组相似金融资产，因此披露要求也适用于已转移的一组相似资产。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 同样，在某些情况下，IFRS 9的终止确认要求适用于一项金融资产（或一组金融资产）的一部分。与IFRS 7第42A段一致，如果适用IFRS 9第3.2.2段的条件，IFRS 7的披露要求仅适用于已转移的金融资产部分。例如，对于导致债务工具的一部分（即仅利息部分）被终止确认的债务工具利息剥离，根据IFRS 9第3.2.2段，终止确认的“资产”仅与利息现金流量相关，因此如果该部分已整体终止确认且不存在继续涉入，则不适用IFRS 7第42E至42G段的披露。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.51.3 – 投资基金和保险公司持有的典型资产是否属于“已转移资产”？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第42A段 正文索引：47.51

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 某些主体（例如投资基金和保险公司）可能持有产生现金流量的相似金融资产组合，这些现金流量用于向其他工具持有人支付义务（例如赎回投资基金份额或支付人寿基金下的人寿保单赔款）。在大多数情况下，主体（例如投资基金或保险公司）能够将资产所得款项（利息、股利或本金合同现金流量，或出售所得款项）进行再投资，而非负有将该现金流量支付给第三方（例如份额持有人或保单持有人）的义务。因此，此类资产不属于“已转移”资产，无需进行IFRS 7的披露。然而，在某些情形下可能需要进行IFRS 7披露（例如对冲基金行业中的某些侧袋安排），但这取决于相关工具的具体条款。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.55.1 – 在何种情况下符合IFRS 7对“继续涉入”的定义？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第42C段 正文索引：47.55

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 应逐案考虑资产与任何其他权利或义务之间关联的程度和实质，以确定是否符合IFRS 7对“继续涉入”的定义。例如，如果负债在合同上与资产挂钩，致使来自该资产的现金流量必须用于清偿该负债，或者资产和相关负债被风险隔离（例如在特殊目的主体SPV中），我们认为其属于IFRS 7披露的范围。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 不属于IFRS 7第42C段豁免范围的持续涉入，例如就已转移金融资产的转移价格作出的或有价格调整（例如因影响该资产的税法或法律变更所致），出于IFRS 7披露目的将被视为继续涉入。然而，未与已转移资产挂钩的利率互换或其他衍生工具不构成继续涉入。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.55.2 – 服务合同是否符合IFRS 7对“继续涉入”的定义？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第42C段 正文索引：47.55

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于已整体终止确认的已转移资产（例如无追索权保理），转出方可能继续为该资产提供服务并收取服务费，该费用可能基于资产价值的一定百分比。由此产生的问题是：该服务合同是否构成对已转移资产的继续涉入，从而属于IFRS 7披露要求的范围？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: IFRS 7第B30段中的“付款”一词不包括主体收取并须汇付给转入方的已转移金融资产的现金流量。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体必须评估服务合同，以确定其是否符合IFRS 7第42C段语境下的“继续涉入”定义。例如，如果服务费取决于已转移资产的业绩或已转移资产现金流量的时间，则出于第42C段的目的，这将构成继续涉入。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 同样，如果固定费用因已转移金融资产未履约而无法全额支付，则出于披露要求的目的，服务方具有继续涉入。在这些示例中，服务方在已转移金融资产的未来业绩中享有利益。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)

text: IFRS 7第13C段要求主体针对已确认金融资产和已确认金融负债分别披露以下定量信息：总额；按照IAS 32抵销的金额；受具有可执行性的总互抵协议约束但未实现抵销的金额；担保物（抵押品）；以及净额。这通常以表格形式列报。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 关于IFRS 7第13C(b)段要求的在确定“净额”时的“已抵销金额”，在同一安排下予以抵销的已确认金融资产和已确认金融负债的金额，均应在金融资产和金融负债的披露中分别列示。但是，披露的金额（例如在表格中）以予以抵销的金额为限。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 例如，主体可能拥有一项已确认的衍生资产和一项已确认的衍生负债，二者满足IAS 32第42段的抵销标准。如果衍生资产的总额大于衍生负债的总额，则金融资产披露表将包含衍生资产的全部金额（按照第13C(a)段）和衍生负债的全部金额（按照第13C(b)段）。然而，尽管金融负债披露表将包含衍生负债的全部金额（按照第13C(a)段），但其仅包含等于衍生负债金额的衍生资产金额（按照第13C(b)段）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 关于IFRS 7第13C(c)段要求的财务状况表中的“净额”披露，IFRS 7第B45段澄清如下：如果主体拥有属于这些披露范围（如第13A段所规定）但不满足IAS 32第42段抵销标准的工具，则第13C(c)段要求披露的金额将等于第13C(a)段要求披露的金额。此外，第13C(c)段要求披露的“净额”必须与财务状况表中列报的各单行项目金额进行调节。例如，如果主体确定对单个财务报表行项目金额进行汇总或分解能提供更相关的信息，则必须将第13C(c)段中披露的汇总或分解金额调节回财务状况表中列报的各单行项目金额。

text: IFRS 7第13C段要求主体针对已确认金融资产和已确认金融负债分别披露以下定量信息：总额；按照IAS 32抵销的金额；受具有可执行性的总互抵协议约束但未实现抵销的金额；担保物（抵押品）；以及净额。这通常以表格形式列报。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 关于“受具有可执行性的总互抵协议或类似协议约束的金额”的披露，IFRS 7第13C(d)(i)段指与不满足IAS 32第42段部分或全部抵销标准的已确认金融工具相关的金额（例如，不满足IAS 32第42(b)段标准的当前抵销权，或仅在违约事项发生时或仅在任何交易对手无力偿债或破产时才具有可执行性和可行使性的附条件抵销权）。第13C(d)(ii)段指与金融担保物（包括现金担保物，含收到和质押的担保物）相关的金额。主体披露作为担保物（抵押品）已质押或收到的该等金融工具的公允价值。按照第13C(d)(ii)段披露的金额应与实际收到或质押的担保物相关，而不应与因归还或收回该等担保物而确认的任何应付款项或应收款项相关。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 关于定量抵销披露，IFRS 7第B51段允许按金融工具类型或按交易类型分组——例如衍生工具、回购和逆回购协议，或证券借入和证券借出协议。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 或者，也允许在定量披露中按金融工具类型分组，并按交易对手进行披露。在此情况下，无需具名识别交易对手，但其代号（交易对手A、交易对手B等）应在各年度之间保持一致。单项重大的交易对手应单独披露，其余交易对手可汇总在一行中。同时应考虑就交易对手的类型提供额外的定性披露。

text: 20X6年11月30日，主体A（以欧元为记账本位币）收购了一家主要竞争对手。由于该次收购，与20X6年6月30日的余额相比，以美元计价的应收款项从1亿美元增至3亿美元，浮动利率债务从2亿欧元翻倍至4亿欧元。主体A的财政年度截止日为12月。截至20X6年12月31日的余额被认为能够代表未来年度的情况。主体A是否必须披露能够代表其年内风险敞口的额外信息？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 在此情景下，主体A应当披露额外信息，因为截至20X6年12月31日的定量数据不能代表20X6年财务期间的情况。仅声明该数据不具代表性是不够的。为满足IFRS 7的要求，主体可以披露报告期内所面临的最高、最低和平均风险金额。但是，如果年末敞口能够代表未来期间且对事实和情况提供了充分说明，则可能不需要完整的最高/最低/平均分析。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: IFRS 7将全额结算衍生合同中交换的金额作为按未折现合同基础纳入到期日分析的金额示例。该准则仅提及衍生金融负债的到期日分析，因此似乎仅要求披露衍生金融负债的现金流出总额（即支付端）。然而，同时披露现金流入（即收取端）可能更有帮助。如FAQ 47.109.1所述，当有关信息为使财务报表使用者能够评价流动性风险的性质和程度而有必要时，IFRS 7要求披露金融资产的到期日分析。类推而言，我们认为披露全额结算衍生金融负债的收取端通常对于理解流动性风险也是必要的。此外，可能还需要提供衍生金融资产的到期日分析。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于属于IFRS 9范围的全额结算商品合同，适用与上段类似的分析。当合同在报告日构成一项金融负债（即具有负公允价值）且将导致现金流出（而非商品实物交付流出）时，相关现金流出应纳入到期日分析。披露所有商品合同（包括资产负债表日具有正公允价值和负公允价值的合同）的合同现金流出可能有所帮助。或者，在单独表格中披露全额结算商品合同，列示所有合同的现金流入/流出以及相关的商品流出/流入，可能更具意义。如果提供此项额外披露，主体可以将现金流出交叉索引至到期日分析。无论采用上述哪种列报替代方法，均应说明编制和计量基础。

text: FAQ 47.108.15 – 到期日分析：永续债券和签出看跌期权应披露在哪个时间段？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第39段 正文索引：47.108

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 对于某些工具（例如永续债券和签出看跌期权），很难确定如何（以及是否）将相关金额纳入到期日分析。就永续债券而言，如果债务人/发行方拥有赎回该债券的看涨期权，则债务人/发行方对本金的偿还具有自主决定权。在行权之前，该债券的合同条款为不可赎回永续债券。一旦行使看涨期权，债券的合同条款即发生变更，该债券将具有到期日。如果未行使看涨期权，未折现现金流量将永续支付。这就引发了最后一个时间段应列示何种金额的问题。准则未明确处理此类情形，因此可以采用多种替代方法。一种方法是将本金纳入最后一个时间段。另一种选择是不在最后一个时间段纳入任何现金流量，而是在标题为“无到期日”的时间段中披露本金金额。无论选择何种披露形式，在此领域提供清晰的工具条款叙述性说明都非常重要。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 在到期日分析中纳入“虚值”签出看跌期权（金融负债）将取决于该期权是净额结算还是全额结算。如果该期权处于虚值状态且按净额结算，则无需在到期日表中披露负债，因为基于资产负债表日存在的条件并不存在付款义务。[IFRS 7 第B11D段]。然而，对于交易对手可迫使发行方付款的全额结算衍生工具，无论该工具处于实值还是虚值状态，支付端均应在流动性表的最早时间段内披露。美式期权应在最早时间段披露，而欧式期权则取决于行权日期。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 叙述性披露应说明签出期权是按其内在价值纳入的，且如果条件发生变化，未来实际应付金额可能会有所不同。IFRS 7第B10A(b)段支持这一做法，该段指出，如果到期日分析中包含的现金流出可能与合同到期日表中披露的金额显著不同，则需要进行说明。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.109.1 – 哪些主体通常使用金融资产来管理流动性风险？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第B11E段 正文索引：47.109

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 金融机构通常使用金融资产来管理其流动性风险。为了使财务报表使用者能够评价流动性风险的性质和程度，金融资产的到期日分析很可能是必要的。然而，该披露要求并不仅仅与金融机构相关；具有重大交易活动的某些其他类型主体（例如能源公司）也可能持有金融资产以管理流动性风险。当此类活动构成主体业务的重要组成部分时，可能需要提供金融资产的到期日分析。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 当主体列报金融资产的到期日分析时，应基于内部向关键管理人员提供的信息进行编制。该分析可以基于合同到期日或预期到期日，取决于风险管理的方式。或者，该分析也可以按净额基础（即公允价值）列报。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.110.1 – 为什么应对可能需要提交担保物（抵押品）的工具考虑进行披露？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第B11F段 正文索引：47.110

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 金融工具的担保物（抵押品）要求可能构成重大的流动性风险。例如，持有衍生负债的主体在负债超过特定限额时可能被要求为该衍生工具提交现金担保物。因此，如果追加担保物通知构成重大流动性风险，主体应就其担保物安排提供定量披露，因为这些现金流量可能早于合同到期日发生。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.111.1 – 敏感性披露应如何汇总？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第40段，IFRS 7 第B17段

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 在针对每种市场风险提供敏感性分析时，主体应决定如何汇总信息以展现全貌，同时不合并来自显著不同经济环境、具有不同特征的风险敞口信息。主体无需针对相关风险变量合理可能变动范围内的每一次变动披露影响。披露合理可能范围边界处的变动影响即可。[IFRS 7 第B18–B19段]。例如，交易金融工具的主体可以分别就为交易而持有的金融工具和非为交易而持有的金融工具披露该信息。同样，主体不会将来自恶性通货膨胀地区的市场风险敞口与来自极低通货膨胀地区的相同市场风险敞口汇总。相反，如果主体仅在单一经济环境中面临单一类型的市场风险敞口，则无需列示分解信息。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.111.2 – 如果合理可能变动的幅度不同，是否应重述上年度披露？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第39段 正文索引：47.111

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 当波动率发生变化时，主体不应重述上年度的披露。例如，如果汇率的合理可能变动从上年的5%变为本年的8%，则不应重述上年度披露。但是，主体可以为比较期间列报额外的敏感性信息。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.113.1 – 利率敏感性分析：对于已就浮动利率风险进行套期的债券，可能需要披露哪些内容？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第IG34、B24段 正文索引：47.113

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 主体就已发行债券的浮动利率风险敞口进行套期。该套期被指定为现金流量套期。债券和套期工具（利率互换）的剩余期限均为五年。互换的浮动端与债券的浮动利息完全匹配（不产生套期无效部分）。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 套期的高度有效性并不一定意味着利率风险的变动不会对权益或损益产生影响。现金流量套期的会计处理意味着与套期工具套期有效部分相关的公允价值变动计入其他综合收益。递延在其他综合收益中的金额在被套期交易发生时重分类至损益。因此，利率风险敞口的合理可能变动将同时对损益和权益产生影响。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 与此同时，未偿还债券利率风险敞口的合理可能变动将对损益产生相反的影响，因为该债券支付浮动利息。

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 如果重分类和套期无效部分的影响并不重大，主体可以考虑将以下披露作为敏感性分析的近似说明：“与债券和互换浮动端相关的变动未予反映，因为它们相互抵销。与互换固定端剩余公允价值敞口相关的变动列示于分析的权益部分。”

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: FAQ 47.114.1 – 对于存在市场风险敞口且影响权益的工具，是否应披露敏感性？

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 准则索引：IFRS 7 第B23段 正文索引：47.114

chapter: 47 - Presentation and disclosure of financial instruments (IFRS 9, IFRS 7)
text: 正如折算敞口可能对权益产生影响但未纳入外汇风险敏感性分析一样，其他一些可能面临市场价格风险的项目也未必纳入。例如，考虑使主体面临自身股价变动的工具。这些工具包括主体发行的以外币计价行权价格的认股权证、未满足IAS 32“固定换固定”要求的可转换债务，以及分类为负债的股份支付报酬奖励。在前两种情形下，主体应披露其股价合理可能变动对损益和权益影响的信息。这是因为前两项工具属于IFRS 9的范围，从而属于IFRS 7的范围。第三项工具尽管分类为负债，但因按照IFRS 2进行会计处理而不属于IFRS 9的范围；因此也不属于IFRS 7的范围。

Introduction and scope (paras 48.1-48.8)

48.1 Earnings per share (EPS) is a ratio that is widely used by financial analysts, investors and other users to gauge an entity’s profitability and to value its shares. Its purpose is to indicate how effective an entity has been in using the resources provided by the ordinary shareholders, and to assess the entity’s current net earnings. EPS also forms the basis for calculating the ‘price-earnings ratio’, which is widely used by investors and an

48.2 Throughout this chapter, reference is made to ‘equity holders of the parent’. In paragraph 54(r) of IAS 1, ‘equity holders of the parent’ was amended to ‘owners of the parent’. IAS 33 has not been updated to reflect this change, so we have used ‘equity holders of the parent’ in line with IAS 33.

48.3 EPS is a ratio of the numerator (that is, earnings measured in terms of profits available to ordinary equity holders of the parent entity) to the denominator (that is, the weighted average number of ordinary shares). In addition to basic EPS, diluted EPS is disclosed with the objective to illustrate the effect of all dilutive potential ordinary shares. Dilution is a reduction in EPS resulting from the assumption that convertible instruments
[IAS 33 para 10]. [IAS 33 para 30].
48.4 IAS 33 prescribes the principles for the determination and presentation of EPS.
48.5 IAS 33 applies to the following entities:

- Those whose ordinary shares or potential ordinary shares (such as convertible debt or warrants) are traded in a public market (that is, a domestic or foreign stock exchange or an over-the-counter market, including local and regional markets).

- Those that file, or are in the process of filing, financial statements with a securities commission or other regulatory body for the purpose of issuing ordinary shares in a public market (that is, not private placements).
48.6 EPS is required only on the basis of consolidated information even if the parent’s separate and consolidated financial statements are presented together.

48.7 An entity may choose to present EPS based on its separate (rather than consolidated) entity financial statements, as well as that based on the consolidated financial statements. The separate entity EPS figures should not be shown in the consolidated financial statements. They should be shown only on the face of the separate entity statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income (or income statement, if presented as a separate stat

48.8 Entities whose securities are not publicly traded are not required to disclose EPS. However, where such entities choose to disclose EPS, they need to calculate and disclose EPS in accordance with IAS 33.

Basic earnings per share (paras 48.9 - 49.46)

48.9 Basic EPS should be calculated by dividing the profit or loss for the period attributable to the parent entity’s ordinary equity holders by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period.
48.10 An ordinary share is defined as an equity instrument that is subordinate to all other classes of equity instruments.
48.11 An equity instrument is any contract that evidences a residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting all of its liabilities.

48.12 Ordinary shares participate in profit only after other types of shares, such as preference shares, have participated. An entity may have more than one class of ordinary shares. Ordinary shares of the same class have the same rights to receive dividends.

48.13 Entities that fall within the scope should calculate basic and diluted EPS for the profit or loss attributable to the parent entity’s ordinary equity holders. Basic and diluted EPS should also be calculated for profit or loss from continuing operations separately if these are presented under IFRS 5. Entities calculating EPS for discontinued operations, as determined in accordance with IFRS 5, apply the same measurement principles under IAS
48.14 Basic and diluted EPS disclosures are required for each class of ordinary shares that have different rights to share in profit for the period.

48.15 Profit or loss from continuing operations, and profit or loss for the period attributable to the parent entity’s ordinary equity holders, are calculated as the relevant profit or loss after tax and non-controlling interest, adjusted for the after-tax effects of preference dividends, differences arising on settlement of preference shares and other similar effects of preference shares classified as equity.

48.16 An entity that has preference shares in issue, will classify those shares as financial liabilities or equity under IAS 32. An adjustment is required to the profit or loss for the period, to arrive at the profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders for the purpose of calculating EPS, if preference shares are classified as equity. Any dividends and other appropriations would be debited directly to equity under IAS 32. Any dividends
FAQ 48.16.1 – How is profit for the period adjusted to reflect preference shares?
48.17 The amount of dividends declared in respect of the year should be deducted in arriving at the profit attributable to ordinary shareholders for preference dividends that are non-cumulative.

48.18 The dividend for the period should be taken into account, whether or not it has been declared for cumulative preference dividends. If an entity is unable to pay or declare a cumulative preference dividend, the undeclared amount of the cumulative preference dividend (net of tax, if applicable) should still be deducted in arriving at earnings for the purpose of the EPS calculation.
48.19 The amount paid is not deducted in arriving at earnings for the purpose of the EPS calculation in the period in which arrears of cumulative preference dividends are paid.
FAQ 48.19.1 – How should other appropriations and adjustments in respect of preference shares treated as liabilities be accounted for?

48.20 Any original discount or premium is treated as amortised to retained earnings if preference shares are classified as equity, using the effective interest method. This is treated as a preference dividend for the purpose of calculating EPS. An entity might have issued non-convertible, non-redeemable preference shares at a discount to compensate for non-payment of dividends in earlier years. The discount is amortised to retained earnings. Such

48.21 An entity might repurchase preference shares classified as equity. Any excess of the fair value of consideration given over the carrying amount of the shares represents a return to the holders of the preference shares and a charge to retained earnings, and it is included in determining the profit or loss available to ordinary equity holders of the parent entity for the purpose of calculating EPS.

48.22 Preference shares classified as equity may be converted early on favourable terms due to changes to the original conversion terms or the payment of additional consideration. The excess of the fair value of ordinary shares or other consideration paid over the fair value of ordinary shares or other consideration payable under the original terms is included in determining the profit or loss available to ordinary equity holders for the purpose

48.23 Any excess of the carrying amount of preference shares classified as equity over the fair value of the consideration paid to settle them is included when determining the profit or loss available to ordinary equity holders for the purpose of calculating EPS.
Participating securities and two-class ordinary shares

48.24 ‘Participating equity instruments’ participate in dividends with ordinary shares according to a predetermined formula (for example, two for one) with, sometimes, an upper limit on participation.
FAQ 48.24.1 – Are puttable financial instruments, which are presented as equity, considered as ordinary shares for EPS purposes?

48.25 Participating preference shares are classified as either financial liabilities or equity instruments. Both the fixed and the participating element of participating preference shares classified as liabilities would have been charged in arriving at profit or loss attributable to the parent entity. No further adjustments are necessary.

48.26 Conversion of participating preference shares is assumed if the effect is dilutive if they are convertible into equity shares. The conversion shares should be included in outstanding ordinary shares for the purpose of calculating diluted EPS.

48.27 An entity might have a class of ordinary shares with a different dividend rate from that of another class of ordinary shares, but without prior or senior rights. Such instruments are termed ‘two-class ordinary shares’. An entity with such shares would disclose a number of EPS figures, each attributable to different classes of ordinary shares.

48.28 The steps that should be followed in allocating earnings for the purpose of calculating basic EPS, where an entity has different instruments that are not convertible into ordinary shares, are as follows:

- Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders is adjusted by the amount of dividends declared in the period for each class of shares and by the contractual amount of dividends that must be paid for the period (for example, unpaid cumulative dividends).

- The remaining profit or loss is allocated to ordinary shares and participating equity instruments to the extent that each instrument shares in earnings or losses. The allocation is made as if all of the profit or loss has been distributed. The total profit or loss allocated to each class of equity instrument is determined by adding together the amount allocated for dividends and the amount allocated for a participation feature.

- The total amount of profit or loss allocated to each class of equity instrument is divided by the number of outstanding instruments to which the profits or losses are allocated (that is, the instruments in that class), to determine the EPS for that class of instrument.

FAQ 48.28.1 – How are earnings allocated for the purpose of calculating basic EPS where an entity has different classes of ordinary shares and participating equity instruments that are not convertible into ordinary shares?
Computation of the number of ordinary shares
48.29 The denominator of the basic EPS calculation is calculated using the weighted average number of those ordinary shares that are outstanding during the period.

FAQ 48.29.1 – How is the weighted average number of shares calculated? FAQ 48.29.2 – Not used FAQ 48.29.3 – How are ordinary shares issued at full market price reflected in the weighted average number of ordinary shares?

48.30 The denominator is the number of ordinary shares outstanding at the year end if there have been no changes in capital structure during the year. However, if additional ordinary shares have been issued during the year, an apportionment of the earnings for the whole of the year over the larger equity base would not give a fair presentation. Similar considerations apply where shares have been bought back during the year. The entity uses an ave

48.31 Shares should be included in the weighted average calculation from the date consideration is receivable, generally the date of issue. The date of inclusion should be determined from the terms and conditions attaching to the issue, taking into account the substance of any contract associated with the issue. A number of examples are given in IAS 33, illustrating the timing of inclusion of ordinary shares in the weighted average calculation:
- Ordinary shares issued in exchange for cash are included when cash is receivable.
- Ordinary shares issued on the voluntary reinvestment of dividends on ordinary or preference shares are included when dividends are reinvested.
- Ordinary shares issued as a result of the conversion of a debt instrument to ordinary shares are included as of the date when interest ceases accruing.
- Ordinary shares issued in place of interest or principal on other financial instruments are included as of the date when interest ceases accruing.
- Ordinary shares issued in exchange for the settlement of a liability of the entity are included as of the settlement date.
- Ordinary shares issued as consideration for the acquisition of an asset other than cash are included as of the date on which the acquisition is recognised.
- Ordinary shares issued for the rendering of services to the entity are included as the services are rendered.

48.31.1 Ordinary shares issued as part of the cost of a business combination are included from the acquisition date (that is, when the earnings of the acquired business are included in the financial statements of the acquirer).

48.32 Shares issued in partly paid form are treated differently to fully paid shares, for which no adjustment is made. Partly paid shares are treated as fractions of shares (payments received to date, as a proportion of the total subscription price) and are included in the calculation of the weighted average number of shares only to the extent that they participate in dividends for the period. Partly paid shares that do not participate in dividen
FAQ 48.32.1 – How are partly paid shares reflected in the weighted average number of ordinary shares?
Purchase and holding of ‘own shares’ and ESOPs
48.33 An entity might hold its own shares in treasury. This situation might arise in a number of ways:
- where a parent has acquired them in the market, by forfeiture, by surrender in lieu of forfeiture, or by way of a gift; such shares are accounted for as a deduction from shareholders’ funds;
- where a subsidiary continues to hold the shares in the parent that were acquired before it became a group member; or
- where an entity holds its own shares where it operates an employee share ownership plan (ESOP) for the benefit of its employees.

These shares are excluded from the weighted average number of ordinary shares for the purpose of calculating EPS as they are not outstanding. Shares held by an ESOP are also excluded from the calculation of basic EPS to the extent that they have not vested unconditionally to the employees.
FAQ 48.33.1 – Does a premium paid on the purchase of an entity’s own shares affect EPS?
Contingently issuable shares
48.34 Contingently issuable shares are ordinary shares that are issuable for little or no cash or other consideration if and when specified conditions in a contingent share agreement have been met.

48.35 Contingently issuable shares are considered to be outstanding and are included in the calculation of basic EPS from the date when all the necessary conditions have been satisfied (that is, the events have occurred). Shares that are issuable solely after the passage of time are not contingently issuable shares, because the passage of time is a certainty and should therefore be included in the calculation from contract inception. Mandatorily convertible instruments

48.36 Entities often issue instruments that are convertible into ordinary shares that may be either mandatorily convertible or convertible at the option of the issuer or holder. The issue of ordinary shares is solely dependent on the passage of time for a mandatorily convertible instrument. Ordinary shares that are issuable on the conversion of a mandatorily convertible instrument should be included in basic EPS from the date the contract is ente

FAQ 48.36.1 – Are convertible instruments included in basic EPS where there is a conversion option? FAQ 48.36.2 – How do mandatorily convertible instruments affect EPS? FAQ 48.36.3 – How do convertible instruments with mandatory conversion based on the share price affect EPS?
Bonus issue (stock dividends), share split and share consolidation

48.37 The weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the period and for all periods presented should be adjusted for events, other than the conversion of potential ordinary shares, that have changed the number of ordinary shares outstanding without a corresponding change in resources.
48.38 Examples of such situations include:
- A capitalisation or bonus issue (or stock dividend).
- A bonus element in any other issue, for example a bonus element in a rights issue to existing shareholders.
- A reverse share split or share consolidation.

FAQ 48.38.1 – How does a share split affect EPS? FAQ 48.38.2 – How does a bonus issue affect EPS? FAQ 48.38.3 – Is the issue of shares below market price an event for which the number of shares prior to the issue is adjusted?

48.39 The number of shares outstanding increases without an increase in resources (cash flow or earnings) if an entity issues new shares by way of a bonus issue or stock dividend during the period. The shares issued should be treated as outstanding, as if the issue had occurred at the beginning of the earliest period reported. Earnings for the year should be apportioned over the number of shares after the capitalisation. The EPS figure disclosed

48.40 Entities might raise additional capital by issuing shares to existing shareholders, on a pro rata basis to their existing holdings, in the form of a rights issue. The rights shares can either be offered at the current market price or at a price that is below the current market price. Ordinary shares might be issued during the year by way of a rights issue at a discount to the market price. The weighting calculation should reflect the fact t

FAQ 48.40.2 – Should the averaging calculation in a rights issue made during the year be performed from the announcement date, the last date of acceptance of the subscription price, or the share issue date following despatch of the share certificates?

48.41 The factor in paragraph 48.40 should be used to adjust the number of shares in issue before the rights issue, in order to correct for the bonus (stock dividend) element in the rights issue. This correction should be made for both the current period prior to the rights issue and all previous periods presented.

48.42 The fair value per share immediately before the exercise of rights is the actual closing price at which the shares are quoted on the last date inclusive of the right to subscribe for the new shares. This is often referred to as the ‘cum-rights price’, being the price on the last day of quotation cum-rights. The ‘ex-rights price’, on the other hand, is the theoretical price at which, in a perfect market and without any external influences, t
Dividends payable in shares or in cash

48.43 An entity may pay its dividends in the form of shares, or give the shareholder the option to receive a dividend in either cash or shares (sometimes referred to as scrip dividends or enhanced scrip dividends). The shares issued increase the weighted average number of shares used in the EPS calculation.

48.44 Scrip dividends might be regarded as potential ordinary shares that entitle the recipient to ordinary shares. These potential ordinary shares are converted into ordinary shares when the scrip shares are issued, which is often after the balance sheet date. As IAS 33 requires shares to be included in basic EPS on a weighted average basis from the date they are outstanding, ordinary shares issued through voluntary reinvestment of dividends sha
FAQ 48.44.1 – Why is a special dividend followed by a share consolidation accounted for like a share repurchase?
Special dividend followed by share consolidation

48.45 Entities might return surplus cash to shareholders. This is normally effected by means of a share repurchase or by a synthetic share repurchase that is achieved by the payment of a special dividend to shareholders followed by a consolidation of share capital (for example, changing five C20 shares into four C25 shares). A share consolidation combined with a special dividend can have the overall effect of a share repurchase at fair value as t
FAQ 48.45.1 – Why is a special dividend followed by a share consolidation accounted for like a share repurchase?

48.46 No adjustment to prior year’s EPS should be made for a special dividend accompanied by a share consolidation, if the economic substance of the transaction is a share repurchase at fair value. If the share repurchase takes place partway through a period, the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding is adjusted for the reduction from the date the special dividend is paid (that is, when resources leave the entity).

Diluted earnings per share (paras 48.47-48.101)

48.47 Basic EPS is calculated on the number of ordinary shares outstanding in respect of the period. Sometimes, entities might have ‘potential ordinary shares’ in issue, defined as financial instruments or other contracts that might entitle their holder to ordinary shares. Such instruments must be assessed to determine if they are dilutive.

48.48 Examples of potential ordinary shares are:
- Financial liabilities or equity instruments, including preference shares, that are convertible into ordinary shares.
- Options (including employee share options) and warrants.
- Shares that would be issued on satisfaction of certain conditions that result from contractual arrangements, such as the purchase of a business or other assets.
48.49 Contracts that might result in the issue of ordinary shares of the entity to the holder of the contract, at the option of the issuer or the holder, are potential ordinary shares.

48.50 Calculation of diluted EPS, in addition to basic EPS, is required for profit or loss attributable to the parent entity’s ordinary equity holders and separately for each of continuing and discontinued operations where these are presented in accordance with IFRS 5.

48.51 The profit or loss for the period attributable to ordinary equity holders is adjusted for the effects of all dilutive potential ordinary shares for the purpose of calculating diluted EPS. The weighted average number of shares outstanding is also adjusted for the effects of all dilutive potential ordinary shares.
48.52 The profit or loss attributable to the parent entity’s ordinary equity holders for the purpose of calculating diluted EPS should be adjusted for the after-tax effect of:

- Dividends or other items related to dilutive potential ordinary shares that have been deducted in arriving at profit attributable to ordinary equity holders for the purpose of calculating basic EPS, such as dividends on dilutive convertible preference shares.
- Interest recognised in the period on dilutive potential ordinary shares, such as interest on dilutive convertible debt.
- Any other changes in income or expense that would result from the conversion of the dilutive potential ordinary shares.

- Transaction costs and discounts (or subtract premiums) on potential ordinary shares that are allocated to periods in accordance with the effective interest method in Appendix A to IFRS 9.
- Issue costs (or similar) amortised in the period.
- Interest/dividend costs.

Computation of number of ordinary shares

48.55 The denominator of diluted EPS should be calculated as the sum of the weighted average number of ordinary shares used in the basic EPS calculation and the weighted average number of ordinary shares that would be issued on the conversion of all the dilutive potential ordinary shares into ordinary shares.

48.56 All potential ordinary shares are assumed converted into ordinary shares at the beginning of the period or, if not in existence at the beginning of the period, at the date of issue of the potential ordinary shares. The date of issue is the date the financial instrument was issued or the granting of the rights by which they are generated. This is sometimes referred to as the ‘if converted’ method.

48.57 The conversion into ordinary shares should be determined from the terms of the financial instrument or the rights granted. This determination should assume the most advantageous conversion rate or exercise price from the standpoint of the holder of the potential ordinary shares.

48.58 Potential ordinary shares are included in the diluted EPS calculation on a weighted basis only for the period they were outstanding. Potential ordinary shares that are issued during the year are included on a time-weighted basis from the date of issue to the balance sheet date. 48.59 The new ordinary shares that are issued on conversion are included from the date of conversion, in both basic and diluted EPS, on a weighted basis. Consideration of convertible instruments in the calculation of basic EPS is discussed in para 48.9 onwards.

48.60 Only potential ordinary shares that are dilutive are considered in the calculation of diluted EPS. Potential ordinary shares should be treated as dilutive only when their conversion to ordinary shares would decrease profit per share or increase loss per share from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders.
48.61 The effects of anti-dilutive potential ordinary shares are ignored in calculating diluted EPS.
48.62 An entity might have a number of different types of potential ordinary shares in issue. Each one would need to be considered separately rather than in aggregate.

48.63 If the potential ordinary shares are dilutive, based on profit or loss from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders, they should be treated as dilutive for all other EPS calculations. This includes, for example, total EPS, discontinued operations EPS and any additional EPS given, whether or not they are actually dilutive at the relevant level of profit.

48.65 Convertible preference shares are dilutive where the amount of dividend on such shares, declared or accrued in the period per ordinary share obtainable on conversion, is below basic EPS for continuing operations. If the amount exceeds basic EPS, the convertible preference shares are anti-dilutive.

48.67 Warrants or options are defined as financial instruments that give the holder the right to purchase ordinary shares.

48.68 Warrants issued to subscribe for shares at fixed prices on specified dates in the future, or share options granted to directors and employees are taken into account in the calculation of diluted EPS, if they are dilutive.

48.69 Warrants and options are dilutive where they would result in the issue of ordinary shares for less than the average market price of ordinary shares during the period. The calculation of the average market price for these instruments is explained in more detail in paragraph 48.73.

48.70 The method by which dilutive warrants and share options are taken into account in the calculation of diluted EPS is called the ‘treasury stock method’. In the calculation of diluted EPS, the expected proceeds from the exercise of the dilutive share warrants and options are deemed to be used by the entity in purchasing as many of its ordinary shares as possible in the open market, using an average market price for the period. 48.71 The treasury stock method reflects more dilution, because the value of options and warrants increases relative to the value of the underlying share. As the average market price for the underlying share increases, the assumed proceeds from exercise will buy fewer shares, thus increasing the number of shares issued for nil consideration and therefore increasing the denominator of the diluted EPS calculation.

48.72 Although increases in the share price over a number of periods might increase the dilutive effect, previously reported EPS figures are not retrospectively adjusted to reflect changes in share prices.

48.73 The fair value of share options and warrants under the treasury stock method should always be calculated on the basis of the average price of an ordinary share for the period rather than the period-end market price. The use of the average stock price is consistent with the objective of diluted EPS to measure EPS for the period based on period information.

48.101 Contracts that require the entity to repurchase its own shares (such as written put options and forward purchase contracts) are reflected in diluted EPS if their effect is dilutive. If the contracts are ‘in the money’ during the period (that is, if the exercise or settlement price is above the average market price for the period), their dilutive effects should be calculated using the ‘reverse treasury stock’ method. Under that method:

- It should be assumed that the proceeds from this issue are used to satisfy the contract to buy back ordinary shares.

- The incremental ordinary shares – that is, the difference between the number of shares assumed to be issued and the number of shares received (bought back) on satisfying the contract – will be included in the calculation of diluted EPS.

Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 20 Reference to standing text: 48.33

Any premium payable on the purchase of an entity’s own ordinary shares will be charged against reserves and will not affect earnings for the year if the shares are acquired for their market price. No adjustments should be made to the prior year’s EPS.

If the holder or issuer has an option which drives conversion, such shares are treated as potential ordinary shares, because they might never be issued if the conversion option is not exercised. For the purpose of EPS, the potential ordinary shares that would be issued on conversion are included in the weighted average number of ordinary shares used in the calculation of basic EPS (and, therefore, also diluted EPS) from the date of issue of the instrument, since their issue is solely dependent on the passage of time. Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 42 Reference to standing text: 48.76

Dilution should never be tested by reference to whether the conversion of a potential ordinary share reduces the standard basic EPS calculated on the total profit or loss for the period. The reason for choosing ‘profit from continuing operations’ as a control number is that this level of profit, unaffected by discontinued operations, is likely to remain stable over time and to reflect the earnings that will exist in the future when the dilution o
FAQ 48.76.2 – If, at the level of overall loss, applying the dilution decreases loss per share, is it still correct to show the effect of diluted EPS?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 42 Reference to standing text: 48.76

An entity has a profit from continuing activities, but a loss for the year overall because of losses on discontinued operations. Options are dilutive when considered at the level of profit from continuing operations, because the diluted EPS at that level decreases profit per share. However, at the level of overall loss for the year, applying the dilution caused by the options decreases loss per share.
Is it still correct to show the effect of the options in the diluted EPS?

Yes. If the options are dilutive at the level of profit from continuing operations, they should be included in the diluted EPS calculation at the level of the loss for the year. If that reduces loss per share, the entity should explain the circumstances. A form of explanation might be: “Options are dilutive at the level of profit from continuing operations and so, in accordance with IAS 33, have been treated as dilutive for the purpose of diluted

In addition to disclosing basic and diluted EPS for the overall loss for the year, the entity would be required to disclose basic and diluted EPS at the level of continuing operations (on the face of the income statement) and the basic and diluted EPS for discontinued operations (either on the face of the income statement or in the notes).
FAQ 48.77.1 – How would an entity carry out a test to determine if a series of convertible instruments, warrants and options is dilutive?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 44 Reference to standing text: 48.77
This consideration is complicated and involves the following steps:
- Step 1 – the entity calculates the profit or loss from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders.

- Step 2 – the entity calculates the earnings per incremental share for each type of potential ordinary share. The earnings per incremental share is the increase in profit or loss (or, less commonly, the decrease) that would result from the exercise or conversion of the security, divided by the weighted average increase in the number of ordinary shares that would result from the conversion.

- Step 3 – the entity ranks all potential ordinary shares, from the most dilutive (lowest earnings per incremental share) to the least dilutive (highest earnings per incremental share). Options and warrants are generally included first, because they do not affect the numerator of the calculation, and so are most dilutive.
- Step 4 – the entity calculates a basic EPS, using profit or loss from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders as the numerator.

- Step 5 – the most dilutive potential ordinary share with the lowest earnings per incremental share is included, and a new EPS (as indicated above) is calculated. If this new figure is lower than the previous one, the entity recalculates EPS including the potential shares with the next lowest earnings per incremental share.
- Step 6 – this process of including increasingly less dilutive shares continues until the resulting EPS figure increases, or there are no more potential ordinary shares to consider.

- Step 7 – any potential ordinary share that has the effect of increasing the cumulative EPS from continuing operations is considered to be anti-dilutive, and it is excluded from the diluted EPS calculation.
- Step 8 – all other potential ordinary shares with higher rankings are considered to be dilutive potential ordinary shares, and they are included in the diluted EPS calculation in the normal way.
FAQ 48.77.2 – Does an entity test to determine whether an instrument is dilutive when there is a loss from continuing operations?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 44 Reference to standing text: 48.77
In most instances, where there is a loss from continuing operations, there would be no difference between the basic and diluted EPS, because potential ordinary shares would be anti-dilutive.

FAQ 48.80.1 – How do a subsidiary and consolidated group calculate EPS if the subsidiary has issued potential ordinary shares?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para A11 Reference to standing text: 48.80

A parent entity has profit attributable to ordinary shareholders of C100,000 (excluding any earnings of the subsidiary). There are 10,000 ordinary shares outstanding. The parent owns 800 ordinary shares in the subsidiary, representing 80% of the subsidiary’s ordinary share capital; it also owns 200 convertible preference shares in the subsidiary, representing 50% of the subsidiary’s preference share capital (which is treated as an equity instrume

The subsidiary has profit attributable to ordinary shareholders of C6,000. Its ordinary share capital consists of 1,000 ordinary shares, and it has 400 convertible (one-for-one) preference shares in issue. It has also issued 150 warrants exercisable to subscribe for ordinary shares of the subsidiary, with an exercise price of C5 per warrant. The average market price of one ordinary share of the subsidiary was C10. Dividends on the preference shar
What are the earnings per share for the subsidiary and for the consolidated group?
Subsidiary’s earnings per share

This is calculated as the subsidiary’s profit, from which is deducted the preference dividend that had been charged to retained earnings. The result is divided by the number of the subsidiary’s ordinary shares.

This is the subsidiary’s profit (preference dividends are not deducted, because they would be saved on conversion of the preference shares), divided by the number of ordinary shares, plus the ordinary shares that would be issued on conversion of the preference shares (on the basis of one for one) and the number of ordinary shares that would be issued for nil consideration on exercise of the warrants, calculated as follows:
Proceeds of warrants: 150 × C5 = C750
Number of ordinary shares that could be issued at fair value: C750 ÷ C10 = 75
Number of ordinary shares that would be issued at nil consideration: 150 − 75 = 75
Consolidated earnings per share

The earnings are calculated as the profit attributable to ordinary shareholders, before taking account of the subsidiary’s results that are included in the consolidated financial statements, of C100,000, plus the share of the subsidiary’s profits, calculated as:
The earnings figure comprises:
- The profit of the parent entity attributable to ordinary shares (excluding dividends from subsidiary) of C100,000.
- The share of the subsidiary’s profit, calculated as 800 shares × 4.07 = C3,256 (C4.07 being the diluted EPS of the subsidiary).
- The parent’s proportionate interest in the subsidiary’s earnings attributable to the warrants, calculated as (75 shares × 4.07) × 20 ÷ 150 = C40.7.
- The parent’s proportionate interest in the subsidiary’s earnings attributable to the convertible preference shares, calculated as 200 shares × 4.07 = C814.

This means that the effect, on the group diluted EPS, of options in a subsidiary that are convertible into shares of the subsidiary, should be included in consolidated EPS, based on the group’s holdings of the subsidiary’s shares.

FAQ 48.91.1 – How should diluted EPS reflect other types of contingently issuable share arrangements?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 53 Reference to standing text: 48.91

The guiding principle is that, where the number of contingently issuable shares depends upon the level of earnings, the diluted EPS computation should include those shares to the extent that they would be issuable under the agreement, based on the current amount of earnings.
Earnings conditions in earn-out agreements come in various forms:

- Maintenance of the current earnings level, or the attainment of a specified increased level of earnings of an acquired entity for a specified number of years, might be the condition.

- Conditions might specify the issue of shares when a minimum earnings target is reached, increasing rateably until the maximum earnings target is reached, with a cap on the maximum number of shares that could be issued.

FAQ 48.119.1 – What should be considered when publishing a five-year track record for EPS purposes?
Reference to standard: IAS 33 para 26 Reference to standing text: 48.119

Entities often publish a historical summary, usually covering at least five years. IAS 33 does not deal specifically with adjustments to historical summaries, but the following guidance is relevant in such situations. In order to present a fair comparison of EPS figures published in such a summary, the basic EPS figure will need to be adjusted for subsequent changes in capital, as set out below:
- Where a capitalisation issue or share split has taken place during a financial year, all previously published EPS figures should be adjusted by the bonus factor (see further para 48.40).

- Where a rights issue at less than full market has taken place during a financial year, all previously published EPS figures should be adjusted by the reciprocal of the bonus element inherent in the rights issue (see further para 48.41).

Where there is more than one capitalisation or rights issue during the year, both of these factors will operate cumulatively. The cumulative effect of all of these events should be taken into account. The resultant figures should be described as restated EPS, and they should be set out separately from the other financial data that is not so adjusted.

Where there has been a bonus or rights issue in the period covered by the summary, the ordinary dividend actually paid in those periods should be set out in the form of pence per share, and it should be similarly adjusted by the same factors used in restating EPS.
